Possible side effects of the extract were assessed using aphid population development and parasitoid mummy counts and weights. Under the tested conditions, the application of A. nodosum extract did not affect any of the variables used as indicators of V. faba growth and development, i.e. no measurable impact on the plant under normal conditions or in the presence of a biotic stressor. The extract did not influence the population development of the herbivore A. fabae . Furthermore, its application did not impair the aphid-suppression efficacy of A. matricariae , nor did it alter individual mummy weight or, as preliminary observations indicate, mummy abundance. This result suggests that the algae extract and the parasitoid biological control agent evaluated can be used in combination without antagonistic interactions.

title: Kalkınmacı Devlet Yaklaşımı Çerçevesinde Singapur’un Ekonomik Büyümesinin Temelleri
source: Ekonomi İşletme ve Maliye Araştırmaları Dergisi
summary: Bu makalede, kısa sürede büyük bir kalkınma mucizesi gösteren Singapur’un başarısının arkasındaki unsurlar dikkate alınarak bir analiz gerçekleştirilmektedir. Uzun süre İngiliz kolonisi olan Singapur, bağımsızlık sonrasında ülkenin ekonomik
content: Bu makalede, kısa sürede büyük bir kalkınma mucizesi gösteren Singapur’un başarısının arkasındaki unsurlar dikkate alınarak bir analiz gerçekleştirilmektedir. Uzun süre İngiliz kolonisi olan Singapur, bağımsızlık sonrasında ülkenin ekonomik gerçekliklerine ve gelecek projeksiyonlarına uygun kalkınma stratejileri geliştirmiştir. Bağımsızlığını kazandığı 1965’ten günümüze sürekli ve istikrarlı denebilecek bir ekonomik büyüme süreci gösteren Singapur, küresel krizlerden etkilenmesine rağmen kendi ekonomik sistemine uygun çözümler üretmiştir. Bu makalede Singapur’un kalkınmacı devlet yaklaşımı sayesinde, ulaştığı büyüme rakamları, ülkenin ekonomik verilerine bakılarak analiz edilmektedir. Kalkınmacı devlet anlayışı çalışmanın temelini oluşturmaktadır. Çalışmada bazı Güneydoğu ve Uzakdoğu Asya ülkelerinin ulaştığı büyüme rakamlarının ardındaki kalkınmacı devlet anlayışı ve bu politikanın en iyi örneklerinden biri olan Singapur’un izlediği yol ele alınmaktadır. Bu makale çalışmasının sonuçları bağlamında Singapur’un ekonomik büyümesinde doğrudan yabancı yatırımların, teknolojik yatırımların, Ar-Ge çalışmalarının yanı sıra eğitim, kanunların sıkı bir şekilde uygulanması ve yolsuzluğunun önlenmesi ülkenin kalkınmasında oldukça etkili olduğu görülmektedir.

title: Community perspectives on the Zambian Farm Block Development Program and an evaluation of household income factors: Lessons from Kawambwa district
summary: Since 2002, the Farm Block Development Program was one of the flagship initiatives within Zambia's agricultural policy. This program was designed to promote commercialization of rural agricultural lands, to contribute to national food secur
content: Since 2002, the Farm Block Development Program was one of the flagship initiatives within Zambia's agricultural policy. This program was designed to promote commercialization of rural agricultural lands, to contribute to national food security, economic growth, and improved rural livelihoods. However, host community concerns remained untold. This paper aimed at shedding light on those concerns, and the factors associated with household incomes. A qualitative evaluation of submissions from Luena Farm Block residents in Kawambwa district in Zambia, showed that reticent project reception; fears of displacement, job scarcity, environmental damage, and cultural erosion were major issues for the local community. Further, a quantitative evaluation of data from 5286 respondents, using Tobit models established that 95% of household incomes were below Zambia's official minimum wage, and the rural average income. Censored Least Absolute Deviation regression revealed that the household income factors were education, household size, cultivated area, and land tenure security. Environment-level income factors were health facility presence, and water access. The conclusion urged a cautious approach to achieve sustainable farm block development. Policy recommendations were that community needs and interests should be mainstreamed in the Farm Block Development Program. Education and health facilities should be promoted to enhance literacy and productivity. Mechanization should be promoted to expand crop areas and production efficiency. Land tenure security should be facilitated to protect fixed investments. Safe water access should be promoted to support irrigation and public health.

title: Pengaruh Firm Size, Corporate Social Responsibility, dan Green Accounting terhadap Tax Avoidance
source: Indonesian Journal of Multidisciplinary on Social and Technology
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Firm Size, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), dan Green Accounting terhadap Tax Avoidance pada perusahaan yang tergabung dalam Indeks SRI-KEHATI dan terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Firm Size, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), dan Green Accounting terhadap Tax Avoidance pada perusahaan yang tergabung dalam Indeks SRI-KEHATI dan terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia selama periode 2020–2025. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan tahunan dan laporan keberlanjutan perusahaan. Pemilihan sampel dilakukan menggunakan metode purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditentukan, sehingga diperoleh 12 perusahaan dengan periode pengamatan selama enam tahun atau sebanyak 72 observasi. Variabel Firm Size diukur berdasarkan ukuran perusahaan, Corporate Social Responsibility diukur menggunakan biaya CSR, sedangkan Green Accounting diukur berdasarkan biaya lingkungan perusahaan. Tax Avoidance dalam penelitian ini digunakan sebagai variabel dependen. Teknik analisis data yang digunakan meliputi statistik deskriptif dan regresi data panel dengan bantuan perangkat lunak EViews 12. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Firm Size, Corporate Social Responsibility, dan Green Accounting secara simultan berpengaruh terhadap Tax Avoidance. Secara parsial, Firm Size berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap Tax Avoidance. Sementara itu, Corporate Social Responsibility tidak berpengaruh terhadap Tax Avoidance dan Green Accounting juga tidak berpengaruh terhadap Tax Avoidance. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa ukuran perusahaan menjadi faktor yang berperan dalam menentukan tingkat Tax Avoidance, sedangkan pelaksanaan CSR dan Green Accounting belum menunjukkan pengaruh secara individual terhadap Tax Avoidance pada perusahaan Indeks SRI-KEHATI.

title: Vision-language encoding models reveal an image-computable food-quality dimension in human occipitotemporal cortex
summary: Perceived calorie content contributes to neural representational structure in human ventral visual cortex, yet it remains unclear whether this reflects an abstract nutritional signal or whether perceived calorie is largely recoverable from
content: Perceived calorie content contributes to neural representational structure in human ventral visual cortex, yet it remains unclear whether this reflects an abstract nutritional signal or whether perceived calorie is largely recoverable from the visual-semantic structure of the food image itself. In 25 female participants who passively viewed 96 food images during functional MRI, we decomposed perceived calorie ratings into a component predicted from CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining) image embeddings, a vision-language model that captures high-level visual-semantic image structure, and a residual component not captured by this CLIP-based prediction. We then tested their respective contributions to neural prediction using cross-validated banded ridge encoding models. The CLIP-predictable component organized foods along a processedness and naturalness dimension, separating raw single-ingredient foods from prepared and energy-dense foods. Adding this component to a visual-semantic baseline improved neural prediction progressively along the ventral visual hierarchy, with the strongest relative contribution in higher-level ventral temporal cortex. These findings indicate that calorie-related encoding in ventral visual cortex is carried mainly by a shared food-quality axis indexing processedness, naturalness, and perceived healthiness, a substantial part of which is recoverable from image-computable visual-semantic structure, rather than providing evidence for an isolated abstract representation of caloric magnitude. Because these results derive from a reanalysis of 25 female participants viewing a fixed set of 96 images, generalization to broader populations and larger, more varied stimulus sets remains to be established.

title: Synthesis of Naphthoquinones by Pd‐Catalyzed Heck–Matsuda Arylation of Lapachol
summary: Direct Heck–Matsuda arylation of lapachol provides rapid access to structurally diverse naphthoquinones under homogeneous and heterogeneous palladium catalysis. The methodology features broad substrate scope, gram‐scale applicability, and u
content: Direct Heck–Matsuda arylation of lapachol provides rapid access to structurally diverse naphthoquinones under homogeneous and heterogeneous palladium catalysis. The methodology features broad substrate scope, gram‐scale applicability, and unambiguous structural assignment by single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction, providing an efficient platform for the diversification of quinones.

title: The Preheating Stage on The Starobinsky Inflation after ACT
summary: Abstract Recent ACT results favor larger e-fold numbers, which tighten the reheating requirements in Starobinsky inflation. We show that efficient reheating generically requires an additional spectator-assisted preheating stage. The preheat
content: Abstract Recent ACT results favor larger e-fold numbers, which tighten the reheating requirements in Starobinsky inflation. We show that efficient reheating generically requires an additional spectator-assisted preheating stage. The preheating dynamics and reheating temperature must be significantly modified to accommodate the higher reheating temperature. We present viable parameter sets compatible with PBH formation and the preferred reheating mechanism in this model. Furthermore, the momentum spectrum evolves from infrared-dominated modes at the early stage of preheating to higher-momentum modes at later times, supporting our scenario.

title: СТРАТЕГІЧНЕ УПРАВЛІННЯ ІНВЕСТИЦІЙНИМИ ПРОЄКТАМИ ЕНЕРГЕТИЧНИХ КОМПАНІЙ НА ЗАСАДАХ ДІДЖИТАЛІЗАЦІЇ
source: Scientific papers OF DMYTRO MOTORNYI TAVRIA STATE AGROTECHNOLOGICAL UNIVERSITY (ECONOMIC SCIENCES)
summary: Сучасний розвиток енергетичного сектору України відбувається під впливом воєнних руйнувань, необхідності відновлення критичної інфраструктури, інтеграції з європейським енергетичним ринком, глобальної декарбонізації, розвитку розподіленої г
content: Сучасний розвиток енергетичного сектору України відбувається під впливом воєнних руйнувань, необхідності відновлення критичної інфраструктури, інтеграції з європейським енергетичним ринком, глобальної декарбонізації, розвитку розподіленої генерації, цифровізації управлінських процесів і зростання вимог до інвестиційної прозорості. Досліджено стратегічне управління інвестиційними проєктами енергетичних компаній України на засадах діджиталізації. Проведено статистичний аналіз розвитку енергетичного сектору України, охарактеризовано діяльність ключових енергетичних компаній, визначено їх сильні та слабкі сторони, можливості й загрози. Здійснено PESTEL-аналіз енергетичного сектору України та надано стратегічну оцінку його розвитку у розрізі регіонів. Запропоновано економіко-математичну модель перспективного аналізу розвитку енергетичного сектору, яка поєднує оцінювання інвестиційної ефективності, цифрової зрілості, енергетичної стійкості, регіональної вразливості, екологічного ефекту та ризиків.

title: Governance pathways to energy‑efficient building retrofitting through peer-to-peer learning and capacity building
summary: Extended abstract 3-070-26 Achieving the EU’s 2050 climate-neutrality goal hinges on advancing energy-efficient building retrofits to decarbonise the sector. Although the European Green Deal provides a strong framework – through legislation
content: Extended abstract 3-070-26 Achieving the EU’s 2050 climate-neutrality goal hinges on advancing energy-efficient building retrofits to decarbonise the sector. Although the European Green Deal provides a strong framework – through legislation such as the Energy Efficiency Directive, Energy Performance of Buildings Directive and the Renovation Wave initiative – Europe’s current annual renovation rate for public and private buildings lingers at just 1%, far below what is needed. Local and regional authorities (LRAs) play a pivotal role in turning these policies into concrete action. Still, they face persistent challenges, such as limited technical and financial resources, knowledge and skills shortages, poor data quality and availability, and other issues, all of which are now quite well documented in the literature. This contribution explores how peer-to-peer capacity building enables LRAs to overcome these challenges. Drawing on evidence from the PROSPECT across its three editions, which, over the last eight years, has supported over 400 cities and regions with innovative financing schemes for energy efficiency retrofits, the study focuses on the participants’ experiences. Combining a survey and online exchanges with mentors and mentees from PROSPECT’s programme, the study demonstrates that the project’s peer learning – especially mentoring and study visits - boosts LRAs’ capacity to design, finance, and implement energy-efficiency renovation projects. It enhances technical and financial knowledge, strengthens stakeholder relations and trust-building, and fosters networking. PROSPECT’s mentees gain skills in communication, project planning and management, and stakeholder engagement, leading to improved projects, new initiatives, and secured or pursued funding. Yet, while peer-to-peer learning advances LRAs’ climate and energy efforts, it falls short of addressing deep-rooted issues, such as those involving bureaucracy, institutions, and politics. Thus, even though peer-to-peer learning supports bottom-up implementation, it alone cannot achieve climate neutrality. Therefore, aligning policies, financial instruments, and capacity-building programmes like peer-to-peer learning is key to scaling up energy-efficient building renovations, thereby supporting the EU’s long-term energy efficiency and climate goals. This research was funded by LIFE24-CET-PROSPECT CUBE (101212861). Download presentation.

title: Institutional theory and vocational education: a discussion
source: Journal of Vocational Education and Training
summary: Institutional theories have come to dominate comparisons of vocational education systems. Their emphasis on the agency of social actors outside the educational sphere has proved attractive to researchers seeking to understand the complex so
content: Institutional theories have come to dominate comparisons of vocational education systems. Their emphasis on the agency of social actors outside the educational sphere has proved attractive to researchers seeking to understand the complex social relations in which vocational education is embedded. These questions are discussed here with special regard to historical institutionalism, by two authors with diverging views of the significance and value of these theoretical approaches. For Maurer, institutional theory, and especially historical institutionalism, offers a valuable opportunity to theorise VET research. For Esmond, its emphasis on shared interests and perpetuation of path-dependent models understate how VET has been contested among irreconcilable actors in the past and the possibility of changes that advance social justice in the future. The authors agree that the descriptive nature of these theories, which lack a normative educational dimension or critical perspective, enables important comparisons but necessarily limits their capacity to guide future change.

title: US Regulatory Burden, Compliance Spending, and Market Structure
summary: This article examines the effect of regulatory cost on market structure. Regulation been associated in a number of studies with market consolidation. However, fewer studies have explicitly examined regulatory burden through the mechanism of
content: This article examines the effect of regulatory cost on market structure. Regulation been associated in a number of studies with market consolidation. However, fewer studies have explicitly examined regulatory burden through the mechanism of higher compliance labor costs. This article extends concepts recently developed in related literature, utilizing U.S. Census Bureau data in a novel way to measure regulatory burden through compliance labor costs in most major sectors of the US economy. Next, it explores these labor costs as a mechanism linking regulatory burden with anticompetitive market dynamics in each sector, such as market consolidation and large firms’ share of revenue. The results demonstrate that conventional measures of regulatory burden (at both the federal and state levels) are associated with higher relative levels of compliance labor spending. It also examines the association between compliance labor and market structure across hundreds of individual industry categories, finding that higher compliance spending is associated with industry consolidation. In doing so, this article helps to establish compliance share of labor as a useful alternative to direct measures of regulatory burden. It also highlights the importance of regulatory burden in contributing to market structure dynamics, an important consideration for policymakers.

title: Piperazine and Morpholine Protoporphyrin IX Derivatives Intensify Biomolecules Oxidation and Phototoxicity in Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer
summary: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a clinically established approach that relies on the localized generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) mediated by a photosensitizer (PS), light, and molecular oxygen. Protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) is an approve
content: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a clinically established approach that relies on the localized generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) mediated by a photosensitizer (PS), light, and molecular oxygen. Protoporphyrin IX (PpIX) is an approved PS; however, its intracellular retention is limited, factor that can alter its overall photodynamic efficiency. In this study, we report how the design of PpIX derivatives bearing piperazine (PpIX-Pip) or morpholine (PpIX-Morp) substituents may modulate lipophilicity, cellular uptake, oxidative stress, and phototoxicity. The photodynamic activity of these derivatives was evaluated in the aggressive triple-negative human breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231. Both derivatives showed greater time-dependent cellular retention and enhanced photodynamic activity compared to PpIX, promoting oxidative stress, and triggering loss of mitochondrial membrane potential and caspase-3 activation. These results highlight the impact of rational structural modification of PpIX on photodynamic efficiency and provide valuable structure-activity relationship insights for the development of improved porphyrin-based PS for PDT.

title: Exploring the spillover of return between gold, Sharia stock, sukuk and exchange rate using TVP-VAR approach: ASEAN-5 case study
summary: The study examines spillover of return across asset classes in the ASEAN-5. Our study sample consists of gold, S&P Shariah, DJ Sukuk, and the currencies of ASEAN-5. The TVP-VAR approach is employed to analyse the interconnections among the
content: The study examines spillover of return across asset classes in the ASEAN-5. Our study sample consists of gold, S&P Shariah, DJ Sukuk, and the currencies of ASEAN-5. The TVP-VAR approach is employed to analyse the interconnections among the assets. The results show that Shariah stocks and gold are key players in the network’s net transmitter, and sukuk is the net receiver in the system. The highest return connectedness is between currency and Shariah stock, whereas the lowest is between gold and Shariah stock. The study suggests that investors can identify the connectedness channels of assets to better manage risk.

title: Bodyweight exercises can acutely impair self-paced interval running performance in male and female runners
summary: Abstract Concurrent training is frequently utilized by endurance runners due to its physiological and neuromuscular benefits. However, despite its practical relevance, the acute effects of a bodyweight (BW) circuit session on self-paced int
content: Abstract Concurrent training is frequently utilized by endurance runners due to its physiological and neuromuscular benefits. However, despite its practical relevance, the acute effects of a bodyweight (BW) circuit session on self-paced interval training (IT SP ), in which runners freely regulate their running speed during each interval, and whether these effects differ by sex, remain unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the acute effects of BW circuit on IT SP performance, perceptual, and physiological responses, comparing male and female runners. Sixteen runners (8 men, 8 women) completed two IT SP sessions (8 × 200 m with 90 s recovery) under randomized, counterbalanced conditions: (i) a control condition and (ii) a condition preceded by a BW circuit consisting of four exercises performed for three sets of 15 s of work and of 45 s rest. Readiness for exercise was evaluated immediately pre IT SP by a 10-point scale. The BW circuit impaired performance (339.9 ± 51.2 vs. 325.1 ± 52.1 s, p < 0.01), irrespective of sex ( p > 0.05). The BW circuit also reduced readiness for IT SP (5.8 ± 2.2 vs. 7.5 ± 2.0 a.u., p < 0.05), with no significant changes in heart rate or rating of perceived exertion ( p > 0.05). These findings indicate that a BW circuit induces sufficient acute fatigue to impair subsequent interval running performance, regardless of sex. Coaches should consider exercise sequencing when integrating bodyweight circuits and high-intensity interval sessions within the same training day.

title: Photochemical fate of synthetic progestins in sunlit surface waters: experimental kinetics, modeling, and ecotoxicological implications
summary: Abstract This study combines experimental and theoretical methods to explore the photochemical stability of progestins in a climate-sensitive model system for urban reservoirs worldwide, with a focus on the Guarapiranga Reservoir in São Pau
content: Abstract This study combines experimental and theoretical methods to explore the photochemical stability of progestins in a climate-sensitive model system for urban reservoirs worldwide, with a focus on the Guarapiranga Reservoir in São Paulo, Brazil. The target contaminants were levonorgestrel (LNG) and gestodene (GES), synthetic progestins used in contraceptive methods. Photoinduced reaction kinetics showed that LNG’s indirect photolysis is affected by triplet excited states of chromophoric dissolved organic matter (3CDOM*), hydroxyl radicals (HO·), and singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ), in the order 3CDOM* > HO· > 1 O 2 . Conversely, for GES, the sequence was HO· ≈ 3CDOM* > 1 O 2 . Water quality data from 2022 to 2024, along with kinetic modeling, estimated half-lives of 6.9 ± 1.2 days for LNG and 25.8 ± 9.0 days for GES. Density Functional Theory (DFT) analysis identified key reactive sites and degradation pathways, aligning well with experimental results. An ecotoxicological assessment of the photo intermediates using the ECOSAR model showed notable toxicity to daphnia, fish, and green algae, especially after the addition of HO· radicals. These findings offer valuable insights into the environmental fate of LNG and GES in urban surface waters and contribute scientific evidence to decision-making on monitoring and removing emerging contaminants through advanced wastewater treatment technologies.

title: Implementation Model of Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag Nanay Act for the selected LGUs of Camarines Sur
source: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
summary: This study aimed to have an Implementation Model of Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag Nanay Act for the selected LGUs in Camarines Sur. The goal was to improve healthcare delivery and nutritional status among infants and young children from zer
content: This study aimed to have an Implementation Model of Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag Nanay Act for the selected LGUs in Camarines Sur. The goal was to improve healthcare delivery and nutritional status among infants and young children from zero to two years old, adolescent females, pregnant, and lactating women. Specifically, the study determined the following objectives 1. To describe the administrative capability of the selected LGUs in Camarines Sur that implement RA 11148 or First 1000 Days Law in terms of a. health workforce capacity, b. budget allocation, c. facilities, d. local legislation & policy support, e. monitoring and evaluation; 2. To determine the performance of the selected LGUs in implementing the RA 11148 or First 1000 Days Law in the following areas, a. good nutrition, b. adequate nutrition, c. opportunities for early education, d. responsive caregiving, and e. safety and security; 3. To identify the factors that influence the implementation of RA 11148 of the selected LGUs in Camarines Sur; 4. To propose an Enhanced Implementation Model of RA 11148 for the selected LGUs in Camarines Sur. The study utilized the descriptive research design, a purposeful sampling method involving the application of a questionnaire as the main data gathering instrument among the identified 24 municipal nutrition action officers and 1 city nutrition action officer of the selected LGUs in Camarines Sur, supplemented by focus group discussion. The statistical tools used were the percentage technique and weighted mean. Findings, for the health workforce, there is no full-time MNAO in the LGUs, there is budget allocation and coordination among different departments and agencies within the LGU to support the programs and activities, the LGU actively engages with community leaders and organizations to promote awareness and participation in F1KD programs and activities and the LGU collaborates with external partners to supplement resources for acquiring facilities and equipment for RA 11148 implementation. The performance, for good health, adequate nutrition, responsive caregiving, all indicators under this category as Agree. Security and Safety indicates that open defecation cases or reports still persist in the LGU (or ZOD coverage is incomplete), serving as an environmental health and sanitation bottleneck for implementing Republic Act 11148. The factors that influence the implementation, political barrier, lack of support from the LGU and lack of materials/equipment is not a hindrance in implementing the RA 11148. While a strong commitment to the job and good communication between the nutrition staff and clients is observed. The following conclusions were drawn there is a need for LGUs to provide manpower such as a full-time Municipal/City Nutrition Action Officer, improvement of the administrative capability should be given focus. LGUs should enhance their performance in terms of safety and security, such as sanitation. LGUs should consider upscaling o

title: Pharmaceutical profile and prescribing practices in compounding pharmacies in Brazil: a cross-sectional study
summary: Introduction The industrialization expanded drug access but standardized formulations often fail to meet individual clinical specificities. Compounding pharmacies fill this gap by providing personalized therapies. In Brazil, although Federa
content: Introduction The industrialization expanded drug access but standardized formulations often fail to meet individual clinical specificities. Compounding pharmacies fill this gap by providing personalized therapies. In Brazil, although Federal Pharmacy Council Resolutions grant pharmacists the autonomy to prescribe over-the-counter drugs and compounded formulations, this clinical practice faces legal instability and structural challenges. This study aimed to outline the profile of pharmacists and analyze the clinical practice of pharmaceutical prescribing in compounding pharmacies across Brazil. Methods This is a quantitative, descriptive, and cross-sectional study conducted through an online survey covering all 27 federal units in Brazil. The questionnaire was distributed between May and December of 2024 via institutional channels and professional social networks. The sample consisted of 186 licensed pharmacists working in the compounding sector. Data collection addressed personal and professional information, prescription practices, and the management of self-limiting health problems. Results The sample was predominantly female (78.5%), with a high concentration in the Southeast region (35%). While 73.1% of participants perform pharmaceutical prescribing, only 43.4% document these prescriptions according to regulatory requirements. Furthermore, 44.3% of participants reported never having taken training courses related to prescribing. The most frequently managed health demands included mild insomnia (86.6%), weight loss (84.4%), and anxiety (83.9%). Herbal medicines were the most prescribed class (87.7%), with Passiflora incarnata (64.8%) being the most common active ingredient. Major barriers to prescribing included a lack of time (67.6%), absence of financial incentives (36.3%), and inadequate infrastructure (32.4%). Most professionals (61.8%) provide prescribing services free of charge. Discussion Pharmacists in Brazilian compounding pharmacies actively perform clinical prescribing, primarily managing self-limiting conditions with herbal and nutritional therapies. However, a significant gap persists between practice and formalization, characterized by low documentation rates, lack of infrastructure privacy, and training deficiencies. Addressing these regulatory, educational, and structural limitations is critical to ensuring patient safety, establishing clinical governance, and consolidating the role of the compounding pharmacist in the healthcare system.

title: Balancing Acts or Self‐Serving: The nexus Between Corporate Social Responsibility Decoupling and Tax Avoidance
summary: ABSTRACT Recent studies highlighted the phenomenon of corporate social responsibility (CSR) decoupling, where firms' CSR disclosures diverge from their actual CSR performance. This study investigates the relationship between CSR decoupling
content: ABSTRACT Recent studies highlighted the phenomenon of corporate social responsibility (CSR) decoupling, where firms' CSR disclosures diverge from their actual CSR performance. This study investigates the relationship between CSR decoupling and tax avoidance, offering a dual‐theoretical lens that integrates legitimacy theory and agency theory. From a legitimacy perspective, we argue that firms experiencing reputational deficits due to CSR decoupling may engage in tax avoidance to signal financial success and restore stakeholder confidence. From an agency standpoint, CSR decoupling exacerbates information asymmetry and weakens governance, enabling opportunistic managers to pursue aggressive tax strategies that enhance short‐term financial metrics. By embedding these theoretical perspectives, our study contributes to the literature by conceptualizing CSR decoupling not merely as a disclosure‐performance gap, but as a strategic condition that influences financial behaviour. Empirical analysis supports our propositions, revealing a positive association between CSR decoupling and tax avoidance. Mechanism testing further validates our framework, identifying poor firm performance, elevated agency costs, and heightened information opacity as key channels linking CSR decoupling to tax avoidance. We also explore contextual contingencies—such as institutional environments, tax enforcement intensity, industry characteristics, and leadership traits—that moderate this relationship. Our findings offer important implications for investors, regulators, and policymakers concerned with corporate transparency, governance, and ethical conduct.

title: Participatory citizen science for Relational One Health and Indigenous food sovereignty
summary: Introduction Food insecurity in First Nations communities in Northern Ontario is shaped by geographic isolation, high transportation costs, colonial disruption of land-based food systems, and environmental change. This paper examines Partic
content: Introduction Food insecurity in First Nations communities in Northern Ontario is shaped by geographic isolation, high transportation costs, colonial disruption of land-based food systems, and environmental change. This paper examines Participatory Citizen Science (PCS) as a community-led, culturally grounded response, drawing on two growing seasons of data from the Braiding Food Systems (BFS) Project, led by the University of Guelph in partnership with the First Nations communities of Red Rock Indian Band (RRIB), Biinjitiwaabik Zaaging Anishinaabek (BZA), and Netmizaaggamig Nishnaabeg (NN) in Northern Ontario. Guided by a Relational One Health (ROH) framework and Two-Eyed Seeing, the project engaged community members as ‘Garden Stewards’ — citizen scientists leading community garden and seed stewardship initiatives. Methods Using a mixed qualitative-descriptive methodology including focus group discussions, semi-structured interviews, participatory workshops, and systematic garden monitoring, the study documents how PCS functioned simultaneously as an epistemic, governance, and food sovereignty practice. Results Findings demonstrate that PCS enabled a progressive realization of Bridging, Braiding, and Weaving — from foundational relationship-building and co-design, through the intertwining of Indigenous and Western knowledge in practice, toward community-led governance of seed lodges and food system decision-making. Garden Stewards evolved from procedural participants to reflexive knowledge producers, disrupting conventional hierarchies between researcher and community. Discussion The study advances understanding of food sovereignty as a relational and epistemic practice enacted through everyday acts of seed selection, intergenerational learning, and land stewardship. Findings have implications for Indigenous data sovereignty, community-led food systems research, and policy addressing food insecurity in remote northern communities.

title: Quantity or quality: how common institutional investors with green experience shape corporate green innovation
summary: Corporate green innovation is constrained not only by financial constraints but also by deficiencies in green governance capabilities. Exploiting the initial entry of common institutional investors with green experience as a quasi-natural e
content: Corporate green innovation is constrained not only by financial constraints but also by deficiencies in green governance capabilities. Exploiting the initial entry of common institutional investors with green experience as a quasi-natural experiment, this study employs a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) model to examine its effect on corporate green innovation using data from Chinese A-share listed firms during 2010–2023. The results show that common institutional investors with green experience significantly enhance both the quantity and the quality of corporate green innovation. These findings remain robust after a series of endogeneity and robustness checks. Mechanism analysis reveals that such investors promote green innovation through two main channels: mitigating managerial myopia and reducing green agency costs. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal that the positive effect is more pronounced in regions with weaker environmental regulation and in firms whose executives exhibit stronger green awareness. Additional analyses indicate that common institutional investors with green experience also significantly enhance firms’ ESG performance, while command-and-control environmental regulation further strengthens these effects. This study contributes novel theoretical insights and empirical evidence on how green finance facilitates corporate green transformation through specialised investor governance channels, offering important policy implications for emerging economies seeking to promote green innovation.

title: Managing resource rents for low-carbon sustainability: the moderating roles of green finance, education and governance in Asian economies
summary: Purpose This study empirically investigates the natural resource rents (NRR)-CO2 emissions nexus in Asian countries, coupled with the moderating effects of green finance (GF), education (EDU) and governance quality (GQ). Design/methodology/
content: Purpose This study empirically investigates the natural resource rents (NRR)-CO2 emissions nexus in Asian countries, coupled with the moderating effects of green finance (GF), education (EDU) and governance quality (GQ). Design/methodology/approach The study uses a panel dataset (2001–2022) of 22 Asian countries for empirical analysis and employs a dynamic panel estimation framework with robustness analyses to evaluate the NRR-CO2 emissions relationship and the moderating roles of GF, EDU and GQ. The findings are interpreted through the resource curse hypothesis (RCH), green finance theory (GFT), human capital theory (HCT) and institutional theory (IT). Findings The empirical results indicate that greater NRR leads to more CO2 emissions, which provides empirical support for the RCH from an Asian viewpoint. GF and GQ significantly weaken the positive association between NRR and CO2 emissions, suggesting that stronger financial and institutional frameworks can mitigate the environmental pressures associated with NRR. In contrast, EDU exhibits a positive direct and moderating association with CO2 emissions. It reveals an unexpected education paradox in which improvements in educational development are not automatically translated into environmental sustainability, potentially reflecting the energy-intensive expansion of educational infrastructure and broader economic activities. Originality/value This is one of the pioneering studies that assesses the moderating effects of GF, EDU and GQ on NRR-CO2 emissions, particularly in economies where environmental and resource rent issues are pressing. Furthermore, the study is the first to provide broader theoretical insights through innovatively integrating the RCH with theories on GFT, HCT and IT.

title: Do streaming ao destino: como as séries influenciam a intenção de visita
summary: Este estudo explora o impacto do conteúdo audiovisual na intenção de visita, focando-se na série portuguesa da Netflix Rabo de Peixe e na sua influência no turismo da vila açoriana com o mesmo nome. Fundamentada num modelo teórico, a invest
content: Este estudo explora o impacto do conteúdo audiovisual na intenção de visita, focando-se na série portuguesa da Netflix Rabo de Peixe e na sua influência no turismo da vila açoriana com o mesmo nome. Fundamentada num modelo teórico, a investigação analisa como o consumo de séries pode desencadear o escapismo e a imersão, levando a respostas afetivas e à formação da imagem de um destino, influenciando, em última análise, a intenção de visita. Utilizando uma metodologia quantitativa e transversal, os dados foram recolhidos junto de 483 respondentes portugueses através de um questionário online com itens validados em escala de Likert. Os resultados confirmam relações estatisticamente significativas entre as variáveis, revelando que o envolvimento emocional e cognitivo com o conteúdo audiovisual pode gerar um interesse real pelos locais retratados. O estudo destaca o potencial do turismo induzido pelo cinema (film-induced tourism) como uma ferramenta estratégica para o marketing territorial, particularmente para destinos menos conhecidos. Reconhece ainda limitações, tais como o seu âmbito geográfico, e sugere investigações futuras em contextos internacionais e em diferentes tipos de conteúdo digital, incluindo redes sociais e conteúdos gerados por inteligência artificial. O estudo contribui para uma compreensão mais profunda da influência dos média no comportamento do turista.

title: Heat action policy ‘Hacks’ & WEHAC’s (Women Heat Action Cooperatives) providing passive cooling in energy-poor communities in India
summary: Extended abstract 3-240-26 Urban Poor Women in India, living in heat-trapping buildings in conditions of cooling-energy poverty (i.e. inadequate energy access for operating active cooling appliances and no access to passive cooling solution
content: Extended abstract 3-240-26 Urban Poor Women in India, living in heat-trapping buildings in conditions of cooling-energy poverty (i.e. inadequate energy access for operating active cooling appliances and no access to passive cooling solutions) are inequitably impacted by climate-crisis induced extreme heat which causes health issues stemming from homes being too hot to sleep in before midnight and social reproduction roles which require them to wake up hours before other family members. Paradoxically, women are under-represented in the ‘green economy’ response to extreme heat (eg. cool roof programmes). The paper presents insights from, and the way forward from the field-test phase of a Women's Heat Action Cooperative (WEHAC) programme underway in an informal settlement in Chennai, India to enhance access to passive cooling solutions co-created with the community. The WEHAC offers cooling products and services to residents who pay an affordable estimated monthly-installments (EMI) to the WEHAC to maintain a revolving fund that serves as future investment capital. The paper presents learnings related to structure of financial/social incentives for initial mobilization of women’s entrepreneurial interests, outcomes of testing solutions to underwrite risk of residents not paying EMIs, and elucidates the process of establishing an ecosystem of trades, material supply chains to foster a locally-owned decentralized response to cooling energy poverty. It also presents results of an ongoing effort to establish a One-Stop-Shop ( technical and finance assistance facility) for WEHACs where finance and in-kind assistance is derived from a multitude of sources (e.g. microfinance institutions, impact investment) and through repurposing municipal development schemes. The paper presents results from the applied policy research work of policy ‘hacking’ (i.e reinterpreting, repurposing) of existing policies (eg. heat action plans, women’s empowerment programs) and unlocking financing from under-subscribed schemes. Download presentation.

title: Networks of Memory: Infrastructures, Dependencies, and Commemorative Practices in Bavaria
summary: Memory culture is built by both tangible and intangible elements, whose interaction is governed by formal norms and laws introduced by state agencies, as well as by unwritten conventions. While standardized processes sustain and support mem
content: Memory culture is built by both tangible and intangible elements, whose interaction is governed by formal norms and laws introduced by state agencies, as well as by unwritten conventions. While standardized processes sustain and support memory culture, underlying networks of dependency and interconnection, particularly those involving local politics and technology, play an equally crucial role. This paper aims to propose an infrastructural approach to “difficult heritage” by examining the interrelations among the components of German memory culture. While existing studies provide an overview of already erected monuments and their reception by the public (such as visitor experience studies), it reconstructs and reflects on processes from the recent past in order to identify key actors who shape the notions and directions of commemorative practices. The examples selected from Bavaria are the documentation center in Munich and commemorative initiatives in Landsberg am Lech and Kaufering. The paper identifies social infrastructures and examines how they influence the management of the material heritage of the period of National Socialism. The conclusions of the study lead to a hypothesis that memory culture in Germany should be examined as an amalgamation of various locally shaped cultures and networks. This approach would lead to an emphasis on local memory, rather than pursuing uniform practices and globalized patterns, as some researchers claim.

title: Research on the Substitution Effect of Green Credit and Commercial Credit Financing
source: Asia Pacific Economic and Management Review
summary: Against the background of green finance development and enterprise financing diversification, green credit has gradually become an important policy tool and financing channel. Taking Chinese industrial enterprises as the research object, th
content: Against the background of green finance development and enterprise financing diversification, green credit has gradually become an important policy tool and financing channel. Taking Chinese industrial enterprises as the research object, this paper empirically examines the substitution effect between green credit and commercial credit financing. The results show that green credit can effectively ease the financing constraints of enterprises, and there is a significant substitution relationship between green credit and commercial credit financing. The improvement of green credit supply reduces enterprises' dependence on commercial credit. Further analysis indicates that the substitution effect is more prominent in non-state-owned enterprises, enterprises with strong environmental performance and enterprises in regions with high financial development. This study enriches the research on the relationship between green finance and informal financing, and provides empirical evidence for optimizing the financing structure of enterprises and promoting the development of green credit[1].

title: Worker Power for the AI Economy: Portable Benefits and the Future of Employment Support
summary: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence could significantly disrupt the political economy of the UK labour market. An economy where labour demand changes rapidly and unpredictably would require a new approach to employment support and skills devel
content: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence could significantly disrupt the political economy of the UK labour market. An economy where labour demand changes rapidly and unpredictably would require a new approach to employment support and skills development, but the UK's system of employment and retraining support is poorly equipped to handle a high level of disruption. This article proposes a policy solution called ‘portable benefits’, a new system of entitlements, savings and training rights based on the French Compte Personnel de Formation and emerging US pilots. Portable benefits would give workers flexible entitlements across jobs, including training credits, income security, legal support and access to worker organisations. The author argues it should be paired with higher expectations from employers to train, consult and redeploy their workforce and a stronger stronger system of cooperative labour market institutions.

title: The Value of Assetised Highways in City Logistics: Class, Commodities, Contradictions
summary: ABSTRACT Urban highways are built to accelerate the circulation of commodities—including labour power—across space, and they play a central role in global supply chains within urban landscapes. What happens when highways themselves are tran
content: ABSTRACT Urban highways are built to accelerate the circulation of commodities—including labour power—across space, and they play a central role in global supply chains within urban landscapes. What happens when highways themselves are transformed into commodities, or asset classes? How can we understand the role of the state in these dynamics and its social reproduction? Drawing on a historical‐geographical materialist approach, I examine the relationship between Highway 407—one of the world's highest‐toll roads—and Canada's largest logistics hub in the Toronto region, where truck freight predominates. I argue that Highway 407 emerged from, and remains deeply entangled with, the class and spatio‐temporal dynamics of capital accumulation shaped by city logistics. I further contend that the capitalist state has facilitated this process—albeit in incomplete and contradictory ways—through highway expansion and labour restructuring aimed at accelerating commodity circulation across space.

title: Siriah Ka Sidang as an Indigenous Mechanism for Customary Forest Governance in Minangkabau
source: International Journal of Asia Pacific Studies
summary: This study examines how siriah ka sidang, a customary conflict resolution mechanism practised by the indigenous community of Nagari Pasia Laweh, West Sumatra, contributes to ecological sustainability, social cohesion, and culturally legitim
content: This study examines how siriah ka sidang, a customary conflict resolution mechanism practised by the indigenous community of Nagari Pasia Laweh, West Sumatra, contributes to ecological sustainability, social cohesion, and culturally legitimate justice. It addresses two questions: (1) How is siriah ka sidang practised? and (2) How does it influence forest governance, the preservation of ecological knowledge, and the reduction of long-term conflicts? A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through in-depth interviews, focus group discussions (FGDs), and participatory observation conducted between June 2025 and May 2026. The findings identify three key principles. First, hearings are convened only after community members submit reports supported by sufficient evidence of customary law violations. Second, proceedings take place only when both parties voluntarily agree to participate, fulfil the required procedures, and accept the final decision. Third, the mechanism prioritises reconciliation, collective responsibility, and environmental stewardship rather than punishment, thereby supporting sustainable forest governance, preserving ecological knowledge, and preventing long-term conflicts. This study concludes that siriah ka sidang reflects the principles of the green economy and exemplifies embedded ecological governance, in which ecological management is rooted in cultural values, customary institutions, local beliefs, and community relationships while promoting a restorative model of justice perceived as more legitimate and effective than alternative dispute-resolution mechanisms.

title: Psychological distress, stigma, and intersectional marginalization in lesbian and bisexual cisgender women in Chinese higher education: a thematic analysis guided by minority stress theory
summary: Background Lesbian and bisexual cisgender women in Chinese higher education institutions (HEIs) face compounded psychological distress at the intersection of gender- and sexuality-based stigma. Despite growing evidence of mental health disp
content: Background Lesbian and bisexual cisgender women in Chinese higher education institutions (HEIs) face compounded psychological distress at the intersection of gender- and sexuality-based stigma. Despite growing evidence of mental health disparities among LGBTQ populations in China, the mechanisms through which structural marginalization is internalized in educational settings remain poorly understood. Objective To identify how structural stigma is translated into internalized psychological harm among lesbian and bisexual cisgender women in Chinese HEIs, through specific, theoretically specified mechanisms. Methods Using a critical realist, reflexive thematic analysis design, I conducted semi-structured interviews with eight self-identified lesbian, bisexual, or same-sex attracted cisgender women at universities in four province-level regions of China. Analysis followed Braun and Clarke's (2006) six-phase approach, guided by Meyer's (2003) minority stress model, Hatzenbuehler's (2009) psychological mediation framework, and Crenshaw's (1989) intersectionality theory. Researcher positionality was integrated analytically throughout. Results Five themes were identified: (1) awareness of structural inequality as anticipatory anxiety and cognitive vigilance; (2) institutional resource deprivation undermining academic self-efficacy; (3) enacted and internalized stigma and their psychological consequences, including shame, identity concealment, and self-reported depressive symptoms; (4) intersectional invisibility compounding distress; and (5) attenuated outcomes where community and institutional support are present. Three mediation pathways were consistently operative: social-cognitive, emotional regulatory, and interpersonal (Hatzenbuehler, 2009). No diagnostic instrument was administered; all psychological states reported are self-described and interpreted from interview accounts. Discussion Distal stigma, internalized homophobia, culture-specific marriage pressure, and regional pathologization interact in complex ways to shape distress, disrupted identity development, and academic disengagement. I examine the limits of applying Western minority stress frameworks in a collectivist context and propose responses grounded in trauma-informed care, LGBTQ-affirmative services, enumerated non-discrimination policy, and educator anti-stigma training. Conclusion The psychological distress of this underserved population is structurally produced, psychologically mediated, and institutionally addressable. Affirmative mental health infrastructure, enumerated anti-discrimination policy, and LGBTQ-inclusive educator training can meaningfully reduce minority stress and its consequences.

title: Managing Solar-Powered Digital Education Infrastructure: Institutional Capacity, Financing, and Sustainability in Rural India
source: Journal of Management for Global Sustainability
summary: Solar-powered digital infrastructure is increasingly being promoted as a sustainable solution for rural education; however, its long-term viability depends less on technological deployment than on institutional management capacity. This stu
content: Solar-powered digital infrastructure is increasingly being promoted as a sustainable solution for rural education; however, its long-term viability depends less on technological deployment than on institutional management capacity. This study examines how solar-powered digital classrooms (SPDCs) are governed, financed, and sustained in eleven rural government schools in Telangana, India. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model and an institutional perspective on sustainability, the study conceptualizes renewable energy integration as a public-sector management process rather than a purely technological intervention. An exploratory case study design was employed using semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, and institutional document analysis. The findings indicate that while solar installations improve energy reliability, reduce electricity expenditure, and support digitally mediated instruction, long-term sustainability depends on institutionalized governance mechanisms, lifecycle-oriented financing, structured maintenance systems, and continuous teacher capacity development. In the absence of these conditions, solar initiatives remain short-term, project-based interventions rather than durable institutional assets. The study contributes to sustainability and management scholarship by reframing solar-powered educational infrastructure as an organizational capability shaped by governance, finance, and institutional learning processes. As the analysis is limited to eleven schools in a single district, the findings are context-specific but offer transferable insights for similar resource-constrained settings.

title: Effects of NPL, NIM, and BOPO on ROA of Banks in the LQ45 Index
source: Jurnal Relevansi Ekonomi Manajemen dan Bisnis
summary: Bank profitability may fluctuate substantially as credit quality, interest margin generation, and operating efficiency change, making Return on Assets (ROA) an important but potentially unstable indicator of bank performance. This study exa
content: Bank profitability may fluctuate substantially as credit quality, interest margin generation, and operating efficiency change, making Return on Assets (ROA) an important but potentially unstable indicator of bank performance. This study examined the effects of Non-Performing Loans (NPL), Net Interest Margin (NIM), and Operating Expenses to Operating Income (Beban Operasional terhadap Pendapatan Operasional/BOPO) on the Return on Assets (ROA) of banks included in the LQ45 Index of the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2018–2024. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data from annual reports, with five banking companies and 35 balanced-panel observations selected through purposive sampling. Panel-data regression was estimated using EViews 12, and the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests were used to select the appropriate model. The random-effects model was selected. The results show that NPL has a negative but insignificant effect on ROA, while NIM has a positive significant effect and BOPO has a negative significant effect. NPL, NIM, and BOPO jointly had a significant effect on the ROA. This study was limited to five LQ45 banking companies and three internal financial ratios. The findings contribute empirical evidence on bank profitability during the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods and provide a basis for future studies to consider additional bank-specific and macroeconomic factors.

title: SuperApps and Omnichannel Banking: Infrastructure and UserCentric Design Strategies for Financial Inclusion
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF BANKING AND FINANCE RESEARCH
summary: Financial management has been revolutionized by mobile banking, but increasing usefulness and satisfaction requires a better user experience. This academic article would explore how SuperApps—integrated mobile platforms that combine multipl
content: Financial management has been revolutionized by mobile banking, but increasing usefulness and satisfaction requires a better user experience. This academic article would explore how SuperApps—integrated mobile platforms that combine multiple financial and lifestyle services into a single interface—can serve as a game-changing model for improving financial inclusion in the United States. It would analyze how user-centric design, interoperable infrastructure, and omnichannel banking strategies (mobile, web, in-branch, ATM, and agent networks) can address longstanding barriers to banking access, especially in rural, low-income, immigrant, and underserved communities.

title: CEO Conversational Receptiveness and Its Role in Reducing ESG Controversies
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) controversies can severely damage firms' legitimacy, reputation, and stakeholder trust. Yet little is known about how CEO leadership behaviors shape firms' exposure to such unfavorable ES
content: ABSTRACT Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) controversies can severely damage firms' legitimacy, reputation, and stakeholder trust. Yet little is known about how CEO leadership behaviors shape firms' exposure to such unfavorable ESG outcomes. Drawing on Information Processing Theory, we examine whether CEO conversational receptiveness, the extent to which CEOs signal willingness to engage with opposing views, is associated with fewer ESG controversies. We argue that conversationally receptive CEOs may facilitate earlier detection of ESG risks, more constructive resolution of emerging issues, and a more open communication climate within the firm. Using multi‐source panel data from 463 S&P 500 firms between 2006 and 2021 (4614 firm‐year observations), we find that CEO conversational receptiveness is negatively associated with ESG controversies. Moreover, this relationship is strengthened when firms possess higher financial slack and larger boards. By extending conversational receptiveness to the organizational level and identifying governance conditions under which it is most effective, we contribute to receptiveness literature and ESG risk mitigation.

title: Polyvinylpyrrolidone-capped MAPbBr3 perovskite nanocrystals synthesized and processed in isopropanol
summary: Lead halide perovskite nanocrystals are promising candidates for many optical and opto-electronic applications due to their strong absorption, high photoluminescence quantum yields, and straightforward synthesis. However, the stability of t
content: Lead halide perovskite nanocrystals are promising candidates for many optical and opto-electronic applications due to their strong absorption, high photoluminescence quantum yields, and straightforward synthesis. However, the stability of these nanocrystals is unsatisfactory, and the synthesis and processing requires undesirable solvents such as DMF, and toluene. These drawbacks not only adversely impact environment, health, and safety, but also renders them incompatible with various industrial processes. To make perovskite nanocrystals widely applicable, an alternative synthesis is crucial, addressing these shortcomings while retaining advantageous properties. Herein, we present a practical, scalable method to synthesize MAPbBr 3 nanocrystals in isopropanol. The nanocrystals, capped with polyvinylpyrrolidone, are around 40nm in size, cubic, and show good optical quality. Polyvinylpyrrolidone capping enhances their stability, making the nanocrystals tolerant to suspension in isopropanol, moisture, and elevated temperatures. In contrast to conventional MAPbBr 3 nanocrystals, which are made in DMF or toluene and degrade in alcohols, these PVP-capped nanocrystals are synthesized, kept, and processed entirely in a green alcohol solvent. This environmentally and safety conscious method offers new routes for practical synthesis and processing of stable perovskite nanocrystals with advanced functionalities.

title: How the Digital Economy Promotes High-Quality Agricultural Development by Improving Agricultural Efficiency
summary: This study examines whether and how the digital economy promotes high-quality agricultural development in China. Using provincial panel data for 30 provinces from 2005 to 2020, it constructs a multidimensional index covering development sca
content: This study examines whether and how the digital economy promotes high-quality agricultural development in China. Using provincial panel data for 30 provinces from 2005 to 2020, it constructs a multidimensional index covering development scale, efficiency, benefits and cost, and estimates fixed-effects, geographically weighted regression and spatial Durbin models. The results indicate that the digital economy is positively associated with high-quality agricultural development. The estimated effect is stronger in provinces with more advanced digital infrastructure and human capital, and the spatial analysis suggests positive spillovers across neighboring regions. Mechanism tests show that digitalization primarily improves development scale and benefits and also raises agricultural efficiency, while the coefficient for development cost is not statistically significant. The paper therefore recommends strengthening rural digital infrastructure, integrating agricultural supply chains, developing farmers' digital capabilities, improving technology and finance policies, and tailoring support to regional conditions. These measures can reduce information and transaction costs and support a more productive, inclusive and environmentally sustainable agricultural transformation.

title: Regularity Clarity Over Restriction Strategic AI and Fintech Adoption Across Global Financial Services
source: International Journal of Computer Information Systems and Industrial Management Applications
summary: The environment of the financial services industry is changing even quicker with the progress in fintech and artificial intelligence and the need to carefully analyse the regulatory implication of a trend and its strategic implementation by
content: The environment of the financial services industry is changing even quicker with the progress in fintech and artificial intelligence and the need to carefully analyse the regulatory implication of a trend and its strategic implementation by an institution depending on that institution. The disparity in performance of the fintech type of the business models in the different facets to financial inclusion examined by the current study and the connection between the regulatory set degree and loss in the adoption of technology. In the present article, the responses of 128 financial firms in five international regions are taken into account based on 128 financial firms in 5 global regions as reported by the world economic forum and secondary data as reported by the Institute of international Finance survey. It achieves this with the help of potent statistics tools including chi-square, correlation, multiple regression, ANOVA. The strategy embodies every component of the industry considering banks, insurance companies, and asset management organizations. Things that specifically caught my eye include the fact that, though regulatory barriers are admittedly a massive barrier in terms of technological integration, the factor of regulation clarity has a positive impact on the fintech shift to a noteworthy degree. Digital lending also proved more successful than Insurtech, wealthtech, and Regtech related to a never-before-seen effective model of financial inclusion. Good relationships are values towards AI on the complaints desk and in the fraud-detection area, suggesting that the technology solutions are getting tactically deployed. Curiously enough, pattern-oriented AI variation was not so high considering the geographical environment, i.e. the ones that that-technological intentions objectives are convergent in our world. Such results can help support the theoretical treatise of the stance that regulation has in financial innovation and provide practical recommendations on how global financial inclusion could be enhanced by achieving strategic use of technology. They are more specifically descriptive to policy makers when developing regulatory systems, and financial institutions strategizing on technology adoptability.

title: Bridging the Abyss: Reclaiming Spirituality in Academic Knowledge Production
summary: Over recent decades, Western academia has shown a growing interest in spirituality, accompanied by methodological innovations and epistemological expansion. Nevertheless, spiritual inquiry continues to be subtly subordinated to scientific r
content: Over recent decades, Western academia has shown a growing interest in spirituality, accompanied by methodological innovations and epistemological expansion. Nevertheless, spiritual inquiry continues to be subtly subordinated to scientific rationalism, with Western science often presiding as gatekeeper over what is considered legitimate knowledge. Drawing on Boaventura de Sousa Santos’ concept of abyssal thinking, this article argues that spiritual and experiential forms of knowing remain largely relegated to the far side of an epistemic divide, valued only insofar as they can be reframed within scientific norms. Despite increasing institutional recognition of spirituality in fields such as education, psychology, and medicine, these validations frequently rely on criteria set by the dominant paradigm, thereby reinforcing the hegemony they purport to challenge. To explore the possibility of a more equitable dialogue between science and spirituality, this article looks at the life and work of Rudolf Steiner (1861–1925), whose spiritual science (Geisteswissenschaft) offers an early example of first-person inquiry grounded in rigorous cognitive training. Steiner’s anthroposophy represents an integrated onto-epistemology that seeks to bridge the Cartesian divide by cultivating enhanced faculties of perception through disciplined practice. I examine how Steiner’s contributions have been, in part, validated in educational and agricultural contexts, while also noting the discursive vacuum around his spiritual methodologies. Ultimately, the article calls for a reconceptualisation of research into spirituality, one in which inner experience is not merely documented by others but is recognised as a valuable site of knowledge production. It suggests that meaningful convergence between science and spirituality will require researchers who are also spiritual practitioners, and spiritual practitioners with a grounding in research practices, inhabiting both epistemic domains with rigour and integrity. Only then might we move beyond the entrenched schism between soul and science, one born of Western rationalism’s claim to epistemic supremacy, and begin to imagine-–and practise-–a more inclusive and integrative vision of knowledge.

title: Droughts and borrowing patterns in poor countries: Evidence from Tanzania
source: Journal of International Financial Markets Institutions and Money
summary: This paper examines whether and to what extent droughts reshape household borrowing patterns in fragmented credit markets in developing economies. Using nationally representative household panel data from the two most recent waves (2014/15
content: This paper examines whether and to what extent droughts reshape household borrowing patterns in fragmented credit markets in developing economies. Using nationally representative household panel data from the two most recent waves (2014/15 and 2020/21) in Tanzania combined with drought indicators, we analyse borrowing responses across lender types – banks, microfinance institutions, and informal lenders – and across credit purposes – business, non-food consumption, and subsistence expenditures. Tanzania is used as a representative case of sub-Saharan African economies that share three institutional features: fragmented credit markets with a dominant informal lending sector, rain-fed agricultural livelihoods exposed to drought risk, and low financial inclusion. The paper reports three findings. First, droughts do not increase borrowing from banks and microfinance institutions but significantly increase borrowing from informal lenders. Second, drought-induced credit is directed at subsistence rather than productive recovery. Third, we examine three mechanisms that may explain these patterns: financial inclusion, credit tightening, and drought-caused crop failures. Results show that households farther from bank branches and mobile money agents significantly increase informal borrowing during droughts. For credit tightening, we find no significant borrowing response from formal lenders, and in some cases, a decline in formal borrowing. Results also show that households experiencing drought-induced crop failures significantly increase subsistence borrowing. These results reconceptualise climate-shock credit response in fragmented financial markets, demonstrating that droughts can reallocate borrowing across market segments and loan purposes.

title: Semi-pessimistic Reinforcement Learning
source: Journal of the American Statistical Association
summary: Offline reinforcement learning aims to learn an optimal policy from pre-collected data. However, it faces challenges of distributional shift, where the learned policy may encounter unseen scenarios not covered in the offline data. Additiona
content: Offline reinforcement learning aims to learn an optimal policy from pre-collected data. However, it faces challenges of distributional shift, where the learned policy may encounter unseen scenarios not covered in the offline data. Additionally, numerous applications suffer from a scarcity of labeled reward data. Relying on labeled data alone often leads to a narrow state-action distribution, further amplifying the distributional shift, and resulting in suboptimal policy learning. To address these issues, we first recognize that the volume of unlabeled data is typically substantially larger than that of labeled data. We then propose a semi-pessimistic reinforcement learning method to effectively leverage abundant unlabeled data. This approach offers several advantages. It considerably simplifies the learning process, as it seeks a lower bound of the reward function, rather than that of the Q-function or state transition function. It is highly flexible, and can be integrated with a range of model-free and model-based reinforcement learning algorithms. It enjoys the guaranteed improvement when utilizing vast unlabeled data, but requires less restrictive conditions. We compare the method with a number of alternative solutions, both analytically and numerically, and demonstrate its clear competitiveness. We further illustrate with an application to adaptive deep brain stimulation for Parkinson’s disease.

title: Effects of Internal Migration on the Life Satisfaction of Apprentices
source: Applied Research in Quality of Life
summary: Abstract Migration can have far-reaching implications for individuals’ life satisfaction (LS). Previous research has mostly examined how migration influences LS using broad samples of the adult population. Moreover, it has not sufficiently
content: Abstract Migration can have far-reaching implications for individuals’ life satisfaction (LS). Previous research has mostly examined how migration influences LS using broad samples of the adult population. Moreover, it has not sufficiently considered the influence of other important life events preceding, accompanying, or following migration. Consequently, its conclusions are not readily transferable to individuals in different life stages and their age-specific coupled life events. To narrow this research gap, we examine how migrating within Germany during the transition to vocational education and training (VET) influences the LS trajectories of apprentices. We estimate fixed-effect panel regressions using data from the German National Educational Panel Study (NEPS). Beyond a substantial increase in LS following the transition to VET, we find no significant average effect of VET-related migration on apprentices’ LS. However, we observe significant effect heterogeneity: migration to enter higher-status (versus lower-status) occupations and migration to urban (versus rural) regions yield larger (short-term) LS gains for apprentices. These results suggest that, beyond strictly VET-related factors, age-specific lifestyle amenities, which become accessible by moving towards urban regions, moderate the effects of internal migration on LS. Overall, our study illustrates the need to consider the specificity of life stages and coupled life events when analysing the effects of migration on LS.

title: Developing blockchain utilization capability in blockchain platforms: Indonesia's dynamic infrastructure and organizational factors
summary: This investigation develops and validates Blockchain Utilization Capability as a novel construct fundamentally reconceptualizing complex enterprise technology adoption by addressing critical limitations in conventional frameworks assuming d
content: This investigation develops and validates Blockchain Utilization Capability as a novel construct fundamentally reconceptualizing complex enterprise technology adoption by addressing critical limitations in conventional frameworks assuming direct antecedent-intention relationships. Through cross-sectional survey methodology examining 300 Indonesian SMEs actively engaged with blockchain platforms, we integrate Technology-Organization-Environment Framework with Technology Acceptance Model, positioning capability as central mediating mechanism analyzed using PLS-SEM with bootstrapping procedures. Results reveal complete mediation configurations wherein organizational infrastructure, environmental pressures, technological features, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use operate exclusively through capability development rather than directly influencing adoption intentions. Organizational dimensions demonstrate substantial effects on capability formation, while perceived ease of use exhibits paradoxical negative associations through suppression mechanisms, with the construct achieving superior predictive performance explaining considerable variance in adoption intentions. We introduce Capability-Mediated TAM, demonstrating perceptual beliefs require translation into organizational capabilities preceding complex technology adoption influence, bridging previously disconnected frameworks by revealing common capability-building pathways through which diverse antecedents operate, transforming TOE from descriptive taxonomy into dynamic process architecture. Findings establish that organizations should prioritize systematic capability development through phased approaches emphasizing organizational readiness, formal governance, and cross-functional integration preceding production implementations, recognizing capability building as essential rather than optional pathway toward blockchain adoption success.

title: Evaluating the Far-red Emitting Fluorescence-Activating and Absorption-Shifting Tag (frFAST) Chemogenetic Labeling System for Live-Cell Super-Resolution Microscopy
summary: Fluorogen-activating proteins (FAPs) provide renewable fluorescence signals through continuous fluorogen exchange, resulting in imaging that is virtually resistant to photobleaching, an especially appealing feature for deterministic super-r
content: Fluorogen-activating proteins (FAPs) provide renewable fluorescence signals through continuous fluorogen exchange, resulting in imaging that is virtually resistant to photobleaching, an especially appealing feature for deterministic super-resolution microscopy techniques. Furthermore, careful adjustment of the fluorogen concentration may lead to reversible, exchange-driven stochastic blinking, allowing the use of FAPs in stochastic superresolution microscopy methods. The green-light-excitable, far-red-emitting Fluorescence-Activating and Absorption-Shifting Tag (frFAST) is particularly well suited for biological imaging due to its favorable spectral properties and live-cell compatibility, however, its performance across different super-resolution microscopy (SRM) modalities has not been evaluated. Here, we assess frFAST for single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM), fluctuation-based computational approaches (super-resolution optical fluctuation imaging -SOFI and extended super-resolution radial fluctuations -eSRRF), and stimulated emission depletion (STED) microscopy. By tuning fluorogen concentration, we induced reversible stochastic blinking in fixed and live cells, enabling SMLM imaging of cytoskeletal structures and filopodia in mammalian and neuroblastoma cells, without the need for harsh reducing agents. Additionally, we successfully labeled and imaged mitochondrial outer membrane, microtubules, cytoskeleton and histone proteins in live cell STED microscopy.
