To address the issues of low efficiency in water flooding alone for ultra-low permeability reservoirs and the insufficient understanding of the mechanisms behind CO 2 miscible water-alternating-gas (WAG) enhanced oil recovery, this study takes the ultra-low permeability reservoir in the Qikeshu Oilfield as an example. Through slim-tube experiments, core flooding experiments combined with nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) testing, and numerical simulation, research was conducted on the minimum miscibility pressure (MMP) of CO 2 and crude oil, the microscopic characteristics of CO 2 miscible WAG flooding, and the optimization of gas-water cooperative injection and production parameters at the core scale. The research indicates that the minimum miscibility pressure between CO 2 and crude oil in the ultra-low permeability reservoir of the Qikeshu Oilfield is 20.6 MPa. The recovery factor of water flooding alone is relatively low, at only 18.36%. In contrast, pure miscible CO 2 flooding achieved the highest recovery factor of 71.56%, as no gas channeling occurred due to the strong homogeneity of the core. Overall, the miscible CO 2 WAG process with 8 slugs, involving gas injection followed by water injection, yielded the best oil recovery performance. The reason is that the initially injected CO 2 slug forms an efficient miscible zone at the displacement front through miscible effects, maximizing microscopic displacement efficiency. Subsequently injected water slugs help control mobility and expand the sweep volume of CO 2 . Simulation results and experimental findings are mutually verified. The research outcomes can not only provide relevant technical guidance and theoretical basis for the practical field development of ultra-low permeability reservoirs, but also contribute to achieving China’s dual-carbon strategic goals.

title: Commingled Injection and Separate-layer Production to Improve the Development Performance of Gas Flooding in Multi-layer Oil Reservoirs
summary: Abstract Continental low-permeability sandstone oil reservoirs generally have multiple layers and strong interlayer heterogeneity, which results in uneven sweep between layers and low oil recovery by gas flooding in the mode of commingled i
content: Abstract Continental low-permeability sandstone oil reservoirs generally have multiple layers and strong interlayer heterogeneity, which results in uneven sweep between layers and low oil recovery by gas flooding in the mode of commingled injection and commingled production. Conventional solutions such as separate-layer gas injection are immature and face a lot of engineering problems. This paper proposes a commingled gas injection but separate-layer oil production scheme to address the problem of interference between layers. According to the typical geological properties, reservoir properties, well pattern and well spacing parameters in Daqingzijing Oilfield in Jilin, a numerical CO 2 flooding model is established, and a set of method and process for designing the suitable production rate of each layer at the side of production well is developed. The results indicate that regarding the multi-layer heterogeneous oil reservoirs, the proposed commingled injection and separate-layer production scheme can effectively promote uniform displacement between layers and delay gas breakthrough. It can not only enlarge CO 2 swept volume in low-permeability layers, but also promote miscibility of CO 2 and oil in high-permeability layers, thus effectively improving the overall oil recovery.

title: Enhancing Well Integrity in Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage Applications: The Role of Insulating Gas Blankets
summary: Summary As part of the net-zero emission plan, capturing CO2 and storing it in geological formations is a key strategy. Existing wells are being repurposed, and new wells drilled to inject CO2 into depleted reservoirs as well as saline aqui
content: Summary As part of the net-zero emission plan, capturing CO2 and storing it in geological formations is a key strategy. Existing wells are being repurposed, and new wells drilled to inject CO2 into depleted reservoirs as well as saline aquifers. These operations are expected to continue for decades, making long-term well integrity critical. The variability of the CO2 phase and the rapid and severe temperature drop during vaporization challenge well integrity, impacting tubulars, connections, annular fluids, cement sheaths, and casing shoes. Integrity of outermost strings and associated cement sheaths and supporting formations is a key concern with particular focus on compressive loads. This study examines the use of insulating gas blankets in the tubing-to-casing annulus and outer annuli as a thermal barrier, mitigating the cooling effects of CO2 while addressing potential issues related to fluid shrinkage and pressure stability maintenance. Gas blankets in wellbore annuli are investigated using a fit-for-purpose application that integrates nodal flow assurance for wellbore temperature and pressure predictions with tubular stress analysis of casing and tubing strings. Gas blanket effectiveness is driven by the relatively low conductivity of gases and negation of natural convection of annular fluids. Surface chokes and reservoir injectivity are incorporated into the flow assurance and stress analysis within a nodal framework. CO2 injection is simulated with particular emphasis on especially cold events, such as injection restart, turn-down, and steady low-rate injection. Annular fluid contraction and expansion are accounted for as loading conditions on tubulars. By combining these factors, an operability envelope for the tubing-to-casing annulus (A-annulus) is established, ensuring pressure remains within limits to maintain integrity. A case study is presented to illustrate the design of a well incorporating nitrogen gas blankets within its design framework. Preliminary results indicate that insulating gas in the annuli effectively reduces heat transfer, thereby maintaining well integrity during CO2 injection. Additionally, it provides a buffer against annular fluid contraction, enhancing long-term well safety and performance. The required gas volumes are determined by predicted temperatures from flow simulations and tubular loads. Such analysis is crucial for newly drilled CO2 injection wells and for repurposing existing wells, ensuring reusability. Thermally induced compression loads on outer and structural strings near surface require careful review, including specification and qualification of connections. Applying insulating gas blankets in CO2 storage wells is a novel approach. While gas blankets are commonly used in deepwater wells, their application in platform and land wells is rare, making this approach unconventional in such settings. Furthermore, gas blankets have yet to be deployed widely in carbon capture, utilization, and storage (C

title: CO 2 Self-healing Resistant Cement Technology for China’s First Offshore CCUS Well
summary: Abstract For Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) wells, supercritical CO 2 exacerbates corrosion of the cement sheath, while cyclic temperature-pressure swings during CO 2 injection promote continuous stress damage to the cement
content: Abstract For Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) wells, supercritical CO 2 exacerbates corrosion of the cement sheath, while cyclic temperature-pressure swings during CO 2 injection promote continuous stress damage to the cement sheath, generating micro-cracks. Ordinary Portland cement (OPC) is susceptible to severe CO 2 corrosion and degradation, compromising long-term sheath integrity. To address the critical challenge, a CO 2 self-healing resistant cement slurry system (CSRC) was developed for CCUS well. Its effectiveness and durability were evaluated through the multi-functional supercritical CO 2 corrosion and self-healing simulation apparatus (SCCSA) that quantifies self-healing, corrosion resistance, and mechanical performance under alternating loads. Cement sheath integrity under multi-cycle CO 2 injection was simulated using a triaxial compression tester and numerical modeling. The CSRC system exhibits a rapid self-healing response to CO 2 , achieving >95% permeability self-healing efficiency within 12 hours and 100% by 24 hours, which is over 80 percentage points higher than OPC within 60 days of curing. It also demonstrates markedly higher compressive strength at all curing ages, with the strength difference increasing from 12 MPa to 25 MPa, alongside a 16.8-29.1 percentage points higher compressive strength self-healing efficiency, which together ensure more complete and lasting mechanical recovery. Furthermore, CSRC maintains high compressive strength and enables rapid early-stage recovery across multiple self-healing cycles, indicating its potential to mitigate performance degradation under cyclic loading or repeated damage. Under harsh CO 2 -rich conditions, it outperforms OPC by providing higher and continuously improving compressive strength, consistently lower permeability, and significantly reduced corrosion depth. Long-term integrity tests simulating CO 2 injection and cyclic loading confirmed that the CSRC cement sheath remained fully intact for 90 days, meeting the operational requirements for zonal isolation and long-term sealing in complex downhole environments. Finally, the successful application of CSRC in the first offshore CCUS well in China, validates its engineering feasibility under real CCUS conditions. These results confirm that the CSRC cement system is a reliable and effective technology for ensuring long-term zonal isolation and mechanical integrity in CCUS wells.

title: Effects of Supercritical CO 2 -Water-Rock Interactions on the Geochemical Properties of Tight Sandstone Reservoirs in the Ordos Basin
summary: Abstract Against the background of the “dual-carbon” targets, CO 2 -EOR and geological CO 2 storage are regarded as important technological pathways for achieving the coordinated development of cleaner and more efficient fossil energy utili
content: Abstract Against the background of the “dual-carbon” targets, CO 2 -EOR and geological CO 2 storage are regarded as important technological pathways for achieving the coordinated development of cleaner and more efficient fossil energy utilization and carbon emissions reduction. Supercritical CO 2 -water-rock interaction experiments were conducted under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions on tight sandstone reservoirs of the Yanchang Formation in the Ordos Basin. These experiments systematically investigated the effects of temperature- and pressure-dependent water-rock reactions on reservoir geochemical characteristics and pore structure evolution. The results show that under supercritical CO 2 injection conditions, formation water pH decreases markedly, while minerals such as calcite, dolomite, and feldspars undergo varying degrees of dissolution. This process leads to significant increases in the concentrations of Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , and K + in solution and the development of abundant secondary dissolution pores. Increasing reaction pressure enhances CO 2 solubility in the aqueous phase and intensifies the acidic environment, thereby significantly promoting mineral dissolution and increasing reservoir porosity. In contrast, increasing reaction temperature reduces CO 2 solubility and exerts an overall inhibitory effect on water-rock reactions, particularly suppressing calcite dissolution. These results indicate that supercritical CO 2 -water-rock interactions substantially alter the physical and geochemical properties of tight sandstone reservoirs, with important geological implications for improving reservoir flow conditions during CO 2 -EOR and for evaluating the long-term stability of subsequent geological CO 2 storage.

title: Sustainable Cement Production Technology
summary: Abstract Cement production is one of the most energy-consuming and carbon-emitting production processes worldwide, requiring the development of sustainable technologies that integrate CO 2 mineralization to limit environmental consequences.
content: Abstract Cement production is one of the most energy-consuming and carbon-emitting production processes worldwide, requiring the development of sustainable technologies that integrate CO 2 mineralization to limit environmental consequences. This research proposes a novel and sustainable cement production process that captures and reuses CO 2 emissions through chemical reaction with Solvay wastewater (mainly CaCl 2 ) in presence of ammonium hydroxide (NH 4 OH). The process results in the formation of calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ), which can be recycled into the kiln, and ammonium chloride (NH 4 Cl), which is valuable in fertilizers industry. The process was simulated by an Aspen plus using ELECNRTL fluid package, resulting in calcium carbonate and ammonium chloride yield of 242869Kg/hr and 97847.7Kg/hr respectively. This system creates a closed-loop CO 2 cycle, minimizes environmental pollution, and promotes circular economy principles by reducing emissions, raw material consumption, and waste disposal management.

title: Effects of reservoir heterogeneity on oil displacement efficiency and spatial utilization during coordinated construction of oil reservoir-based underground gas storage
summary: Based on the geological characteristics of the JD reservoir-based underground gas storage (UGS) facility, two-dimensional visual plate physical models representing vertical and areal heterogeneity were constructed. UGS operation was experim
content: Based on the geological characteristics of the JD reservoir-based underground gas storage (UGS) facility, two-dimensional visual plate physical models representing vertical and areal heterogeneity were constructed. UGS operation was experimentally simulated under two injection-production schemes. An experimental-scale compositional reservoir model was also developed to characterize the spatial sweep patterns under different heterogeneity configurations and injection-production modes. The results show that the vertically heterogeneous model generally achieves higher oil displacement efficiency than the areally heterogeneous model. The relative sweep efficiencies of the two models depend on the injection-production scheme. Their difference is small after a single depressurization cycle, whereas the vertically heterogeneous model exhibits higher sweep efficiency after repeated depressurization cycles. Compared with a single cycle, repeated depressurization cycles increase the injection-production pressure difference and intensify cyclic flow perturbations. These effects weaken the persistent dominance of preferential flow pathways on injection-production process, promote fluid mobilization in medium- and low-permeability zones, and markedly improve sweep efficiency during UGS operation. Given vertical heterogeneity, increasing heterogeneity intensifies gravity segregation and interlayer channeling, suppresses the sweep into low-permeability zones, and reduces sweep efficiency. Given areal heterogeneity, by contrast, increasing heterogeneity enhances the flow conductivity of high-permeability zones and improves displacement effectiveness within the swept areas, thereby increasing the overall sweep efficiency. Accordingly, stratified injection-production combined with graded pressure drawdown is recommended for vertically heterogeneous reservoirs to suppress channeling through high-permeability zones and improve the utilization of low-permeability zones. For areally heterogeneous reservoirs, optimized well placement and zonal injection-production should be combined with multistage depressurization cycles to improve storage-capacity utilization efficiency and operational stability.

title: Desarrollo de un modelo de inteligencia artificial para la clasificaión del nivel de práctica deliberada en ajedrecistas mediante marcadores EEG en bandas theta, alfa y beta asociados a eficiencia neural
source: Universidad Politécnica Salesiana Repositorio Digital (Universidad Politécnica Salesiana)
summary: El presente proyecto aborda el análisis de señales electroencefalográficas (EEG) con el propósito de explorar la clasificación del nivel de práctica deliberada en ajedrecistas mediante modelos de inteligencia artificial. El trabajo se desar
content: El presente proyecto aborda el análisis de señales electroencefalográficas (EEG) con el propósito de explorar la clasificación del nivel de práctica deliberada en ajedrecistas mediante modelos de inteligencia artificial. El trabajo se desarrolló a partir de una base de datos compuesta por 20 participantes infantiles, distribuidos en dos grupos según la intensidad del entrenamiento ajedrecístico reportado. Para efectos metodológicos, la práctica deliberada fue operacionalizada de manera indirecta a partir de indicadores relacionados con la frecuencia y continuidad del entrenamiento. El procesamiento de las señales encefalográficas incluyó etapas de filtrado, segmen- tación temporal, extracción de características espectrales y construcción de un dataset balanceado. A partir de 19 canales EEG se obtuvieron 114 características por segmento, incluyendo potencias logarítmicas en bandas theta, alfa, beta y gamma, además de ra- zones espectrales theta/beta y alfa/beta. Posteriormente, se implementaron modelos de clasificación supervisada, utilizando una arquitectura de perceptrón multicapa (MLP) como modelo principal y Random Forest como modelo baseline. La evaluación se realizó mediante validación Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) balanceada, con el fin de analizar la capacidad de generalización intersujeto. Los resultados mostraron que la arquitectura MLP reducida en la configuración C3 obtuvo el mejor desempeño según el criterio ROC-AUC, alcanzando una exactitud de 0.6113, un F1-score de 0.6661, un ROC-AUC de 0.7334 y una exactitud balanceada de 0.6113. Estos valores indican una capacidad discriminativa moderada, superior al azar, aunque insuficiente para establecer una clasificación definitiva entre grupos. El análisis de características evidenció tendencias espectrales distribuidas entre canales y bandas de frecuencia; sin embargo, las diferencias estadísticas evaluadas en la razón theta/beta no alcanzaron significancia después de la corrección por comparaciones múltiples. Esta investigación debe entenderse como una aproximación exploratoria, los datos obtenidos muestran que las señales encefalográficas pueden aportar información útil para estudiar diferencias neurofisiológicas asociadas al entrenamiento ajedrecístico, a pesar de esto, no permiten afirmar la existencia de biomarcadores definitivos de efi- ciencia neural, a partir de este trabajo queda implementado un flujo computacional para procesar señales EEG, extraer características espectrales y evaluar modelos de clasificación, para futuras investigaciones se recomienda ampliar la muestra, incorporar validación externa y utilizar instrumentos específicos para medir la práctica deliberada.

title: Energy-efficient neuromorphic computing: A multiplier-free CORDIC Engine for high-speed Izhikevich realization on FPGAs
source: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
summary: The cyber–physical integration of modern electrical power and energy systems increasingly demands high-performance, real-time computational tools. Bio-inspired computing paradigms, such as Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), offer a highly ener
content: The cyber–physical integration of modern electrical power and energy systems increasingly demands high-performance, real-time computational tools. Bio-inspired computing paradigms, such as Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), offer a highly energy-efficient framework for handling complex, data-driven analytics in these systems. However, their hardware implementation remains a significant challenge, heavily constrained by computational speed and power consumption. The Izhikevich model, celebrated for its rich nonlinear dynamics, exemplifies this issue; its resource-intensive quadratic term typically demands costly hardware multipliers, limiting scalability in power-constrained environments. This paper presents a highly optimized, low-power, and multiplier-free digital architecture for synaptic-coupled Izhikevich models on FPGAs, tailored to address the computational efficiency required by next-generation cyber–physical systems. Instead of a direct computation, we reformulate the model’s quadratic dynamics into a trigonometric representation. This transformation enables the deployment of a high-speed, customized CORDIC engine, effectively replacing the expensive multipliers. This refined geometric approach not only preserves the full spectrum of dynamic behaviors but also yields substantial performance gains. Our FPGA implementation demonstrates a significant 4.24-fold speedup and an 8% reduction in power consumption when benchmarked against conventional designs, while also showing notable improvements over other CORDIC-based approaches. This work provides a scalable and highly energy-efficient hardware pathway for developing real-time computational engines capable of complex, large-scale simulations in modern energy infrastructures.

title: Migration and distribution characteristics of CO 2 and influencing factors in deep saline aquifers
summary: Abstract Deep saline aquifers are regarded as the optimal carriers for large-scale CO 2 geological sequestration, and their storage efficiency and long-term stability are jointly controlled by reservoir physical properties and engineering i
content: Abstract Deep saline aquifers are regarded as the optimal carriers for large-scale CO 2 geological sequestration, and their storage efficiency and long-term stability are jointly controlled by reservoir physical properties and engineering injection parameters. In order to clarify the migration and evolution characteristics of CO 2 in deep saline aquifers and identify the dominant controlling factors of various sequestration mechanisms, a three-dimensional homogeneous numerical model was established in this study to simulate the full life cycle of 30-year CO 2 injection and 600-year storage. Combined with four core CO 2 trapping mechanisms (structural trapping, residual trapping, dissolution trapping, and mineral trapping), single-factor sensitivity analysis and orthogonal experiments were carried out to investigate the regulatory effects of reservoir permeability, injection rate and initial formation pressure on CO 2 plume sweep volume and sequestration performance, and the influence weight and significance of each factor were quantified via range analysis. The results show that the four trapping mechanisms present a sequential evolution pattern during the whole storage cycle: structural trapping dominates the injection stage, while residual and dissolution trapping gradually take the lead in the long-term storage period, and mineral trapping develops slowly and steadily. Permeability exerts a highly significant regulatory effect on all four trapping mechanisms and thereby dominates the migration, distribution, and morphological transformation of CO 2 . Injection rate only affects the short-term sweep range of the CO 2 plume and has no significant effect on long-term sequestration efficiency. Initial reservoir pressure imposes dual regulatory effects on the sequestration process, enhancing structural and residual trapping but inhibiting dissolution and mineral trapping. Furthermore, reservoir permeability is determined as the common dominant controlling factor for all CO 2 trapping mechanisms, initial formation pressure is the secondary controlling factor, and injection rate is a general influencing factor with insignificant effect.

title: Quantifying dissolved CO₂ storage: A unified NaCl‑based solubility model for CCS applications
summary: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) in deep saline aquifers requires a CO₂ solubility model that is accurate, computationally efficient, and transparent about its range of validity. This study develops a unified, physics-based correlation for
content: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) in deep saline aquifers requires a CO₂ solubility model that is accurate, computationally efficient, and transparent about its range of validity. This study develops a unified, physics-based correlation for CO₂ solubility in NaCl brines, integrating Henry-type equilibrium, temperature dependence, salting-out behavior, and a pressure-saturation correction into a closed-form expression calibrated against a compiled database (871 records; T = 338–447 K, P = 8.80–43.39 MPa, S = 1,000–71,938 mg/L NaCl-equivalent). The model achieves strong predictive accuracy (mean absolute percentage error of approximately 7–9%, R² = 0.93 after bootstrap validation), substantially outperforming a simpler empirical regression retained for rapid screening. A 1,000-replicate bootstrap quantifies parameter uncertainty, and a second-level Monte Carlo confirms that reservoir-condition variability, rather than parameter uncertainty, dominates predictive uncertainty. Sensitivity analysis shows solubility is most strongly governed by temperature and pressure, with a smaller, systematic salting-out effect from salinity. For basin-scale screening, an operational salinity cutoff of approximately 55,000 mg/L is derived from the solubility-to-salinity ratio, with an explicit mathematical basis, sensitivity testing across the calibrated range, and negligible effect on capacity estimates when varied between 45,000 and 65,000 mg/L. Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 realizations) yields P5, P50, and P95 CO₂ solubility estimates of 28,122, 31,230, and 45,539 mg/L for representative Thai conditions. Applied to eight major Thai saline aquifers, the framework estimates basin-level dissolved CO₂ storage capacities and provides a reproducible, efficient basis for regional CCS screening, uncertainty quantification, and future decision-support integration.

title: Virtual Reality: Enhancing Chemical Engineering Students' Learning in Process Safety
summary: The complexity of processes encountered in the field of chemical engineering poses a challenge for educators trying to deliver the field’s depth through traditional teaching methods. Virtual Reality (VR) offers dynamic, interactive experien
content: The complexity of processes encountered in the field of chemical engineering poses a challenge for educators trying to deliver the field’s depth through traditional teaching methods. Virtual Reality (VR) offers dynamic, interactive experiences that transcend these limitations and enable engagement beyond real-world limitations. This research adopted a constructivist approach to design process safety learning activities which could be experienced using a head-mounted display. Process control through supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) allowed students to observe real-time consequences of their actions, and safely reverse adverse or unstable events. The effectiveness of VR-based learning in process safety was evaluated among 80 undergraduate chemical engineering students across three universities. Students were assessed by comparing their pre- and post-VR results using properly designed Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP) questions embedded within the VR environment. Positive outcomes were reported, with students expressing greater confidence in utilizing VR as a platform for experiential learning of complex concepts and for developing transferable skills. Over 93% agreed that the tool was beneficial for learning process safety, while 96% indicated it enhanced decision-making (µ = 4.66, z = 0.53). This study serves as a reference for future studies to design virtual environments and contents for process safety education using a systematic pedagogical approach.

title: CO2-induced in-situ rapid mineralization in fractures to remedy CO2 leakage for safe carbon geo-sequestration
summary: Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) is crucial for climate change mitigation, yet CO 2 leakage through geological fractures significantly threatens storage security. Inspired by microbially induced carbonate precipitation and CO
content: Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) is crucial for climate change mitigation, yet CO 2 leakage through geological fractures significantly threatens storage security. Inspired by microbially induced carbonate precipitation and CO 2 mineralization sequestration in basalts, we propose an innovative method: injecting reactive minerals into fractures, where CO 2 triggers in-situ mineralization to form cementing carbonates, effectively remedying leakage pathways. To systematically evaluate the feasibility of this approach, macroscopic performance assessments were integrated with microscopic mechanistic analyses. Macroscopically, it was mainly reflected in compressive strength, mineralization degree and equivalent permeability test. Static experiments under high-temperature, high-pressure conditions showed that, among five tested silicate minerals, wollastonite achieved superior consolidation performance, with 2.56 MPa compressive strength and 82.38% mineralization degree after 7 days. Permeability measurements on fractured shale cores further quantified sealing effectiveness: for partially open fractures, permeability was reduced from 1.21×10 -4 to 9.60×10 -5 mD after 7 days; for fully open fractures, permeability decreased to 3.28 mD (7 days) and further to 2.31 mD (14 days), confirming effective fracture sealing. Microscopically, XRD, SEM, and EDS analyses elucidated the underlying mechanisms. XRD confirmed the transformation of silicates to carbonates, while SEM-EDS revealed intimate interfacial cementation between consolidated materials and shale surfaces via the reprecipitation of carbonate minerals. These findings collectively demonstrate that the proposed method effectively seals leakage pathways by promoting carbonate formation and robust interfacial bonding. This study demonstrates that CO 2 -induced in-situ mineralization is a reliable and efficient technique for enhancing the safety of geological CO 2 sequestration.

title: Carbon Credits, Capture and Storage Markets in the UAE
source: RIT Scholar Works (Rochester Institute of Technology)
summary: The growing urgency to address climate change has placed carbon markets and carbon capture technologies at the core of global climate strategies. This thesis looks into whether the United Arab Emirates can develop its emerging carbon credit
content: The growing urgency to address climate change has placed carbon markets and carbon capture technologies at the core of global climate strategies. This thesis looks into whether the United Arab Emirates can develop its emerging carbon credit framework into a platform that supports viable private investment and national sustainability goals. While systems that are established, such as the EU Emission Trading System (EU ETS) and voluntary schemes, such as Verra's Verified Carbon Standard (VCS), provide mature models, the UAE shows a unique case: a market still in its early stages yet backed by ambitious climate commitments and world-class hydrocarbon infrastructure. This research assesses the feasibility of developing a Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) enterprise within this developing market. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, combining sector-by-sector market analysis, original financial modelling of revenue per kilogram of CO₂, break-even analysis across nine scenarios, and policy benchmarking against leading international frameworks. Attention was given to the UAE’s hard-to-abate sectors: natural gas processing, steel, cement, fertilizers, and power generation, which collectively represent over 90% of the UAE’s major emitting sectors. The analysis finds that only two CCUS pathways are commercially profitable in the UAE today without government support: natural gas processing combined with Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR), yielding a net profit of $0 to +$50 per ton of CO₂; and ammonia or fertilizer production combined with EOR and urea feedstock, yielding +$0 to +$50 per ton. All other sectors require additional policy support, such as a domestic carbon incentive of approximately $50/t, to become commercially attractive. The thesis concludes with sector-specific recommendations for investors and policymakers to unlock the remaining revenue potential, close the 7.7-million-ton gap between current and targeted CCUS capacity, and position the UAE as a credible global hub for low-carbon industrial investment. Keywords: Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS); Carbon Credits; Carbon Markets; United Arab Emirates (UAE); Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR); Break-Even Analysis; CCUS Investment Feasibility.

title: La place de l’océan dans la transition énergétique
source: Annales des Mines - Responsabilité et environnement
summary: Longtemps oublié des politiques climatiques, l’océan est désormais au coeur des stratégies de neutralité carbone. L’émergence du « carbone bleu » comme axe stratégique de la Stratégie nationale bas-carbone impose ainsi une double mission de
content: Longtemps oublié des politiques climatiques, l’océan est désormais au coeur des stratégies de neutralité carbone. L’émergence du « carbone bleu » comme axe stratégique de la Stratégie nationale bas-carbone impose ainsi une double mission de sanctuarisation et de restauration des écosystèmes côtiers. Parallèlement, la géo-ingénierie et le stockage géologique offshore ouvrent des perspectives de séquestration active, mais leurs incertitudes environnementales et sociétales, ainsi que leur bilan carbone global, appellent à la prudence. Les énergies marines renouvelables constituent un levier majeur de décarbonation avec l’éolien offshore comme figure de proue. Cependant, l’intégration de ces infrastructures soulève des défis écologiques et matériels majeurs. Entre solutions fondées sur la nature et déploiement d’infrastructures critiques, comment définir une trajectoire maritime qui concilie urgence climatique et préservation des écosystèmes marins ?

title: End-of-life management of crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules: current technologies, economic constraints and future perspectives
source: Solar Energy Materials and Solar Cells
summary: The energy transition towards net-zero emissions is accelerating the global spread of photovoltaics (PV), simultaneously generating a growing flow of end-of-life (EoL) modules whose management represents one of the most urgent environmental
content: The energy transition towards net-zero emissions is accelerating the global spread of photovoltaics (PV), simultaneously generating a growing flow of end-of-life (EoL) modules whose management represents one of the most urgent environmental and economic challenges in the sector. Crystalline silicon (c-Si) modules, which dominate the market with a share exceeding 90 %, will constitute the main component of this waste stream, with cumulative volumes estimated between 60 and 78 million tonnes by 2050. Despite the growing interest from the scientific community, most of the proposed recycling technologies remain in the experimental phase, and critical aspects such as process costs, the quality of recovered materials, and the generation of secondary pollutants are still insufficiently addressed. This review critically analyses delamination and material recovery technologies for EoL c-Si modules, discussing their strengths, limitations, and development prospects, with particular attention to the technical, economic and environmental conditions necessary for the transition to industrially mature processes. The objective is to provide an updated analytical framework that can guide research and development choices in a sector poised for rapid growth in the coming decades.

title: Null Objects in Recipe Context
source: Ahi Evran Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Enstitüsü Dergisi
summary: In English, null objects are generally considered ungrammatical, except in certain registers such as recipes, user manuals, and sports reports. The present study examines null objects in the context of recipes using a corpus-based methodolo
content: In English, null objects are generally considered ungrammatical, except in certain registers such as recipes, user manuals, and sports reports. The present study examines null objects in the context of recipes using a corpus-based methodology, specifically focusing on five target verbs: bake, let, place, put, and serve. Utilizing a curated version of the FoodBase corpus and AntConc 3.5.9, the study investigates the syntactic features and limitations of these omissions. The findings demonstrate that null objects are significantly favored over direct objects (59.51%) and frequently precede prepositions. Crucially, while null objects are predominantly tied to subjectless imperatives, the study identifies rare instances of co-occurrence with overt subjects (e.g., in 'as you stir' constructions), challenging traditional syntactic assumptions. Furthermore, the results indicate that null objects avoid inflected verb forms but are relatively common in non-finite and participial constructions like 'until serving'. The study contributes to the understanding of argument omission in specialized discourse and underscores the role of corpus-driven analysis in refining theoretical models of English syntax.
