The study demonstrates the potential of combining optical and SAR data for effective, crop-specific flood monitoring in near real time.

title: Tourism expansion, economic development and environmental sustainability: Empırıcal evidence from Asia-Pacific countries
source: Erciyes Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Making economic growth sustainable, which is the aim of economies, has become the most important goal of the new century in order to leave a more livable world for future generations in an environmentally friendly way. Furthermore, the clos
content: Making economic growth sustainable, which is the aim of economies, has become the most important goal of the new century in order to leave a more livable world for future generations in an environmentally friendly way. Furthermore, the close relationship between economic development and tourism development brings the sustainable tourism approach to the forefront. Therefore, economies should be open to regional and international collaborations to move confidently towards achieving sustainable development goals with effective policies that include these elements. In this context, this study examines the determinants of tourism development, environmental performance, and economic growth in the most important tourism destinations of the Asia-Pacific Region (China, Thailand, Japan, Malaysia, Vietnam, India, South Korea, and Indonesia). Three separate models were created using data from the 2002-2020 period. Based on empirical findings, the first model shows that economic growth has a positive effect on tourism development. However, the regulatory quality variable has a negative effect on tourism, while no significant relationship was found between political stability and ecological footprint and tourism development. The second model concludes that tourism development increases economic growth, while ecological footprint decreases economic growth. Furthermore, political stability and regulatory quality variables were found to have a positive impact on economic growth. In the third model, only economic growth was observed to have a statistically significant and positive effect on the ecological footprint. The research findings provide important research areas for academics, as well as assisting planners in developing appropriate approaches to tourism.

title: Beyond Reputation: A Function for CSR in the Age of Systemic Crises. Evidence From the Italian Business Landscape
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Corporate Sustainability (CS) are historically distinct constructs that have converged to the point of conceptual confusion. This paper operates within the CSR tradition, arguing that authe
content: ABSTRACT Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Corporate Sustainability (CS) are historically distinct constructs that have converged to the point of conceptual confusion. This paper operates within the CSR tradition, arguing that authentic CS is structurally impossible without the ethical foundation CSR provides. Moving beyond shareholder value requires grounding CSR in Virtue Ethics rather than utilitarian or contractual frameworks. An original normative model is proposed: the Ethical CSR Function t ( x ( y )), in which ( y ) is the ethical foundation (Aristotelian habitus), ( x ) managerial intensity, and ( t ) the temporal horizon. An exploratory survey of 114 Italian companies reveals a persistent value gap: only 47% report a value system understood by all employees, and merely 13% show concern for future generations. These findings suggest that authentic CS requires an ethical foundation that compliance‐driven frameworks cannot generate, and offer scholars a normative instrument for distinguishing genuine sustainability commitments from reputational greenwashing.

title: Parental Involvement in Public Pre-primary Education in Ilemela District, Tanzania: Factors Influencing Participation
source: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
summary: This study explored the factors influencing parental involvement in public pre-primary education in Ilemela District, Mwanza Region, Tanzania. The study was guided by Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Theory, which explains children’s lea
content: This study explored the factors influencing parental involvement in public pre-primary education in Ilemela District, Mwanza Region, Tanzania. The study was guided by Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Theory, which explains children’s learning and development through interactions among family, school, community and wider social systems. A qualitative research approach within the interpretivist paradigm was adopted, using a case study design to gain detailed insights into parents’ participation in pre-primary education. The target population comprised 39 public pre-primary schools in Ilemela District Council. Participants included 20 parents of children attending selected public pre-primary schools, 20 teachers and 2 pre-primary education officers. Ten (10) public pre-primary schools were purposively selected, and data were collected through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions. The data were analysed thematically to identify recurring meanings and patterns related to parental participation in pre-primary education. The findings showed that three interrelated factors influenced parental involvement. First, parents’ awareness of the academic benefits of pre-primary education motivated them to enrol children, monitor attendance and support learning at home. Second, socio-cultural beliefs, community expectations, peer influence and guidance from local educational authorities shaped parents’ decisions to participate in pre-primary education. Third, school-related factors, including a welcoming school environment, teachers’ attitudes, communication practices and supportive parent-teacher relationships, encouraged parents to engage in school activities. The study concluded that individual awareness, social expectations and institutional practices shaped parental involvement in pre-primary education. It recommended strengthening parent-teacher collaboration, enhancing community sensitisation and fostering school environments that promote trust, communication and shared responsibility for children’s early learning.

title: Climate Change Documentary Film Analysis: Before the Flood
summary: This paper analyzes Before the Flood (2016) in relation to climate change, population health, and health equity. The documentary film analysis focuses on two interconnected climate-related issues: extreme rainfall and food insecurity in Sou
content: This paper analyzes Before the Flood (2016) in relation to climate change, population health, and health equity. The documentary film analysis focuses on two interconnected climate-related issues: extreme rainfall and food insecurity in South Asia, and sea-level rise and displacement in Kiribati. Using climate justice, environmental justice, planetary health, and United Nations Sustainable Development Goal frameworks, the paper argues that climate change is not only an environmental crisis but also a public health issue shaped by structural inequities. Drawing on peer-reviewed literature, the analysis demonstrates how climate-driven disruptions threaten agricultural livelihoods in India and Bangladesh, contribute to food insecurity and mental health stress, and pose existential risks to Pacific Island nations through freshwater insecurity, displacement, and cultural loss. The paper concludes with three evidence-informed, equity-centred recommendations: integrated early warning systems combined with climate-smart agriculture and weather-indexed crop insurance for South Asian farming communities; a dignity-centred planned relocation framework for Pacific Island nations; and mangrove ecosystem restoration as a cross-cutting, nature-based solution. Overall, the findings underscore that effective climate action must address ecological, social, and structural determinants of health together, and that health equity cannot be achieved without confronting the systemic inequities that leave vulnerable populations least able to adapt to a changing climate. Keywords: climate change, health equity, food insecurity, planned relocation, mangrove restoration, climate justice, planetary health

title: Temporal lag in post-mining regrowth amplifies carbon loss in tropical forests during the period 2000–2023
summary: Mining-induced deforestation is an under-recognized source of tropical forest carbon loss, and the extent to which post-mining regrowth offsets this loss remains unclear. Here, we reconstruct mining-related deforestation and subsequent fore
content: Mining-induced deforestation is an under-recognized source of tropical forest carbon loss, and the extent to which post-mining regrowth offsets this loss remains unclear. Here, we reconstruct mining-related deforestation and subsequent forest regrowth across the tropics from 2000 to 2023 using high-resolution satellite observations. We estimate that mining causes ~4537 km2 of deforestation, whereas post-mining regrowth covers ~300 km2, equivalent to 6.6% of the deforested area. Forest regrowth also exhibits a pronounced temporal lag, with ~40% occurring more than five years after deforestation and ~16% occurring at least a decade later. Mining-related deforestation results in ~47.5 Tg C of carbon loss, while regrowth contributes ~3.8 Tg C of carbon gain, offsetting 8% of losses. These findings indicate that post-mining forest regrowth provides a limited carbon offset, highlighting the need to improve both the extent and timeliness of forest recovery in mining-affected tropical forests. Mining-related deforestation can be a source of tropical forest carbon loss, but whether post-mining regrowth offsets it remains unclear. This study shows that post-mining forest regrowth is limited and delayed, amplifying carbon loss.

title: Ecological Construction of Religious Resilience among Islamic Education Students Facing Quarter-Life Crisis: A Comparative Case Study of Public and State Islamic Campus Ecologies
summary: Islamic Religious Education (IRE/PAI) students are highly vulnerable to quarter-life crises amidst intense social expectations of piety. This study aims to analyze and compare the construction of PAI students' religious resilience in naviga
content: Islamic Religious Education (IRE/PAI) students are highly vulnerable to quarter-life crises amidst intense social expectations of piety. This study aims to analyze and compare the construction of PAI students' religious resilience in navigating this crisis at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia (UPI) and UIN Sunan Gunung Djati Bandung. A qualitative comparative case study design was applied to eight purposively selected informants, four at each site, in their fifth and seventh semesters, through indepth interviews, ecological observation, and document analysis, followed by intra- and cross-case analysis. Findings reveal that the heterogeneous general university ecology of UPI fosters flexible and independent resilience, supported by restorative physical spaces. Conversely, the religioncentred state Islamic university ecosystem of UIN offers strong structural support but carries risks of social-moral pressure due to standardized communal piety. This study concludes that religious resilience is not an innate attribute (given trait), but rather a systemic construction significantly shaped by the campus ecosystem (ecological construction of religious resilience)

title: Silencing dissent: military co-optation and authoritarian consolidation in Nigeria’s Fourth Republic
summary: Literature has shown a resurgence of authoritarianism across Africa since the early 2000s, both hybrid and fully consolidated forms, whether through democratically elected leaders consolidating power or via military coups, as recently obser
content: Literature has shown a resurgence of authoritarianism across Africa since the early 2000s, both hybrid and fully consolidated forms, whether through democratically elected leaders consolidating power or via military coups, as recently observed in Niger, Burkina Faso, Sudan, Mali, and Guinea. This article argues that Nigeria, under the APC government, has transitioned toward authoritarianism, consolidating control through the systematic co-optation of military and security institutions and the strategic suppression of dissent. Adopting a qualitative research design based on document and content analysis, this study draws on media reports, official statements, legal frameworks, and observer reports to examine patterns of state behaviour. It focuses on the militarisation of elections, the imposition of a state of emergency in opposition strongholds such as Rivers State, and the coerced defection of key opposition figures as mechanisms of political control. The findings reveal a systematic use of institutional power, intimidation, and military co-optation to capture political space and weaken opposition mobilisation, demonstrating how formally democratic processes are subordinated to authoritarian objectives. The article identifies a shift in the operational logic of authoritarian consolidation from primarily electoral manipulation to an institutionalised reliance on coercive state power, in which military co-optation serves not only to suppress opposition but also to manage elite cohesion within the ruling coalition.

title: Research on Technological Risks and Governance Mechanisms in Morocco’s Renewable Energy Transition
source: International Journal of Global Economics and Management
summary: With the rapid depletion of the Earth’s natural resources, green development approaches such as low-carbon development and energy transition are becoming major directions for economic development across the world. In recent years, Morocco h
content: With the rapid depletion of the Earth’s natural resources, green development approaches such as low-carbon development and energy transition are becoming major directions for economic development across the world. In recent years, Morocco has introduced a series of incentive measures to support renewable energy, injecting strong momentum into the transformation of its energy structure. However, current technical barriers, talent structure issues, and energy cost pressures continue to constrain the country’s energy transition process. Based on a literature analysis method, this paper systematically examines policy documents and publicly available data to investigate the major technological risks and governance mechanisms involved in Morocco’s renewable energy transition.

title: Shocks and labour mobility across rural–urban destinations: Evidence from Ethiopia
summary: Abstract Motivation Labour mobility is an important driver of economic development in low‐ and middle‐income countries. It is driven by pull factors that increase labour productivity in destination areas and improve the expected returns to
content: Abstract Motivation Labour mobility is an important driver of economic development in low‐ and middle‐income countries. It is driven by pull factors that increase labour productivity in destination areas and improve the expected returns to migration, as well as by push factors such as shocks and risks in areas of origin. Purpose This study empirically examines the role of shocks in shaping rural labour mobility decisions, focusing on participation and destination choices. Recognizing that rural households in low‐ and middle‐income countries are often exposed to multiple and frequent shocks, we identify more than 30 types of shocks across six domains—COVID‐19, production, marketing, institutional, financial, and personal—and analyse the effects of overall and domain‐specific shocks on labour mobility outcomes. Moreover, we distinguish between different labour mobility destinations and examine migration to rural villages, secondary towns, and cities. Approach and methods Using data from a three‐round household survey of 806 observations, we apply cross‐sectional probit, trivariate probit, and conditional mixed process regression models, complemented with an IV approach. Findings Results show that exposure to shocks is associated with a higher likelihood of labour mobility, with resource‐poor households more likely to migrate to rural destinations. The estimated effects vary by shock type and mobility destination and suggest that production shocks promote rural–rural migration but deter urban migration, while personal and financial shocks stimulate movements to urban or secondary‐town destinations. Policy implications These patterns highlight the differentiated role of migration as a risk‐coping strategy and underscore the need for policies that strengthen production resilience and promote financial inclusion to help households cope with shocks and make more effective decisions around labour mobility.

title: Effects of mulch-based conservation tillage and nutrient management on sweet corn growth and yield under dryland conditions
source: Jurnal Agronomi Indonesia (Indonesian Journal of Agronomy)
summary: The study aimed to examine the effect of mulch-based conservation tillage combined with different nutrient management practices on the growth and yield of sweet corn under dryland conditions. The experiment was arranged in a randomized comp
content: The study aimed to examine the effect of mulch-based conservation tillage combined with different nutrient management practices on the growth and yield of sweet corn under dryland conditions. The experiment was arranged in a randomized complete block design with six treatment combinations involving tillage system, organic mulch, organic manure, and inorganic fertilizer input. Each treatment was replicated three times. Growth parameters included plant height, leaf number, and leaf color, while yield components were measured at harvest. The results showed that plant height did not differ significantly among treatments at 21 and 35 days after planting (DAP), but a significant treatment effect was detected at 49 DAP. Leaf number did not differ significantly at 21 DAP but was significantly affected at 35 and 49 DAP. This indicates that, during the initial stage, sweet corn growth was more influenced by seed reserves and plant vigor than by external treatments. However, treatment effects became clearer at the later growth stage. The integrated nutrient management treatment (P5), consisting of 50% inorganic fertilizer combined with organic manure and organic mulch, produced the best vegetative performance, with the highest plant height (178.00±06.82 cm) and leaf number (13.67±0.58 leaves per plant). P5 also produced the longest cobs (18.60±0.50 cm) while maintaining high cob weight (397±54 g) and sweetness (13.91±0.08 °Brix), both statistically comparable to full inorganic fertilization. Although full-dose inorganic fertilizer + conventional tillage treatment (P1) produced the largest cob diameter (7.36±0.11 cm), the results demonstrate that reducing inorganic fertilizer by 50% through integrated nutrient management can maintain yield quality while supporting more sustainable sweet corn production under tropical dryland conditions. Keywords: crop productivity; dryland farming; integrated nutrient management; organic amendment; soil conservation.

title: The impact of teacher support on EFL student engagement in Ethiopian higher education
summary: Student participation is an essential component of effective English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning in Ethiopian higher education. Although teacher support is widely acknowledged to be an important element, the specific impact of vari
content: Student participation is an essential component of effective English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning in Ethiopian higher education. Although teacher support is widely acknowledged to be an important element, the specific impact of various types of assistance, as well as the possible influence of gender, remain unexplored in Ethiopia. The purpose of this study was to examine how different types of teacher assistance affect cognitive, emotional, and behavioral involvement in EFL students at Ethiopian institutions. A mixed-methods research design was employed, involving 800 undergraduate students from four public universities (Jimma, Wachamo, Wolaita Sodo, and Wolkite). Structured questionnaires and semi-structured interviews were used to assess students' perceptions of instrumental, informational, affective, and evaluative support. The findings revealed that students experienced a somewhat supportive learning environment, with instrumental support rated highest in perceived usefulness. However, informational support emerged as the most significant predictor across all engagement areas. Evaluative support had a notable impact on behavioral engagement, while effective and instrumental support showed minimal direct benefits. Affective support demonstrated a positive trend. There were no significant differences between genders regarding perceptions of teacher support or levels of involvement. These findings underscore the importance of timely feedback, clear instruction, and scaffolded learning in enhancing engagement. The study recommends that teacher training and institutional policies focus on emotionally sensitive and differentiated pedagogical practices to foster inclusive and equitable EFL learning environments.

title: Alcohol and social control: customary authority versus management authority in the construction and management of ‘deviance’ in Fiji soccer, 1980–2000
summary: The aim of this article is to interrogate the use of alcohol in elite soccer in the Fiji Islands covering the period 1980–2000. Based on interviews with six ex-Premier League players from the 1980s, and participant-observation, we find that
content: The aim of this article is to interrogate the use of alcohol in elite soccer in the Fiji Islands covering the period 1980–2000. Based on interviews with six ex-Premier League players from the 1980s, and participant-observation, we find that alcohol works as a form of currency, social lubricant, source of temptation, tool of tribute, and tool of resistance. Alcohol-related excesses reveal and are a product of the wealth disparity and income-inequality between the Fiji Indian businessmen, who manage, control and sponsor the sport, and the mostly very poor players (both Indigenous and Fiji Indian) who require payment and organisation from powerful others to go on overseas playing trips. The players are aware of these inequalities and find ways to assert their independence including social drinking. They assert their independence in this way to maximise the enjoyment factor and to create memories that can be recalled as the years pass.

title: Religious Moderation as An Effort to Increase Religious Understanding Among Teenagers in Bekasi Regency
summary: As a nation rich in religious and cultural diversity, Indonesia faces challenges in maintaining interfaith harmony, particularly among the younger generation. Adolescents—the group most vulnerable to the influence of radicalization—require
content: As a nation rich in religious and cultural diversity, Indonesia faces challenges in maintaining interfaith harmony, particularly among the younger generation. Adolescents—the group most vulnerable to the influence of radicalization—require a moderate understanding of religion to prevent potential social conflict. With its large youth population, Bekasi Regency serves as a strategic location for implementing religious moderation to foster a more inclusive and tolerant religious understanding. This study aims to explore the role of religious moderation in enhancing religious understanding among adolescents in Bekasi Regency and to analyze the factors influencing the application of religious moderation in their daily lives. A qualitative approach utilizing a case study design was employed. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and focus group discussions with adolescents from diverse religious and social backgrounds in Bekasi Regency. Purposive sampling was used to obtain in-depth insights into perceptions and practices regarding religious moderation among the youth. The findings indicate that adolescents in Bekasi Regency tend to possess a moderate religious understanding when they participate in religious activities that promote tolerance and inclusivity. Religious education emphasizing values ​​of religious moderation has proven effective in reducing radical attitudes and strengthening interfaith relations among adolescents. The study concludes that religious moderation is key to fostering a more inclusive and tolerant religious understanding among young people. Consequently, efforts to integrate religious moderation into religious education and activities in Bekasi Regency can enhance social harmony among adolescents. This research makes a significant contribution to the development of more moderate religious education, particularly for the youth. The findings are expected to serve as a reference for policymakers and educators in designing curricula that promote religious moderation at the local level.

title: The dynamics of urban growth rate on carbon footprints in the SADC
summary: This paper examines the influence of urban growth rates on per capita carbon emissions across 13 member countries of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), by examining urban growth dynamics with data from 2002 to 2022. Urban gr
content: This paper examines the influence of urban growth rates on per capita carbon emissions across 13 member countries of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), by examining urban growth dynamics with data from 2002 to 2022. Urban growth rate is captured through three separate indicators: urban growth, the urban-to-rural population growth ratio, and the urban-to-total population growth ratio. Data analysis was conducted employing the Panel Estimated Generalised Least Squares (EGLS) method, specifically the cross-sectionally seemingly unrelated regression (SUR) method. The results from the empirical analysis showed that all three urban growth rate proxies exert negligible influence on carbon emissions per capita, suggesting that urban expansion within the SADC region has not substantially contributed to increased carbon emissions over the years examined. Therefore, given the continuing rise in urban populations across Southern Africa and the accompanying escalation in carbon footprints, institutional and managerial policies promoting environmentally sustainable production to lower carbon emissions per head may not need to account for specific urban growth dynamics such as those examined in this study. However, accounting for specific urbanisation characteristics should be based on preference and what might be fundamental and material to an organisation or institution, provided cost does not outweigh the benefit.

title: Millet, Ritual, and Identity: The Socio-Cultural Significance of Indigenous Food Among the Kutia Kandha of Odisha, India
summary: The declining share of millets in India’s food systems from 22.2 per cent of total food grain production in 1950–1951 to around 6 per cent in recent years not only altered agrarian economies but also disrupted the ritual and cosmological wo
content: The declining share of millets in India’s food systems from 22.2 per cent of total food grain production in 1950–1951 to around 6 per cent in recent years not only altered agrarian economies but also disrupted the ritual and cosmological worlds of indigenous (tribal) communities. This article investigates the socio-cultural significance of millet among the Kutia Kandha, a particularly vulnerable tribal group of Kandhamal and Kalahandi districts, Odisha. It poses the questions how does millet function as a ritual medium through which social relations, gendered identities, and ecological ethics are produced and reproduced? How are these practices changing under the pressures of market integration, outmigration, and state-led millet revival? Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork and ritual economy framework, it shows that millet operates simultaneously as a subsistence grain, a ritual offering to Dharni Penu (the Earth Goddess), and a gendered knowledge system in which women are primary custodians of seeds, songs, and sacred practice. The article demonstrates that while generational shifts and market forces are eroding millet-based practices, state interventions such as the Odisha Millet Mission (OMM) have had uneven reach among subsistence-level households. The study’s originality lies in its insider ethnographic positioning conducted in Kui by a researcher from Kandhamal and in its contribution to debates on indigenous food sovereignty, ritual economy, and decolonial approaches to sustainable development, including the UN Sustainable Development Goal on Zero Hunger (SDG 2).

title: Targeted mitigation strategies for critically polluted PM2.5 regions in India using spatially constrained airsheds
summary: Air pollution in India is a regional problem, yet the current air quality management policy is largely city-centric. Here, we developed an airshed management framework that emphasizes cooperative action for PM2.5 pollution mitigation. This
content: Air pollution in India is a regional problem, yet the current air quality management policy is largely city-centric. Here, we developed an airshed management framework that emphasizes cooperative action for PM2.5 pollution mitigation. This framework identifies air pollution control areas (APCAs) for targeted emissions control across four critically polluted regions in the Indo-Gangetic Plain by mapping sectoral emissions from administrative units to pollution levels to meet specified air quality targets. We find that the dominant emission sectors differ across APCAs, such as agriculture, transport, and domestic to micro, small and medium-scale industry, highlighting the inadequacy of broad regional airshed management and the need for tailored air quality management plans. This framework yields differentiated policy guidance at the airshed and sub-airshed scales for the districts that constitute an APCA, leading to a spatially fine-tuned and implicitly minimal-effort mitigation plan. The developed framework is generalizable worldwide to polluted regions at any PM2.5 level.

title: A GENDERED COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF NET FARM INCOME AND ITS DETERMINANTS AMONG BAMBARA GROUNDNUT FARMERS IN NORTHEAST NIGERIA
source: FUDMA Journal of Agriculture and Agricultural Technology
summary: This study examined gender-based differences in net farm income and its determinants among Bambara groundnut farmers in Northeast Nigeria. A multi-stage sampling technique was employed to select 360 male and 360 female smallholder Bambara g
content: This study examined gender-based differences in net farm income and its determinants among Bambara groundnut farmers in Northeast Nigeria. A multi-stage sampling technique was employed to select 360 male and 360 female smallholder Bambara groundnut farmers from three selected states in the region. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, farm budgeting model, independent z-test, and log-linear multiple regression model were employed for the analysis. The results revealed that the mean net farm income of male and female Bambara groundnut farmers was ₦838,145.57 and ₦1,040,863.77, respectively, indicating a significant difference between the groups. For male farmers, age (δ₁ = -0.542, p < 0.05), level of education (δ₃ = 0.609, p < 0.01), off-farm income (δ₄ = 1.011, p < 0.01), farm size (δ₆ = 1.281, p < 0.01), extension visits (δ₁₃ = 0.561, p < 0.01), farming experience (δ₁₄ = 0.733, p < 0.05), factor productivity and efficiency indices significantly influenced net farm income. While for female farmers, age (δ₁ = -0.710, p < 0.01), marital status (δ₂ = 0.247, p < 0.01), household size (δ5 = 0.138, p < 0.10), farm size (δ₆ = 1.589, p < 0.01), interest amount (δ₇ = 0.289, p < 0.01), farming experience (δ₁₄ = 1.129, p < 0.01), amount of credit obtained (δ₁₅ = 1.341, p < 0.01), factor productivity and efficiency indices were significant. The study concludes that gender differences exist in both income levels and determinants, necessitating gender-responsive policies to improve access to resources, credit and extension services.

title: Translating Higher Education into Vietnamese: An Applied Linguistics Approach to Language Equity and Higher Education Access
source: Journal of Southeast Asian American Education and Advancement
summary: One growing population of non-native English speakers in the U.S. education system are native Vietnamese speakers, yet no studies have examined how higher education communication could be made more accessible for Vietnamese speakers. As a r
content: One growing population of non-native English speakers in the U.S. education system are native Vietnamese speakers, yet no studies have examined how higher education communication could be made more accessible for Vietnamese speakers. As a result, this case study reports on human and machine translational linguistics work conducted in partnership with the University of Iowa focused on simplifying and translating English enrollment management information into Vietnamese. Findings suggest that the institution increased the clarity and accessibility of enrollment management information by using second-person pronouns, shorter sentence structures, clearer diction, and explanations of institution-specific jargon. Moreover, analyses of machine and human translations of English to Vietnamese suggest that human translation should be preferred over machines, as Google Translate and Chat GPT provided adequate but not perfect translations of Iowa’s information. Implications for practice and college access are addressed.

title: Fertilidad del suelo y crecimiento de Pinus patula Schiede ex Schltdl. & Cham., en dos plantaciones forestales comerciales
summary: La productividad de las plantaciones forestales comerciales depende en gran medida de la fertilidad del suelo y la densidad arbórea. El objetivo de esta investigación fue comparar las características edáficas y su influencia en el desarroll
content: La productividad de las plantaciones forestales comerciales depende en gran medida de la fertilidad del suelo y la densidad arbórea. El objetivo de esta investigación fue comparar las características edáficas y su influencia en el desarrollo del arbolado, además de generar modelos altura-diámetro específicos en dos plantaciones de 18 años de Pinus patula. De cada ejemplar se midieron el diámetro normal y la altura, y se calcularon el área basal, la biomasa y el carbono arbóreo. Para caracterizar la fertilidad del suelo se determinaron las propiedades químicas en el perfil 0-30 cm. Finalmente, se ajustaron 14 modelos altura-diámetro. Los árboles de la Plantación A fueron superiores en altura y los de la Plantación B en diámetro, área basal y carbono por árbol, aunque a nivel de superficie, el almacén de carbono aéreo fue similar (75.6 Mg ha-1 en A y 73.7 Mg ha-1 en B). El suelo de la Plantación B registró altos niveles de MOS, N, Ca, Mg y CIC, lo que se reflejó en un mayor almacén de COS. Los modelos altura-diámetro resultaron con coeficientes de determinación bajos (R2=0.25-0.34); el modelo MT1 presentó el mejor ajuste global y residuales con distribución normal. En conclusión, la fertilidad del suelo y densidad de plantación determinaron la productividad y almacenamiento de carbono. Sin embargo, en la modelación altura-diámetro aún es necesario incorporar variables adicionales para mejorar su capacidad predictiva a escala local.

title: A Review of Liquid Cooling for Electric Vehicle Thermal Management
source: Academic Journal of Science and Technology
summary: As global automotive industries undergo a massive transition toward New Energy Vehicles (NEVs), maintaining the suitable temperature for the increasing compact and high- power electric motors has become a significant challenge. This review
content: As global automotive industries undergo a massive transition toward New Energy Vehicles (NEVs), maintaining the suitable temperature for the increasing compact and high- power electric motors has become a significant challenge. This review of literature systematically reviews the history, current state, and future path of development of liquid cooling technologies for electric vehicle (EV) thermal management. By comparing traditional air cooling with advanced liquid cooling — including the innovative application of hybrid nanofluids, direct liquid cooling, and micro pump integration— this review highlights the thermal performance and efficiency contributed by liquid systems. In electric motors, increased winding temperature raises copper losses (I²R), reducing motor efficiency. This applies directly to the motors used in electric vehicles, which further emphasizes the need for advanced cooling methods. This essay also addresses the challenges associated with liquid cooling, specifically regarding the complexity of structure, the expensive costs, and the long- term stability of advanced coolants. By synthesizing recent international and domestic research, this review presents a framework for optimizing thermal management efficiency and proposes directions for future research.

title: Behavioural-Spatial Diagnosis for the Revitalisation of Tanjung Raja Market
summary: Traditional market revitalisation is often judged by visible physical change: a new roof, a tidier façade, or more permanent stalls. Yet spatial improvement depends on how those changes interact with everyday trading routines. This study de
content: Traditional market revitalisation is often judged by visible physical change: a new roof, a tidier façade, or more permanent stalls. Yet spatial improvement depends on how those changes interact with everyday trading routines. This study develops a structured qualitative approach for tracing relationships among use routines, spatial conditions, and trader needs at Tanjung Raja Market, Ogan Ilir Regency, Indonesia. The exploratory case study analyses a 2023 field archive comprising a physical inventory, route-based observations, photographs, and 12 trader-interview summaries representing 12 commodity groups. Analysis combines meaning-unit construction, 1/0/missing coding, evidence-source tagging, case matrices, co-occurrence analysis, and checks against alternative explanations. The inventory records 97 shophouses, 506 kiosks, and 300 open stalls and street-vendor pitches; documented daily use ranges from 5 to 12 hours. Stall suitability does not emerge as a fixed property of one spatial type. Instead, it depends on the relationship among permanence, circulation exposure, environmental openness, and commodity-specific operational needs. Nine cases remain unclassified because spatial evidence is insufficient, while three support only partial diagnoses. The procedure therefore creates an audit trail from field evidence to inference boundaries, preliminary design hypotheses, and validation needs. Broader claims about flexibility remain provisional and require technical measurement and participatory design.

title: Adaptive Cycles in Open Innovation: A Longitudinal Study of Circular Economy Collaborations in a Fashion Incumbent
summary: ABSTRACT This single case study examines how the H&M Group, a large fashion multinational, uses open innovation (OI) to support the transition towards a circular business model. Although collaborations are recognized as key to advancing cir
content: ABSTRACT This single case study examines how the H&M Group, a large fashion multinational, uses open innovation (OI) to support the transition towards a circular business model. Although collaborations are recognized as key to advancing circularity, limited empirical evidence exists on how co‐creative OI processes drive circular practices across the value chain. Using adaptive cycle theory (the panarchy model) and institutional theory, the study analyses H&M Group's involvement in circular and collaborative innovation from 2010 to 2025 through a mixed‐methods approach, including case study analysis, content analysis, financial data and market trends. The findings show that H&M Group's participation in circular OI initiatives targets seven main categories of collaborations in a nonlinear process shaped by recursive interactions between institutional factors and financial and competitive pressures. The research demonstrates the existence of a full adaptive cycle of circular OI participation, offering insights for researchers, industry actors and policymakers.

title: Long‐Term Impact of Cropping System and Nitrogen Input Quality on Nitrogen Release and Organic Matter Chemistry
summary: ABSTRACT Long‐term integrated soil management strategies are essential for enhancing soil organic matter (SOM) quality and promoting the availability of mineralizable nitrogen (N). This study employed a tripartite analytical framework to in
content: ABSTRACT Long‐term integrated soil management strategies are essential for enhancing soil organic matter (SOM) quality and promoting the availability of mineralizable nitrogen (N). This study employed a tripartite analytical framework to investigate how crop rotations and organic N amendments influence soil N availability and SOM chemistry. A twelve‐week incubation assay quantified potentially mineralizable nitrogen (Min N) across five cropping systems: continuous corn (CC), continuous soybean (Soy), continuous clover (Cl), corn‐soybean (CS), and corn‐clover (CCl), under four N fertility regimes: no N input (N0), synthetic N as Urea (NF), uncomposted manure (UCM), and composted manure (CM). To evaluate the chemical stability of soil N, pyrolysis was used to calculate NH 3 ‐T50 (the temperature at which 50% of ammonia is released), serving as an indicator of thermal N stability. In parallel, X‐ray Absorption Near Edge Structure (XANES) spectroscopy characterized the chemical speciation of carbon and N in SOM. The Min N assay revealed significantly enhanced N availability in legume‐inclusive systems, particularly Cl and CCl treatment amended with CM or UCM. The NH 3 ‐T50 exhibited a significant negative correlation with Min N, indicating that more labile, biologically accessible N forms are associated with lower thermal stability. The XANES spectroscopy suggested that CC systems were characterized by amide and pyrrole N structures: markers of proteinaceous residues and limited microbial decomposition. In contrast, CCl treatments were enriched with pyridinic, aromatic, and aliphatic compounds, indicative of advanced microbial processing and stabilization pathways. Notably, UCM and CM treatments clustered closely in multivariate space, suggesting comparable SOM transformation trajectories despite compost maturity differences. Divergence in SOM chemistry under NF and N0 treatments reflected shifts toward labile or recalcitrant N pools, modulated by rotation context and input type. These findings highlight that integrating legumes and organic N amendments fosters a more microbially accessible soil N pool while supporting the development of chemically complex and stable SOM. The combined use of Min N assays, thermal analysis, and molecular spectroscopy provides a robust framework for understanding the interactions between crop rotation, N management, and SOM quality in sustainable agroecosystems.

title: Workload, stress, and nurse job satisfaction: Testing coping self-efficacy as a buffer
summary: This study examined the associations between clinical workload and job satisfaction among nursing professionals, focusing on the mediating role of work stress and the moderating role of occupational coping self-efficacy (OCSE). A quantitati
content: This study examined the associations between clinical workload and job satisfaction among nursing professionals, focusing on the mediating role of work stress and the moderating role of occupational coping self-efficacy (OCSE). A quantitative study was conducted among nurses at an Indonesian national referral hospital, with data analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling. The findings showed that clinical workload was not directly associated with job satisfaction but was positively associated with work stress. In turn, work stress was negatively associated with job satisfaction and fully mediated the relationship between clinical workload and job satisfaction. Occupational coping self-efficacy did not significantly moderate the association between workload and work stress. These findings suggest that sustained clinical demands may place substantial pressure on nurses’ psychological resources. Accordingly, organizational interventions addressing workload and systemic working conditions may be more effective in supporting nurses’ professional well-being than interventions focused solely on individual coping or resilience.

title: China’s Territorial Nationalism: A Case Study on China’s Irredentist Claim on Ladakh
summary: China, as known today, is bequeathed to the Republic of China (ROC) and later to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) from Qing China at the time of its abdication. To reclaim lost territories due to foreign aggressions in the colonial peri
content: China, as known today, is bequeathed to the Republic of China (ROC) and later to the People’s Republic of China (PRC) from Qing China at the time of its abdication. To reclaim lost territories due to foreign aggressions in the colonial period, successive Chinese governments have pursued both diplomatic negotiations, as seen with Myanmar and Nepal, and more assertive measures with India and Southeast Asian countries. This study employs a qualitative research methodology with the help of archival methods within the constructivist theory and explicates China preference formation, specifically focused on Ladakh and Aksai Chin.

title: Pragmatic data-driven AI-based approach for exploring the effects of important constructs on flight cancellations in disruptions and infectious diseases
source: European journal of tourism, hospitality and recreation
summary: Abstract This study presents a pragmatic real-world approach for exploring flight cancellations in disrupted situations and infectious diseases. The airline industry has been prone to disruptions, and a huge number of flight cancellations h
content: Abstract This study presents a pragmatic real-world approach for exploring flight cancellations in disrupted situations and infectious diseases. The airline industry has been prone to disruptions, and a huge number of flight cancellations have been reported in recent years. In this study, an AI-based, data-driven approach is used to explore flight cancellation patterns in the wake of disruption. The correct flight information is important to save time, money and resources for airline customers. Data pertaining to the event of flight cancellation in disruption has not been properly presented in previous studies. Thus, in this study, the prediction power of artificial intelligence tools has been exploited for flight cancellations. Artificial intelligence tools, namely two-class neural network regression, two-class decision forest, a two-class locally deep support vector machine, and two-class logistic regression, were utilized for prediction. The precision, accuracy and recall performances of all the methods used are 100%. The confusion matrix depicts that all four methods correctly predict the outcome of flight cancellation. For the total of 549169 tested flights, 549168 flights have been correctly predicted. The only false positive instance shows that there is only one case where the flight was not canceled, but the methods incorrectly predicted it as canceled. Thus, for almost all the cases, the predictions are correct. The correlation calculated from the huge data of 2745847 flights reveals that flight cancellations have a frail positive relation with departure and arrival delays. Moreover, there is a fragile negative relationship with airtime, weather delay, carrier delay, security delay, NAS delay, and late aircraft delay. The lessons learned from planning and coping with disruptions can be used as preemptive preparation guidelines for handling emergency situations in the future.

title: Glocalising pedagogy in a bicultural and multilingual school ecology: professional legitimacy and identity negotiation among transnational novice Chinese language teachers in Aotearoa New Zealand
source: Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development
summary: As language teachers increasingly move across countries, they need to negotiate the relationship between global professional knowledge and local educational and cultural demands. Yet little is known about how transnational novice language t
content: As language teachers increasingly move across countries, they need to negotiate the relationship between global professional knowledge and local educational and cultural demands. Yet little is known about how transnational novice language teachers experience glocalisation over time, particularly when gaining professional recognition requires them to engage with unfamiliar local cultural expectations and ways of knowing. This study examined how transnational novice Chinese language teachers experienced and negotiated glocalisation within a bicultural and multilingual school ecology in Aotearoa New Zealand, and how this process shaped their professional legitimacy and teacher identity. It drew on longitudinal data, including reflective journals and interviews over 8 months, and analysed them through an abductive qualitative longitudinal approach. Findings show that glocalisation developed through a gradual process of local becoming. Participants first entered the local school world through everyday and Māori cultural practices, gradually recognising the limits of their prior knowledge and adapting Chinese teaching to locally meaningful practices and learner contexts. Over time, these experiences strengthened local professional recognition and reshaped how participants understood themselves as teachers. In addition, the professional capital gained through glocalisation may not travel easily across contexts but may depend on how it is reinterpreted and revalued in future settings.

title: Ethnographies of Human‐AI Collaborations: What Arrangements of Expertise Emerge?
summary: ABSTRACT In this review, I outline four arrangements on the spectrum of human experts‐AI collaboration, as studied from an ethnographic, grounded perspective by sociology, management, and STS scholars. Starting with the sociology of experti
content: ABSTRACT In this review, I outline four arrangements on the spectrum of human experts‐AI collaboration, as studied from an ethnographic, grounded perspective by sociology, management, and STS scholars. Starting with the sociology of expertise's definitions of what constitutes “expert work,” I first review cases in which AI almost replaced human expertise, those in which AI aims for ‘no human in the loop,’ offering reasons why such complete automation has not succeeded. Second, I review cases where AI is a bit ‘too much’ and becomes exploitive and bossy, where most sociological research is focused, that is, algorithmic management, platform and gig economies, surveillance capitalism, and digital labor. Third, I review cases where AI offers new opportunities for expertise to develop new markets, roles, and co‐productions, and while incurring some professional risks for myself, I title these cases as ‘yay.’ And last, I review cases where ethnographic, grounded studies have shown that experts simply ignore or dismiss AI, with a simple ‘ nah .’ While differentiating these four points on the continuum of human‐AI collaboration, I discuss how the study of AI is entangled with the study of expertise in the 21st century, highlight questions and agendas, and offer directions for future research.

title: Big Brother or Good Steward? Earnings Management and the Disclosure of Personal Data Protection Systems
summary: Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2024, we examine whether voluntary disclosure of personal data protection systems (PDPS) is associated with earnings management. We document a moral licensing effect; that is, firms with h
content: Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2024, we examine whether voluntary disclosure of personal data protection systems (PDPS) is associated with earnings management. We document a moral licensing effect; that is, firms with higher PDPS disclosure engage in more real earnings management (REM). Specifically, a one‐standard‐deviation increase in PDPS disclosure is associated with a 21.5% increase in REM relative to its absolute mean, while accrual‐based earnings management (AEM) remains statistically unaffected. Decomposing REM reveals that abnormal production costs account for the overall increase, whereas discretionary expenses and abnormal operating cash flows exhibit offsetting patterns. Mechanism analyses suggest that the moral licensing conferred by PDPS disclosure facilitates opportunistic operational decisions through heightened operational risk under compliance pressure and weakened external monitoring reflected in lower audit quality. Cross‐sectional tests further indicate that this licensing effect is attenuated in firms embedded in stronger Confucian cultures, without political connections, and with more stable executive leadership. Overall, this study extends research on the determinants of earnings management from the perspective of data governance. We also enrich understanding of the economic consequences of voluntary PDPS disclosure. Our findings caution that disclosure of data protection practices may generate unintended governance consequences by enabling value‐destroying operational manipulation. The lesson is clear: in a world shaped by data and moral perception, voluntary disclosure is not always the cure; it can just as easily become the cover.

title: A meta-ethnography of staff experiences of raising concerns about quality and safety in residential aged care
summary: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Speaking up about quality and safety issues can protect older people and support learning in health and social care systems. In aged care, staff work in diverse roles to deliver care to residents with complex care
content: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Speaking up about quality and safety issues can protect older people and support learning in health and social care systems. In aged care, staff work in diverse roles to deliver care to residents with complex care needs. This meta-ethnography aimed to synthesise evidence on staff experiences of raising concerns about quality and safety in long-term residential aged care. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We included qualitative studies examining staff experiences of speaking up, incident reporting, and whistleblowing. Five databases were searched. The seven phases of meta-ethnography were used to translate first and second order constructs into third order constructs and a line-of-argument synthesis. RESULTS: Thirteen articles of 11 studies were synthesised to reveal four third order constructs: 1. Sensemaking a concern, 2. Organisational cultures determine how they are voiced, heard and respond to, 3. Systemic resources shape and constrain possibilities for voicing, and 4. Normalisation of poor care and loss of moral agency in organisations that respond with indifference. Raising concerns was a dynamic, recursive process encompassing phases of recognising, voicing, and organisational responding. Where quality and safety issues were normalised, individualised, or met with limited action, staff described moral distress, disengagement, and, in some cases, exit from the organisation or sector. DISCUSSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Raising concerns in residential aged care is a dynamic process shaped by interrelated individual, organisational and systemic factors. Speaking up interventions need to go beyond skills training to address phases of recognising care quality issues and how organisations respond when they are raised.

title: Oxidizer temperature effect on the modes of ignition of wood biomass particles
source: Bulletin of the Tomsk Polytechnic University Geo Assets Engineering
summary: In 2022–2024, it was officially established that unconventional renewable energy sources (wind turbines and solar panels) in the foreseeable future (15–20 years) will not be able to replace traditional energy (thermal and nuclear power plan
content: In 2022–2024, it was officially established that unconventional renewable energy sources (wind turbines and solar panels) in the foreseeable future (15–20 years) will not be able to replace traditional energy (thermal and nuclear power plants) due to the lack of powerful, reliable and safe electric energy storage systems. Therefore, coal-fired power plants in the coming decades will certainly generate large amounts of electricity not only in China, India, the USA and Poland, but also in many other countries. In this regard, the world-class scientific problem is environmental pollution by coal combustion products (flue gases from coal-fired power plants). This problem can be solved by burning coal in the furnaces of steam and hot water boilers mixed with biomass (wood in the first place). But wood burning in the furnaces of boiler installations so far in most real technologies leads to intensive slagging of heating surfaces. Therefore, an urgent task, the solution of which can ensure the transition to environmentally friendly and resource-saving coal-fired power in the future, is the task of substantiating the parameters of ignition and combustion of wood biomass particles. Aim. To determine the combustion modes of wood biomass particles of different sizes during high-temperature heating. Object. Wood particles (pine) of cubic shape of three characteristic sizes. Method. To determine the ignition and combustion modes of cubic wood particles under high-temperature heating conditions, a special experimental setup with laser illumination was used. Results. A conventional temperature boundary of Tcr=908 K was established for the transition between two ignition modes (gas-phase and heterogeneous) for pine wood biomass particles. It was also shown that the characteristic particle size of the wood (in the studied size range, L=4–8 mm) has no significant effect on the characteristics and conditions of the transition from one ignition mode to another. It was also experimentally established that, at relatively low oxidizer temperatures, the difference in ignition delay times for different ignition modes with a characteristic particle size of L=8 mm can reach 10%. For citation: Baranova (Kostoreva) A.A., Syrodoy S.V., Solodovnikova (Kostoreva) Zh.A., Omarov A.A., Nekrasov S.S., Senchikhin D.K. Oxidizer temperature effect on the modes of ignition of wood biomass particles. Bulletin of the Tomsk Polytechnic University. Geo Assets Engineering, 2026, vol. 337, no. 8, pp. 32–44. http://doi.org/10.18799/24131830/2026/8/5436

title: The Continuity and Rupture of the ‘New Washington Consensus’: From Biden to Trump 2.0
summary: ABSTRACT The ‘New Washington Consensus’ (NWC) represents a major intellectual shift in the US approach to global economic governance. However, the NWC has never been subject to systematic academic critique. With Trump's return to the White
content: ABSTRACT The ‘New Washington Consensus’ (NWC) represents a major intellectual shift in the US approach to global economic governance. However, the NWC has never been subject to systematic academic critique. With Trump's return to the White House ushering in a new era of US trade policy, the NWC is widely considered to be politically irrelevant in the existing literature. This article provides one of the first sustained critical assessments of the NWC and its legacy for the future of the international economic order. In particular, it argues that, contrary to prevailing assumptions, it is too early to dismiss the NWC as intellectually defunct. Although some elements of the NWC have been criticised and subsequently discarded in the Trump 2.0 era, the NWC nonetheless established the intellectual framework for Trump 2.0's trade statecraft. Therefore, a more rigorous engagement with the NWC and its evolving legacy provides a useful lens for imagining the future of the international economic order.

title: School well-being and student engagement among university students: The mediating role of growth mindset
summary: Student engagement is a key determinant of academic achievement in higher education. This study examined whether growth mindset mediates the relationship between school well-being and student engagement among university students. A cross-se
content: Student engagement is a key determinant of academic achievement in higher education. This study examined whether growth mindset mediates the relationship between school well-being and student engagement among university students. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with university students in Purwokerto, Indonesia, using standardized measures of school well-being, growth mindset, and student engagement. Mediation analysis was performed using Jamovi with bootstrapped confidence intervals. The findings showed that school well-being was positively associated with growth mindset, which in turn was positively associated with student engagement. Growth mindset significantly mediated the relationship between school well-being and student engagement, while the direct relationship between school well-being and student engagement was not significant. These findings suggest that growth mindset serves as an important psychological mechanism linking school well-being with student engagement. Supportive learning environments that foster both well-being and adaptive cognitive beliefs may therefore promote greater student engagement in higher education.

title: Örgütlerde Sürdürülebilir Davranışa Giden Psikolojik Yollar: Psikolojik Sahiplenme ve Yeşil Tutku
summary: Sürdürülebilir davranış, çevrenin korunması ve doğal kaynakların dengeli kullanımı açısından stratejik öneme sahiptir; ancak bu davranışların hangi psikolojik mekanizmalarla kalıcı olduğu konusunda literatür, psikolojik sahiplenme ve yeşil
content: Sürdürülebilir davranış, çevrenin korunması ve doğal kaynakların dengeli kullanımı açısından stratejik öneme sahiptir; ancak bu davranışların hangi psikolojik mekanizmalarla kalıcı olduğu konusunda literatür, psikolojik sahiplenme ve yeşil tutkuyu çoğunlukla birbirinden ayrı ayrı ele almıştır. Bu kavramsal çalışma, öz-belirleme kuramı (ÖBK) çerçevesinde özerklik, yeterlik ve ilişkililik ihtiyaçlarının doyumunun, sürdürülebilir davranışın iki kritik bileşeni olan psikolojik sahiplenme ve yeşil tutkuyu nasıl besleyebileceğini bütünleşik bir modelle açıklamaktadır. Psikolojik sahiplenme, çevresel hedefleri sahiplenme ve sorumluluk almayı; yeşil tutku çevresel değerlere yönelik duygusal enerji ve gönüllü katılımı artırarak sürdürülebilir davranışın motivasyonel temelini pekiştirmektedir. Çalışmanın özgün katkısı, bu iki yapıyı birlikte ele alarak sürdürülebilir davranışın psikolojik dinamiklerle güçlendiğini gösteren açıklayıcı bir çerçeve sunmasıdır. Bu çerçeve, farklı sektör ve kültürlerde ampirik sınamalar, aracı veya düzenleyici değişkenlerin test edilmesi ve boylamsal tasarımlarla süreç dinamiklerinin incelenmesi için somut bir araştırma gündemi önermektedir. Model, uygulayıcılar açısından ise sürdürülebilir davranışların geliştirilmesinde yalnızca farkındalık ve teşviklere değil, çalışanların katılımını, otonomisini ve anlamlı katkı fırsatlarını artırarak sahiplenme ve yeşil tutkuyu birlikte besleyen insan kaynakları ve liderlik uygulamalarına odaklanılması gerektiğine işaret etmektedir.

title: Academic burnout among female adolescents: A resource-based model of social support, perfectionism, and academic self-efficacy
summary: Academic burnout is an increasingly recognized psychosocial challenge among adolescents exposed to sustained academic demands. Guided by Conservation of Resources theory, this study develops and tests a resource-based model examining how so
content: Academic burnout is an increasingly recognized psychosocial challenge among adolescents exposed to sustained academic demands. Guided by Conservation of Resources theory, this study develops and tests a resource-based model examining how social support and perfectionism are associated with academic burnout through academic self-efficacy among female upper secondary students. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 522 students aged 15–18 years in metropolitan Thailand and analyzed using structural equation modeling. Academic self-efficacy was negatively associated with burnout, whereas both adaptive and socially prescribed perfectionism were positively related to burnout. Adaptive perfectionism was positively associated with self-efficacy, while socially prescribed perfectionism showed no direct association. Family support was indirectly associated with lower burnout through self-efficacy, whereas teacher emotional support demonstrated a direct negative association with burnout. Mediation analyses indicated that academic self-efficacy partially explained the relationships between adaptive perfectionism, family support, and burnout. Overall, the findings extend Conservation of Resources theory by highlighting how interactions between internal psychological resources and external social resources shape burnout processes among female adolescents in high-pressure educational contexts. The study contributes to interdisciplinary social science research by providing gender-sensitive insights into adolescent well-being and informing resource-focused prevention strategies.

title: Strategic human resource management, leadership, and governance practices in a university hospital: a qualitative study of healthcare managers’ experiences
summary: Strategic human resource management, leadership, and governance are recognized as complementary management processes that play a fundamental role in enhancing organizational effectiveness and improving the quality of healthcare services. Ho
content: Strategic human resource management, leadership, and governance are recognized as complementary management processes that play a fundamental role in enhancing organizational effectiveness and improving the quality of healthcare services. However, translating these processes into practice is often challenged by competing organizational priorities, structural constraints, and limited resources. This qualitative study, drawing on the experiences of physicians, nurses, and administrative managers working in a public university hospital, aims to examine how strategic human resource management and leadership practices are carried out, how these practices reflect in employee engagement and performance, the main challenges encountered during implementation, and how misalignments between policy and everyday practice are managed. Additionally, managerial strategies developed to support motivation and sustainable performance are interpreted through a qualitative lens. Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with purposively sampled managers, and the data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis approach. The study's reporting aligned with COREQ guidelines developed for qualitative interview research. The analysis identified six interrelated themes: (i) competency-based planning, training and development, and quality-oriented strategic HRM practices; (ii) relational leadership, role modeling, and trust building; (iii) fairness, transparency, and accountability in governance processes, along with policy-practice misalignments; (iv) staff shortages, increasing workload, and the risk of burnout; (v) managerial strategies supporting motivation and employee engagement; and (vi) local adaptation and innovative solution practices developed under structural constraints. The findings indicate that balancing institutional performance targets with workforce capacity cannot be achieved solely through technical planning tools; rather, the sustainability of this balance depends critically on fair and transparent governance mechanisms that are perceived as legitimate by frontline staff. The study contributes qualitative evidence to ongoing discussions on the integrated consideration of strategic HRM, leadership, and governance processes and aims to offer analytical insights to inform policy development and institutional improvement efforts in healthcare organizations.

title: Infidelity, Emotional Abuse, and Domestic Violence as Predictors of Marital Dissolution Among Married Couples in Delta North Senatorial District, Delta State, Nigeria.
source: RADINKA JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
summary: This study investigated adultery, emotional abuse, and domestic violence as key predictors of divorce, driven by the rising prevalence of marital instability and the need to comprehend the combined impact of relational stressors within the
content: This study investigated adultery, emotional abuse, and domestic violence as key predictors of divorce, driven by the rising prevalence of marital instability and the need to comprehend the combined impact of relational stressors within the Nigerian sociocultural context. Utilizing a quantitative descriptive survey design, the population comprised married men and women in the study area, with a sample size of 392 respondents determined using the Taro Yamane formula via a multi-stage sampling technique. Data were gathered using a validated instrument entitled the Infidelity, Emotional Abuse, Domestic Violence, and Marital Dissolution Questionnaire (IEDVMDQ), which demonstrated high internal consistency with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient greater than 0.70. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics for descriptive statistics (mean and standard deviation) and inferential statistics at a significance level of 0.05. The results revealed that all variables exceeded the criterion mean of, indicating that infidelity (aggregate mean = ), emotional abuse (aggregate mean = ), and domestic violence (aggregate mean = ) significantly impact marital breakdown. Domestic violence emerged as the strongest predictor, followed by emotional abuse and adultery, while the combined effect of these factors substantially predicted marital dissolution among married couples. These findings underscore the multifaceted nature of marital instability and the critical need for coordinated therapeutic strategies. The study concludes that adultery, emotional abuse, and domestic violence are deeply intertwined factors driving marriage breakup in the Delta North Senatorial District, thereby recommending the implementation of targeted counseling programs, public awareness campaigns, and robust policy measures.

title: The Effect of Schema Therapy on Aggressive Behaviour among Senior Secondary School Students in Oyo State, Nigeria
source: International Journal of Counseling and Psychotherapy
summary: Background: Pervasive aggressive behavior in secondary schools severely undermines school safety, yet conventional school guidance rarely addresses the underlying early maladaptive schemas. Objective: This study aims to investigate the effe
content: Background: Pervasive aggressive behavior in secondary schools severely undermines school safety, yet conventional school guidance rarely addresses the underlying early maladaptive schemas. Objective: This study aims to investigate the effect of Schema Therapy on aggressive behavior among senior secondary school students in Oyo State, Nigeria. Methods: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design was employed, involving 116 Senior Secondary School II students with high aggression scores recruited via multistage sampling. The experimental group received a ten-week structured Schema Therapy protocol, while the control group received conventional counseling. Data were collected using the Aggressive Behaviour Questionnaire (α = 0.89) and analyzed using Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) at the .05 level. Results: Schema Therapy produced a statistically significant main effect in reducing student aggression compared to conventional counseling. Gender also had a significant main effect, with female students recording higher post-test aggression scores than males. No significant treatment-by-gender interaction occurred, demonstrating consistent therapeutic gains across participants. Conclusion: Schema Therapy is empirically superior to conventional guidance in reducing adolescent aggression regardless of gender. Originality/Value: This study brings scientific novelty to the field of counseling and psychotherapy by uncovering the efficacy of Schema Therapy in restructuring early maladaptive schemas within a non-Western educational context that has remained underexplored. These findings enrich empirical evidence while providing a strategic reference for school counselors and policymakers in developing sustainable interventions.

title: The effect of proactive personality on professional commitment through career mindfulness in tour guidance students
summary: This study examines the mediating role of career mindfulness (CM) in the relationship between proactive personality (PP) and professional commitment (PC) among Turkish undergraduate students aiming for a career in tour guiding. Despite the
content: This study examines the mediating role of career mindfulness (CM) in the relationship between proactive personality (PP) and professional commitment (PC) among Turkish undergraduate students aiming for a career in tour guiding. Despite the importance of PP and mindfulness in career success, previous studies have not tested this relationship using the CM scale. Data collected from 592 students via online and face-to-face surveys between 1 November and 20 December 2023 were analyzed using structural equation modelling within the mediation framework. The findings revealed that PP did not have a direct significant effect on PC; however, PP positively predicted CM, and CM significantly increased PC. The results indicate that the effect of personality tendencies on professional attitudes can be mediated by career-focused self-regulation processes, such as CM, in the context of tour guiding. By integrating CM into the career development literature, the study contributes to personality–attitude relationships in a mechanism-based manner and generates implications for education and industry practice.

title: Scalable isolation of soil genomic DNA from microbial eukaryotes to multicellular micro‑ and mesofauna
summary: Global initiatives emphasise the need for harmonised soil biodiversity assessments. Efficient DNA extraction methods that accommodate larger soil volumes are essential for capturing organisms at higher trophic levels than bacteria and fungi
content: Global initiatives emphasise the need for harmonised soil biodiversity assessments. Efficient DNA extraction methods that accommodate larger soil volumes are essential for capturing organisms at higher trophic levels than bacteria and fungi and for supporting extensive sampling campaigns. We developed and evaluated a scalable, cost-efficient, and automation-ready soil DNA isolation protocol and compared its performance with two widely used commercial extraction methods: Qiagen DNeasy PowerSoil Pro (0.25 g soil input) and Qiagen DNeasy PowerMax Soil (2.5 g soil input). Four contrasting soil types representing agricultural and forest ecosystems (mull, sandy till, peat, and coarse mineral soil) were analysed. The new protocol combines bead-beating in sodium thiocyanate lysis buffer with either silica-membrane or carboxyl-coated magnetic bead purification and was tested using soil inputs of 2.5 g and 5 g for one soil type. DNA extracts were sequenced on an Illumina MiSeq platform using universal eukaryotic 18S rRNA gene primers to characterise soil metazoans and microbial eukaryotes. The developed protocol, combining a tenfold increase in soil input with commercial kit purification, produced the highest DNA yields in three of four soil types, increasing DNA recovery by up to 2.3-fold compared with the commercial maxiprep method. It also consistently detected the greatest metazoan richness, recovering up to 103% more taxa than the conventional miniprep method and up to 82% more taxa than the commercial maxiprep method. The carboxyl-coated magnetic bead workflow also performed well, recovering up to 83% more metazoan taxa than the miniprep method and up to 55% more taxa than the maxiprep method, particularly in forest soils. For microbial eukaryotes and protists, the commercial maxiprep and combination of developed high lysis volume and commercial kit silica purification protocols generally yielded the highest richness in agricultural soils, whereas the developed protocol performed best in coarse xeric forest soils. These results indicate that at least a tenfold increase in soil input relative to conventional 0.25 g extractions is required for reliable characterisation of mesofauna diversity, while further increases may provide additional gains. The developed DNA isolation protocol offers a solution for large-scale soil biodiversity assessments, supporting the integration of higher trophic levels into eDNA-based monitoring frameworks and future soil health monitoring programmes.

title: AI-based models for risks of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in office workers: exploring generalisability, interpretability and use of binary scales
summary: Artificial intelligence has the potential to enhance risk assessment of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in office environments. This study externally validated previously developed machine learning models and evaluated the performanc
content: Artificial intelligence has the potential to enhance risk assessment of work-related musculoskeletal disorders in office environments. This study externally validated previously developed machine learning models and evaluated the performance of simplified binary data inputs. Six models trained on data from 810 office workers were validated using an independent dataset of 74 globally recruited participants. Model performance across nine anatomical regions was assessed using F1-scores and AUC-ROC metrics. SHapley Additive exPlanations were used to interpret risk factor contributions, and model performance using ordinal Likert-scale inputs was compared with binary-transformed representations. Generalisability varied by anatomical region, with moderate performance for high-prevalence regions (neck and lower back) and reduced accuracy for low-prevalence regions. XGB showed moderate but comparatively stable performance across several anatomical regions. These findings highlight the need for region-specific validation and support the feasibility of simplified, interpretable, and scalable AI-based tools for practical ergonomic risk assessment in office environments.

title: GIS-based flood risk assessment in the Zhabay River Basin, Kazakhstan
