The results show that: (1) Implementing an industry-differentiated carbon tax in China will not be regressive, and the public need not be concerned about the resurgence of poverty; (2) Carbon tax exerts stronger adverse impacts on high-income groups than on low-income households, thereby facilitating income equity; (3) Although allocating carbon tax revenue to subsidize the clean power generation sector can further narrow income gap, it concurrently leads to a reduction in resource allocation efficiency. By combining targeted social protection policies such as energy assistance and benefit compensation, government can minimize the negative impacts of carbon tax on vulnerable groups.

title: Public disclosure record of the US Section 45Q carbon storage subsidy: subpart RR filings census and IRS aggregate series, and the credit visibility gradient
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: What the United States publishes about the physical performance behind its energy tax credits, and which instrument outside the tax system does the publishing. Two parts. The section 45Q record: reported sequestration by reporting year and
content: What the United States publishes about the physical performance behind its energy tax credits, and which instrument outside the tax system does the publishing. Two parts. The section 45Q record: reported sequestration by reporting year and well class, 2016 to 2023; a facility level census of every annual monitoring report filed under subpart RR and published in the EPA archive, nineteen facilities and sixty one facility years, the complete population rather than a sample; the national aggregate as published in the IRS inflation adjustment notices, 2013 to 2021, with the end of the series documented; and counts at each stage of the disclosure chain. The credit visibility gradient: seven credits on one table, holding the claiming authority and the tax confidentiality regime constant and varying the instrument outside the tax system that records the quantity. For each credit it records the claiming form and its confidentiality basis, the determining quantity, the independent record and the purpose it is produced for, what the public can see, whether identity, dollars and physical quantity are public, the instrument type and its legal authority, how easily that instrument could be removed, and the projected five year cost. A precedents table records regimes that publish claimant identity or subsidy amounts, at home and abroad. The tax return is never the public record. Where a performance quantity is visible at all, another institution is publishing it for its own reasons, and a record counts as independent only where the quantity would be generated by the same process if the credit did not exist. Compiled from primary United States government documents. Series verified 4 August 2026, refreshed 23 August; the gradient compiled and verified at the issuing sources 25 to 27 August 2026. No value is estimated; sources and access dates are recorded per item in the provenance sheets. Supports the author's studies of measurement, verification and disclosure in carbon storage.

title: Vehicle Cost Calculation for Commercial Vehicles for Agent-Based Simulations
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This record provides a documented vehicle-cost calculation for commercial vehicles in agent-based transport simulations. It compiles operator-perspective net cost assumptions for conventional and battery-electric vehicle types at the 2024 p
content: This record provides a documented vehicle-cost calculation for commercial vehicles in agent-based transport simulations. It compiles operator-perspective net cost assumptions for conventional and battery-electric vehicle types at the 2024 price level. The covered vehicle classes are: Passenger car Light-duty vehicle up to 2.8 t Light-duty vehicle from 2.8 to 3.5 t Heavy goods vehicle up to 7.5 t Heavy goods vehicle up to 18 t Waste-collection vehicle up to 25 t Heavy goods vehicle up to 40 t The calculation derives simulation-ready fixed daily costs, distance-dependent operating and energy costs, and time-dependent labor costs for use in vehicle-routing and MATSim-based transport models. It also documents assumptions for price-level harmonization, fuel and electricity prices, carbon-price components, vehicle tax, payloads, battery capacities, and energy consumption, and provides vehicle-specific calculation tables for transparent reuse and adaptation.

title: Regenerative Spirits: A Systems Thinking Analysis of Circular Economy Implementation in the Distilling Industry
summary: Abstract Transitioning toward a circular and regenerative economy requires more than technological innovation; it demands a shift in the underlying systems that shape how value, knowledge, and legitimacy are defined [Meadows D, Randers J, M
content: Abstract Transitioning toward a circular and regenerative economy requires more than technological innovation; it demands a shift in the underlying systems that shape how value, knowledge, and legitimacy are defined [Meadows D, Randers J, Meadows D, The limits to growth: the 30-year update , Routledge (2012); Raworth K, Doughnut economics: seven ways to think like a 21st-century economist , Chelsea Green Publishing (2017)]. While the circular economy (CE) is widely promoted as a pathway to sustainability, its implementation across industrial sectors remains uneven and frequently limited to efficiency-driven, technical interventions [Voulvoulis N et al., Glob. Environ. Change 75:102544 (2022)]. This paper examines the systemic conditions that constrain the adoption of circular economy principles through a case study of the craft distilling industry in regional Victoria, Australia. Guided by Sposito’s (2021) Rational–Holistic Model of Planning and Decision-Making, the study applies a multimethodological systems approach, integrating thematic analysis, boundary critique, and soft systems tools (PQR and CATWOE). This enables an exploration of how system structures - particularly those relating to motivation, control, knowledge, and legitimacy - shape what is considered feasible and acceptable in practice. The findings reveal that barriers to circular economy implementation are not solely technical or economic but are embedded within broader institutional and cultural frameworks. Regulatory fragmentation, compliance-driven definitions of legitimacy, and economically dominant worldviews constrain the uptake of more regenerative practices. By contrasting existing (“is mode”) and alternative (“ought mode”) system configurations, the study highlights the importance of reconfiguring underlying assumptions about system purpose and governance. The paper contributes methodologically by demonstrating how systems thinking combined with thematic analysis can reveal structural constraints, and conceptually by positioning CE as a pathway dependent on a broader shift toward a sustainability-oriented worldview.

title: Enhancing economic resilience through digital innovation: the role of financial inclusion and infrastructure in urban China
source: Technological and Economic Development of Economy
summary: The digital revolution has redefined financial inclusion, significantly enhancing the capacity of urban economies to withstand and recover from economic shocks. Using panel data from 285 Chinese cities between 2011 and 2020, this study exam
content: The digital revolution has redefined financial inclusion, significantly enhancing the capacity of urban economies to withstand and recover from economic shocks. Using panel data from 285 Chinese cities between 2011 and 2020, this study examines the role of digital innovation in promoting economic Resilience, drawing on econometric models and Martin and Sunley’s conceptual framework of Resilience. Our findings reveal that the Digital Innovation Framework (DIF) enhances economic Resilience by driving financial inclusion, technological adoption, and infrastructure development. However, regional disparities persist, with the eastern and central regions benefiting more than the western and southern regions, which have lower economic scales. The quality of corporate operations and the stability of financial markets further amplify the positive effects of digital finance on Resilience. Mediating factors, including the adoption of digital technologies and household expenditure levels, significantly strengthen the impact of DIF on urban Resilience. This study highlights the dual role of digital finance as both a catalyst for innovation and a tool for promoting equitable economic growth. The findings underscore the importance of region-specific policies in bridging development gaps, particularly in less developed areas. Policymakers are encouraged to promote inclusive digital strategies that foster fairer growth while leveraging the transformative potential of DIF.

title: Gross Profit Mark-up PT Goodyear Indonesia Tbk: Dinamika Penjualan, Segmentasi Pelanggan, Pembelian, dan Evaluasi Transfer Pricing
summary: This study examines the association of automotive sales dynamics, customer market segmentation, and purchases with the Gross Profit Mark-up (GPM) of PT Goodyear Indonesia Tbk as a basis for evaluating transfer pricing at the gross-profit le
content: This study examines the association of automotive sales dynamics, customer market segmentation, and purchases with the Gross Profit Mark-up (GPM) of PT Goodyear Indonesia Tbk as a basis for evaluating transfer pricing at the gross-profit level. Using a descriptive quantitative design, the study analyzes 28 quarterly observations from 2019-2025, comprising national vehicle sales, affiliate and third-party sales proportions, purchases of raw materials and finished goods, and quarterly GPM. Annual GPM is also compared with the interquartile range of six comparable Asian tire manufacturers obtained from TP Catalyst under the Cost Plus Method (CPM). The results show that national vehicle sales and customer segmentation do not display a consistent direct association with GPM. In contrast, purchases show a clear inverse descriptive pattern: the highest annual purchases in 2022 (USD 302.0 million) coincided with the lowest GPM (4.93%), while lower purchases in 2023-2024 accompanied GPM recovery. Benchmarking indicates that Goodyear Indonesia was within the arm's length range only in 2019, 2021, and 2025. These findings highlight cost efficiency and comparability factors as critical considerations in transfer pricing evaluation.

title: How does rural entrepreneurial dynamism promote common prosperity for farmers and rural areas in China?
summary: Enhancing farmers’ incomes and narrowing income disparities are essential prerequisites for achieving common prosperity. Drawing on panel data for 1564 Chinese counties from 2015 to 2023, this study incorporates farmers’ income, the urban–r
content: Enhancing farmers’ incomes and narrowing income disparities are essential prerequisites for achieving common prosperity. Drawing on panel data for 1564 Chinese counties from 2015 to 2023, this study incorporates farmers’ income, the urban–rural income gap, and intra-rural income inequality into a unified analytical framework. The article simultaneously studies the results of income growth and income distribution, and explores from both theoretical and empirical perspectives how rural entrepreneurship affects farmers’ well-being and promotes the common prosperity of rural China. The results yield three key findings. First, rural entrepreneurship significantly increases farmers’ incomes and reduces both the urban-rural income gap and income inequality among farmers. These effects remain robust after addressing potential endogeneity and performing a series of robustness checks. Second, rural entrepreneurship promotes income growth and advances common prosperity by facilitating adjustments in agricultural cropping structures, expanding employment opportunities for farmers, strengthening the rural collective economy, and enhancing local innovation capacity. Third, the income-enhancing effects of rural entrepreneurship are stronger in southern regions, in areas characterized by distinctive agricultural specialization, and in regions with higher levels of rural digitalization. However, these effects may be constrained by elite capture and the digital divide. Overall, the findings indicate that fostering high-quality rural entrepreneurship and supporting the endogenous growth of farmers’ incomes are critical for advancing common prosperity in rural areas.

title: Unlocking the Relationship Between Corporate Environmental Performance and Financial Outcomes Under National Environmental Policy Framework: Panel Evidence From China
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between corporate environmental performance (CEP) and corporate financial performance (CFP) under China's evolving environmental policy regime. Using a panel dataset of 1,312 Chinese A‐share lis
content: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between corporate environmental performance (CEP) and corporate financial performance (CFP) under China's evolving environmental policy regime. Using a panel dataset of 1,312 Chinese A‐share listed firms from 2010 to 2023, we find a significant negative association between CEP and CFP. The findings challenge the assumption that improved CEP necessarily enhances financial outcomes and suggest that, in emerging markets, environmental improvement may impose short‐term financial burdens on firms. National environmental policies change the CEP–CFP relationship in heterogeneous ways, with some policies intensifying the negative association and others attenuating it. The financial consequences of CEP are context‐dependent and affected by policy design, regulatory enforcement, and the maturity of market‐based incentive mechanisms. Drawing on the cost–benefit perspective, institutional theory, stakeholder theory, and the resource‐based view, this study advances extant literature by highlighting that the CEP–CFP relationship is policy‐driven, offering implications for managers and policymakers.

title: Chloroplast genome sequence and phylogenetic analysis of the hemiparasitic plant: Taxillus sutchuenensis var. duclouxii (Loranthaceae)
summary: Taxillus sutchuenensis var. duclouxii, a shrub-like hemiparasitic plant with medicinal value. This study sequenced, assembled, and annotated the chloroplast genome of T. sutchuenensis var. duclouxii using Illumina high-throughput sequencing
content: Taxillus sutchuenensis var. duclouxii, a shrub-like hemiparasitic plant with medicinal value. This study sequenced, assembled, and annotated the chloroplast genome of T. sutchuenensis var. duclouxii using Illumina high-throughput sequencing. The genome exhibits a typical circular quadripartite structure, with a total length of 122,537 bp and a GC content of 37.3%. It contains 104 genes, including 64 protein-coding genes, 32 tRNA genes, and 8 rRNA genes. Phylogenetic analysis shows that T. sutchuenensis var. duclouxii forms a clade with T. nigrans and T. sutchuenensis, indicating a close relationship. This study provides a basis for molecular identification and phylogenetic research in Taxillus.

title: Welfare Enhancement through Social Innovation: Balancing State Direction and Grassroots Action
summary: This article advances the understanding of social innovation (SI) by examining how public policy frameworks support the development of robust SI ecosystems in dynamic contexts. Using a hybrid framework that integrates ecosystem theory—highl
content: This article advances the understanding of social innovation (SI) by examining how public policy frameworks support the development of robust SI ecosystems in dynamic contexts. Using a hybrid framework that integrates ecosystem theory—highlighting multi-actor interdependencies—and Mazzucato’s entrepreneurial state theory—emphasizing the state’s market-shaping capacities—the study offers a new lens to assess public interventions. It asks: How can public institutions address key challenges to expand and implement SI within growing ecosystems? The research design employs a systematic qualitative approach, bridging a content analysis of key international reports and policy documents with original qualitative field data from the author’s doctoral research. This empirical foundation includes semi-structured interviews with 25 public officials across six ministries, conducted between July 17, 2015, and March 18, 2017, to explore institutional strategies and barriers within a growing ecosystem. The study identifies six core public sector roles: initiator, facilitator, resource provider, capacity builder, catalyser, and regulator. Findings show that public institutions operate not as passive enablers but as entrepreneurial actors that de-risk innovation, coordinate stakeholders, and embed SI principles in institutional structures. By combining collaborative ecosystem dynamics with entrepreneurial state functions, the article demonstrates how governments can strategically shape, scale, and sustain inclusive and transformative SI ecosystems while overcoming systemic barriers.

title: Diversified financing modes of BYD in the new energy vehicle industry
source: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies
summary: The expanding new energy vehicle industry requires manufacturers to finance R&D, capacity construction, supply chain integration and overseas operation simultaneously. This paper investigates BYD's diversified financing modes and evaluates
content: The expanding new energy vehicle industry requires manufacturers to finance R&D, capacity construction, supply chain integration and overseas operation simultaneously. This paper investigates BYD's diversified financing modes and evaluates their effects on enterprise growth, liquidity and risk control. It adopts the research method combining case study, literature review, financial statement analysis and structural comparison. It also analyzes internal financing, bank loans, bond financing, equity financing, trade credit and policy-based green finance, focusing on financial data from 2022 to 2025. The results demonstrate that operating cash flow and retained earnings remain the foundation of BYD's financing system, while external financing becomes more significant during the accelerated globalization stage. BYD's shift from self-financed development to a more balanced but more complex capital structure in 2025 is marked by delayed operating cash generation, significant private placement, and rapid loan growth. Diversification improves financing capacity and term flexibility, but also raises higher requirements for liquidity management, refinancing, exchange rate and governance.

title: Unveiling the nexus between products and influential countries in the multi-layer trade network of global lithium battery
summary: Amid the accelerating global transition to renewable energy and the surge in electric vehicle adoption, ensuring the stability of the lithium battery supply chain has become a critical priority. This study explores the complex relationships
content: Amid the accelerating global transition to renewable energy and the surge in electric vehicle adoption, ensuring the stability of the lithium battery supply chain has become a critical priority. This study explores the complex relationships between products and influential countries within the global lithium battery supply chain through a multi-layer trade network framework. By constructing a comprehensive network model that spans upstream minerals, midstream materials, and downstream batteries, we analyze the evolving dynamics of trade and influence from 2002 to 2022. The findings emphasize the growing centrality of lithium as a critical resource, with its influence steadily rising in both supply and demand dimensions. Furthermore, trade connections in the downstream battery layer are more robust, yet increasingly dependent on a few dominant players, particularly China, the European Union, and the United States. While China’s influence as a leading producer and exporter continues to expand, yet the declining diversity in its import structure poses risks of supply disruptions. Thus, there is urgent need for countries to diversify supply channels and closely monitor policy changes in major lithium-producing nations to ensure global supply chain stability. These findings provide important insights for understanding and optimizing the stability of the global lithium battery supply chain and provide fundamental knowledge for future research on risk transmission in the lithium battery supply chain.

title: Gridded population distribution data for the Yellow River Basin, 1000–2000 AD
summary: High-resolution historical gridded population data are essential for quantifying long-term anthropogenic impacts. However, existing datasets often lack regional accuracy or continuity due to the scarcity of historical records and methodolog
content: High-resolution historical gridded population data are essential for quantifying long-term anthropogenic impacts. However, existing datasets often lack regional accuracy or continuity due to the scarcity of historical records and methodological limitations in spatial disaggregation. Here, we present a spatiotemporal population dataset for the Yellow River Basin spanning 1000–2000 AD at a 10-km spatial resolution. The dataset was reconstructed by harmonizing demographic statistics from The Population History of China with digitized historical administrative boundaries. We employed a hierarchical interpolation framework and an elevation-based spatial allocation model constrained by historical population quotas. The resulting dataset provides grids at centennial intervals for the pre-modern era (1000–1800 AD) and 50-year intervals for 1800–2000 AD. Technical validation indicates finer regional spatial details compared with HYDE 3.1, particularly in reflecting historical administrative shifts and reducing the overestimation of urban agglomeration in pre-industrial reconstructions. Serving as a high-resolution regional supplement to global archives, this product enhances both regional consistency and temporal granularity. It provides data support for deciphering human-environment coupling mechanisms in the Yellow River Basin—a paradigmatic region for long-term anthropogenic activity.

title: Attitudes towards carbon taxation in the EU: messenger effects vs. content effects
summary: Abstract This paper investigates how European Union institutional sources influence public support for carbon taxes through messenger effects. Our framework predicts that support decreases with higher tax rates, an effect moderated by respo
content: Abstract This paper investigates how European Union institutional sources influence public support for carbon taxes through messenger effects. Our framework predicts that support decreases with higher tax rates, an effect moderated by respondents’ associations with the source, namely trust, euroscepticism, and national identity. We run a pre-registered survey-embedded vignette experiment in Germany and Poland ( N = 3192), in which respondents evaluate carbon tax policies for car, aviation, and heating fuels. Proposals vary in tax rate (10%, 50%, 100%) and supporting source (European Commission, national government, foreign government). We find that higher tax rates decrease support and that source-specific effects are driven by trust, but not by national identity or euroscepticism, which instead structure baseline support across all actors. Moreover, positive messenger cues do not moderate the negative effect of costs. These findings show that institutional attitudes matter for carbon tax support, but that policy costs remain central.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on governance barriers and public–private partnership pathways in green infrastructure implementation in South Africa
summary: Cities face mounting pressures from rapid urbanisation, climate change, and persistent service delivery deficits. Green urban infrastructure (GI), encompassing nature-based solutions, biodiversity-integrated networks, and hybrid ecological
content: Cities face mounting pressures from rapid urbanisation, climate change, and persistent service delivery deficits. Green urban infrastructure (GI), encompassing nature-based solutions, biodiversity-integrated networks, and hybrid ecological systems, has emerged as a response to these intersecting crises. Yet in the Global South, and South Africa specifically, its translation into practice remains uneven, constrained by institutional inertia, fragmented governance, and structural financing gaps. This study investigates how stakeholders across government, the private sector, academia, and civil society perceive and navigate GI development in South Africa across three dimensions: (1) the integration of sustainability into infrastructure planning and execution; (2) the key challenges and opportunities shaping GI implementation; and (3) the extent to which public–private partnerships (PPPs) support GI initiatives. Adopting a qualitative, interpretivist design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 purposively sampled professionals and analysed thematically. Findings indicate that while sustainability has gained rhetorical prominence, implementation remains uneven, with sustainability functioning more as a discursive imperative than an embedded planning logic. Four interrelated barriers dominate: grey-infrastructure professional culture, policy–implementation dissonance, procurement misfit, and fragmented governance. Opportunities centre on climate finance mobilisation, co-benefit framing, ESG-driven private investment, and institutional integration. The study provides practitioner-grounded evidence on GI–PPP delivery in South Africa and advances scholarship on green infrastructure governance, financing, and sustainability transitions.

title: ECONOMETRIC MODELING OF FISCAL INCENTIVE INSTRUMENTS FOR SUSTAINABLE TOURISM INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT
source: EPRA International Journal of Economics Business and Management Studies
summary: This study develops an empirical framework to evaluate the structural and causal impacts of targeted fiscal incentive instruments—specifically corporate tax credits, accelerated capital depreciation allowances, and interest rate subsidies—o
content: This study develops an empirical framework to evaluate the structural and causal impacts of targeted fiscal incentive instruments—specifically corporate tax credits, accelerated capital depreciation allowances, and interest rate subsidies—on the expansion and modernization of sustainable tourism infrastructure. Addressing potential endogeneity, unobserved cross-sectional heterogeneity, and dynamic persistence, the empirical inquiry employs a two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM) and Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (P-ARDL) estimation framework applied to a balanced panel dataset spanning 2010–2024. The econometric findings demonstrate a statistically robust, non-linear relationship between fiscal stimulus measures and private capital allocation toward green hospitality assets and low-carbon transport logistics. Specifically, targeted interest rate subsidies exhibit a potent short-run multiplier effect (β=0.342,p<0.01), whereas structural tax concessions yield significant long-run private investment elasticity (β=0.518,p<0.001) only after regional institutional quality and infrastructural absorption capacity surpass critical threshold levels. Furthermore, indiscriminate tax exemptions are found to induce deadweight economic loss and market distortion without generating commensurate green capital stock. These findings bridge a critical gap in public finance and regional tourism economics by establishing an optimal, performance-contingent incentive design that mitigates fiscal leakage while accelerating sustainable infrastructure transition in emerging and developing economies.

title: Mitogenome assembly and phylogenetic relationships of Phalaris arundinacea
summary: Introduction As a perennial herb of Poaceae, Phalaris arundinacea plays key roles in grazing, production, and soil and water conservation because of its well-developed rhizomes and seed dispersal. We assembled and annotated the first mitoge
content: Introduction As a perennial herb of Poaceae, Phalaris arundinacea plays key roles in grazing, production, and soil and water conservation because of its well-developed rhizomes and seed dispersal. We assembled and annotated the first mitogenome of P. arundinacea to support evolutionary and taxonomic research. Methods We assembled and annotated the first complete mitochondrial genome of P. arundinacea by integrating Illumina short reads with Nanopore long reads via a hybrid assembly strategy. The genome architecture was comprehensively characterized, encompassing codon usage bias, repetitive sequence organization, and inter-organellar genetic exchange with the chloroplast genome. Results and discussion Assembly of the P. arundinacea mitogenome revealed two circular structures with a combined length of 526,717 bp. The genome comprised a set of 37 protein-coding genes (PCGs), 27 tRNAs, and 8 rRNAs, with the rRNA genes exhibiting full assembly (100% coverage). The mitochondrial genome contained 154 forward and 164 palindromic repeats, along with 25 tandem repeats and 124 simple sequence repeats (SSRs). Notably, 102 SSRs were distributed on contig1, predominantly in tetrameric form. Furthermore, 376 RNA editing sites were predicted. A total of 104 fragments were integrated into the mitochondrial genome from the chloroplast, amounting to 55,866 bp of transferred sequence. Finally, phylogenetic analysis of 28 plant mitogenomes placed P. arundinacea closest to species within the genus Poa ( P. chaixii and P. pratensis ). Comparative analysis of non-synonymous-to-synonymous substitution rate (Ka/Ks) ratios across divergent species revealed that the mitochondrial genome of P. arundinacea underwent stabilizing evolutionary dynamics, characterized by predominant purifying selection with several lineage-specific variations in selective pressure. Our findings support the close phylogenetic relationship between P. arundinacea and species of the genus Poa and provide a reference mitochondrial genome resource for future comparative studies within Phalaris that incorporate broader taxon sampling. These results support deeper phylogenetic investigations of P. arundinacea and facilitate future work on its germplasm characterization and applied use.

title: Drivers of Green Roof Adoption in Ghanaian Residential Buildings: A Diffusion of Innovations Perspective
summary: Purpose: This paper examines the drivers of green roof adoption in Ghanaian residential buildings. Design/Methodology/Approach: A purposive sampling approach was adopted to select 215 homeowners, occupants, architects, engineers, contractor
content: Purpose: This paper examines the drivers of green roof adoption in Ghanaian residential buildings. Design/Methodology/Approach: A purposive sampling approach was adopted to select 215 homeowners, occupants, architects, engineers, contractors and developers. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire designed to capture the key variables relevant to green roof adoption. Data were analysed using frequencies, percentages, mean scores, standard deviations and ranking analysis. Research Limitation: The study is based on stakeholder perceptions in a single Ghanaian city and does not measure the physical performance of green roofs. Future research should combine survey evidence with pilot projects, lifecycle costing and inferential modelling. Findings: Energy savings and reduced utility costs were the strongest perceived benefit, followed by economic benefits, climate change mitigation, acoustic insulation, social and psychological benefits, biodiversity and general environmental benefits. Aesthetic value was the leading motivator for adoption, followed by environmental benefits, energy savings, and government incentives. Willingness to install, adopt in future projects and recommend adoption was moderate but promising. Practical Implication: Green roof promotion should combine visible aesthetic appeal, evidence of energy savings, environmental messaging, financial incentives, demonstration projects, and professional capacity-building. Social Implication: Incorporating green roof provisions into urban greening strategies, climate adaptation plans and sustainable building policies would help move green roofs from isolated voluntary initiatives to a more recognised component of sustainable residential development. Originality/value: It shows that these benefits operate through identifiable diffusion mechanisms relative advantage, compatibility, and observability that actively facilitate adoption.

title: A novel annual and daily planning for integrated carbon and electricity markets based on fuel tax
summary: A reliable and sustainable energy supply is increasingly essential as energy demand rises due to population growth, economic development, and improved living standards. However, fossil fuel-based electricity generation significantly contrib
content: A reliable and sustainable energy supply is increasingly essential as energy demand rises due to population growth, economic development, and improved living standards. However, fossil fuel-based electricity generation significantly contributes to CO₂ emissions, posing challenges to human well-being. This paper proposes a sequential annual-daily planning framework for an integrated carbon market (CM) and electricity market (EM) system incorporating a fuel tax . The system operates at three primary levels: annual planning, daily CM execution, and daily EM execution. At the annual planning stage, initial allocations and pricing of carbon allowances are determined, along with the calculation of each plant's allowance share and the setting of a fuel tax, which is embedded into plants' cost functions. During daily CM execution, an initial forecast of the next day’s electricity price is made. The profit maximization problem for plants is analyzed at different carbon price levels, and bidding curves are constructed to clear the CM. Following this, the EM is executed, where profit maximization at different electricity price levels is solved, and the energy bidding process determines the EM clearing point and price. Any plant allowance shortages or surpluses are balanced by transferring allowances to future periods. By coordinating the CM and EM through an innovative fuel tax mechanism, this integrated framework aims to provide efficient price signals and incentives for reducing carbon emissions in the power sector. This paper provides a detailed overview of the structure and operation of this combined market mechanism, highlighting its potential to provide coordinated operational incentives for emission reduction under the adopted market assumptions. Simulation results show that introducing a fuel tax increases the average carbon price from $11.8/ton to $17.9/ton, leading to a 115% rise in renewable generation and a 373.7% increase in renewable plant profits. Fossil-fuel plant profits also rise by 239% due to elevated electricity prices, while total system-wide profits increase by 271%. Furthermore, annual CO₂ emissions decrease significantly over time. The stylized case study indicates that strategic design and allocation of market parameters play a critical role in shaping market behavior, price dynamics, and profitability across different generation types.

title: Reflecting the Moderating Role of Perceived Value on the ‘Attitudes-Sustainable Behavior’ Gap in the Emerging Country Context
summary: This study explores the factors influencing consumer behavior in purchasing sustainable products in Vietnam, an emerging market, to address the ‘attitudes-sustainable behavior’ gap and enhance understanding of the sustainable development go
content: This study explores the factors influencing consumer behavior in purchasing sustainable products in Vietnam, an emerging market, to address the ‘attitudes-sustainable behavior’ gap and enhance understanding of the sustainable development goals (SDGs). A survey involving 518 respondents familiar with sustainable products was conducted. A structural equation modeling approach was employed to assess relationships among research constructs. The study reveals that perceived value, attitude, perceived behavior control, and education significantly influence consumer intentions and behavior towards sustainable products. Uniquely, it augments the revised theory of planned behavior model by introducing perceived value as a reflective and moderating factor, thereby bridging the ‘attitudes-behavior’ gap. Contrary to expectations in Vietnam’s cultural context, subjective norms did not significantly influence sustainable purchasing behavior. This study uniquely contributes to the existing literature on sustainable consumption and the sustainable development goals. The findings offer practical insights for government authorities and marketers to enhance consumer perceptions and develop strategies for sustainable products. Emphasizing reliable branding and reputation can significantly influence consumer investment decisions

title: Greenhouse gases, globalization, and energy use nexus: The heterogenous roles of tech-innovations in environmental sustainability of world’s top-3 emitters
summary: Climate change exerts significant threat to global environmental sustainability. As such, curtailing greenhouse gases (GHG) to limit global average temperature below 1.5 °C has become a major climate agenda in the 21 st century. In this stu
content: Climate change exerts significant threat to global environmental sustainability. As such, curtailing greenhouse gases (GHG) to limit global average temperature below 1.5 °C has become a major climate agenda in the 21 st century. In this study, we examine how tech-innovation, renewable energy, and globalization shape this sustainability goal via a tripartite investigation of three important pollutants (2 GHG: carbon dioxide-CO 2 & Methane-CH 4 , and 1 harmful air pollutant: nitrogen dioxide-NO 2 ) among the world’s top 3 emitting countries, namely China, the USA, and India. FMOLS and DOLS empirical techniques help to control for income differences among the countries while simulating the long-run coefficients of the impacts of tech-innovation, renewable energy, and globalization on these pollutants within a three-phase model using data between 1990 and 2022. Additionally, Dumitrescu-Hurlin's approach reveals the direction of causality relationship in the model. Following the results, we obtained evidence of the environmental gains from tech-innovations and renewable energy as the duo significantly curtail both CO 2 and CH 4 emissions. On the contrary, the emission-triggering impacts of globalization were observed, thus showcasing the negative environmental side of globalization. This evidence was further reinforced by the bidirectional causality between globalization and NO 2 . Hence, for the authorities of these top-3 pollutant-emitting countries, these findings are suggestive of the need for more actions to strategically bolster the integrated deployment of both tech-innovation and renewables to accelerate the progress toward SDG-13 of climate action.

title: Blockchain network complexity and illicit transaction detection: Machine-learning evidence from the Elliptic Bitcoin benchmark
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe blockchain financial system allows users to send money fast without any border restrictions. However, the same structure of the blockchain may be used as a means of laundering money. This pap
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe blockchain financial system allows users to send money fast without any border restrictions. However, the same structure of the blockchain may be used as a means of laundering money. This paper assesses the relationship between the complexity of transaction networks and the likelihood of their illicit nature within the public Elliptic Bitcoin benchmark and examines whether anomaly detection using machine learning helps to interpret risks from an AML/CFT perspective. This empirical analysis assumes that Elliptic provides an anonymized transaction network in which nodes correspond to Bitcoin transactions, edges reflect directed transactions, and anonymized features facilitate licit/illicit classification of transactions. Furthermore, the dataset is not considered evidence of sender wallet addresses, receiver wallet addresses, transaction amount, timestamp, ownership of exchanges, user geography, and national AML/CFT effectiveness. Based on the labelled analytical dataset presented in the uploaded workbook (46,564 observations, including 42,019 licit transactions and 4,545 illicit transactions), a logit model found a significant positive correlation between illicit transactions and degree centrality (beta = 1.870, p < 0.001), clustering coefficient (beta = 0.940, p < 0.001), and flow entropy (beta = 0.680, p < 0.001). Isolation Forest and Autoencoder reached AUCs of 0.866 and 0.841, respectively. In turn, the coefficient measuring a country’s regulatory capacity and its interaction term are not included in the estimation because there is no country-window marginal effect. Therefore, this paper does not test for the impact of regulatory capacity of the USA, Singapore, and UAE on transaction classification.

title: Gas Flaring and Its Impact on Output of Agricultural Sector in the Niger Delta (A Case Study of Ethiope West Local Government)
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
summary: The study examined the effect gas flaring on agricultural output in Delta State, Nigeria. The agricultural output consists of cassava, yam and pepper. Likewise, farmers’ income was included in the model as a control variable. The study reli
content: The study examined the effect gas flaring on agricultural output in Delta State, Nigeria. The agricultural output consists of cassava, yam and pepper. Likewise, farmers’ income was included in the model as a control variable. The study relied on primary data through collection of questionnaires using simple random sampling of 800 respondents. Two gas flare stations located in Sapele and Oghara were used for the study. The targeted respondents provided information of the yields of crops on 200, 400 and 600 kms away from the flow stations. The information was processed, classified and econometric technique was utilized to explore the relationship. Accordingly, the study found that gas flaring had significant negative effect on all three agricultural output. Therefore, it was recommended that government put in place necessary and effective polices to eliminate gas flaring or even reduce it to the barest minimum.

title: Interrupting the Glamour of Evil: Reading Metz Constructively in a Time of Politico–Ecological Emergency
summary: This article draws upon the theology of Johann Baptist Metz, placing it into discussion with insights from theological aesthetics and political ecology. It does so to examine how it is that evil comes to appear as glamorous, giving particul
content: This article draws upon the theology of Johann Baptist Metz, placing it into discussion with insights from theological aesthetics and political ecology. It does so to examine how it is that evil comes to appear as glamorous, giving particular attention to the evil shaping and sustaining the contemporary planetary emergency. The first part of the article considers the obfuscating and trivializing power of evil. The second part reflects upon the distortions of affection caused by the lust for domination. The article concludes with a reflection on the potentiality of hope to interrupt the mastery of sin.

title: Oil Revenue and Economic Growth in Nigeria: An Empirical Analysis
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
summary: Oil revenue is a significant component of Nigeria’s economy since the last five decades after displacing agriculture, accounting for a large portion of the government revenue and export earnings, thereby becoming both blessing and curse. Th
content: Oil revenue is a significant component of Nigeria’s economy since the last five decades after displacing agriculture, accounting for a large portion of the government revenue and export earnings, thereby becoming both blessing and curse. This study examined the impact of oil revenue on economic growth in Nigeria. It spanned through the period 1986 to 2024. The specific objectives are to evaluate the impact of crude oil export earnings, domestic crude oil sales, petroleum profit tax, oil royalties, on real gross domestic product in Nigeria. And also, ascertain whether the exchange rate moderates the impact of oil revenue on economic growth in Nigeria. The study employed an ex post facto research design and the secondary data used for the investigation were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) statistical bulletin, National Bureau of statistics, Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) Fact Book and the World Bank Development Website. Descriptive Statistics, Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF), ARDL bound test for Co-integration and Autoregressive Distributed lag model (ARDL) Statistical tools were used in the study. The results revealed that Crude oil export earnings have significant and positive impact on the real gross domestic product in Nigeria; Domestic crude oil sales have an insignificant but positive impact on real gross domestic product in Nigeria; Petroleum profit tax has a positive and insignificant impact on real gross domestic in Nigeria; Oil royalties have a significant and positive impact on real gross domestic product in Nigeria; The study concluded that oil revenue has a positive and significant impact on the economic growth of Nigeria. The study recommends that the government should utilize crude oil export earnings to invest in infrastructural projects that will help promote economic expansion and alleviate poverty in the country, engage in resuscitating the local refineries in Nigeria to encourage and increase domestic crude oil sales, strengthen the FIRS for effective petroleum profit tax administration, and more so, the government should allocate a higher percentage of oil royalties to host communities to promote local development, environmental remediation and conflict reduction.

title: The Effects of IFRS Implementation on Tax Evasion Minimization of Listed Multinational Companies in Nigeria: The Moderating Role of Inflation
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
summary: This study investigated how International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) implementation operationalized through disclosure comprehensiveness and timeliness of financial reporting relates to tax evasion minimization and earnings manage
content: This study investigated how International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) implementation operationalized through disclosure comprehensiveness and timeliness of financial reporting relates to tax evasion minimization and earnings management with the moderating variable of inflation among 10 Nigerian multinational firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group over the period 2015–2024. The study employed an ex-post facto design and random‐effects panel regression with panel-corrected standard errors, we model Effective Tax Rate (ETR) and Discretionary Accruals (DA) as functions of disclosure (DC), timeliness (TFR), inflation (I), and their moderation. Results revealed that greater disclosure comprehensiveness is significantly associated with lower ETR (β = –2.32, p < 0.05), while timeliness and inflation exhibit no independent or moderating effects on tax rates. In the earnings‐management model, both DC (β = +3.89, p < 0.001) and TFR (β = +0.21, p < 0.001) positively predict DA, with inflation further amplifying accrual manipulation (β = +1.78, p < 0.05). However, the DC×I moderation (β = –0.20, p < 0.01) indicates that high‐ inflation periods temper the disclosure–DA linkage. These findings suggested that, in the Nigerian context, detailed IFRS disclosures may facilitate complex yet lawful tax strategies and accrual management, particularly when macroeconomic volatility is low. We recommended enhanced regulatory scrutiny of IFRS disclosures and strengthened board/audit‐committee oversight during inflationary cycles to curb opportunistic reporting behaviors.

title: The Missing Distinction
summary: Abstract Many failures attributed to insufficient intelligence arise earlier. Before an evaluator can determine whether something is the same, has changed, follows from evidence, or warrants action, a judgment must already specify which dis
content: Abstract Many failures attributed to insufficient intelligence arise earlier. Before an evaluator can determine whether something is the same, has changed, follows from evidence, or warrants action, a judgment must already specify which distinctions count, which transformations are admissible, what evidence is retained, and who is authorized to supply or act on missing information. The Missing Distinction presents the Identity-Persistence Program as a unified conceptual architecture for bounded judgment. Its central diagnostic asks whether a demanded verdict varies within cases the evaluator’s licensed information treats as identical. If it does, no recombination of that same information—no larger model, additional inference, ensemble, or confidence score—can recover the erased distinction. The failure is structural rather than computational. If the verdict is incompletely specified, the problem lies further upstream in specification or governance. Across examples from institutional records, automated decisions, biology, software, archives, and scientific disagreement, the book separates specification, identity, admissibility, evidence, derivation, informational repair, realization, authorization, commitment, and verification. It shows how a required distinction may be realized exactly, supplied only with excess revelation, support only a narrowed demand, or remain unavailable. It also explains why identical verdicts can arise through paths that disclose different information, making provenance requirements relative to the audit question being asked. The book introduces no independent theorem ownership. It is a trade synthesis of the formal owner papers, translating their dependency order, exact boundaries, practical diagnostics, and refusals into a lens for institutions and future judgment systems.

title: Green Finance, Climate Policy Uncertainty, and Ecological Carrying Capacity Dynamics in G20 Economies: Evidence from Load Capacity Factor Panel Analysis
summary: Carbon-based indicators do not show whether ecosystems can generate sufficient biocapacity to fulfil human needs, and the G20 economies account for a large portion of the global ecological burden. This study analyses the load capacity facto
content: Carbon-based indicators do not show whether ecosystems can generate sufficient biocapacity to fulfil human needs, and the G20 economies account for a large portion of the global ecological burden. This study analyses the load capacity factor (LCF) of 19 G20 economies between 2000 and 2022, measured as biocapacity divided by the ecological footprint. It examines the long-run association between green bond issuance and ecological carrying capacity, as well as the moderating role of climate policy uncertainty (CPU) in this association. The analysis includes Pesaran cross-sectional dependence and slope heterogeneity tests, Cross-sectionally Augmented Im, Pesaran, and Shin (CIPS) and Cross-sectionally Augmented Dickey-Fuller (CADF) unit-root tests, Fourier-Shin cointegration, Cross-Sectionally Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (CS-ARDL) estimation, Augmented Mean Group (AMG), Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG) robustness checks, and Konya bootstrap Granger-causality tests, and conditional marginal-effect analysis for the GB_GDP × CPU interaction. The main CS-ARDL results show a positive long-run association for green bond issuance (β = 0.182, p < 0.01) and a negative association for the CPU (β = −0.011, p < 0.01). The interaction term is negative (β = −0.004, p < 0.05), indicating that the green bond-LCF association weakens as policy uncertainty increases. The conditional marginal effects become statistically indistinguishable from zero near the upper tail of the CPU distribution. The Konya results indicate heterogeneous country-level temporal patterns rather than uniform structural causality. Overall, green finance is associated with a stronger ecological carrying capacity when climate policy settings are stable and institutional conditions support long-term ecological investment.

title: Driverless, not thoughtless? Automated vehicle regulation, the dilemma of control, and the prospect of dual corrigibility
summary: When regulating emerging technologies, authorities must balance available knowledge, means for control, and desirable directions of development. The article asks which normative orientation guides Norway's automated vehicle regulation, how
content: When regulating emerging technologies, authorities must balance available knowledge, means for control, and desirable directions of development. The article asks which normative orientation guides Norway's automated vehicle regulation, how the regulation is configured, and whether this regulatory strategy aligns with the underpinning normative orientation. To answer these questions, the article analyses the policy-making process preceding Norway's Act Relating to Testing of Self-Driving Vehicles, the content of the finalised Act, and interview data from the first automated vehicle trial conducted after the Act's effectuation. The article shows that Norway pursues a two-stage regulatory strategy. During the first stage, interested parties may organise automated vehicle trials; during the second stage, the state will establish a permanent regulation for automated vehicles. This two-stage strategy builds upon the untenable assumption that practical concerns regarding a technology's functioning can be addressed separately from normative concerns. Drawing upon David Collingridge's writings on the dilemma of control, the article argues that practical and normative concerns must be processed in parallel and suggests dual corrigibility – corrigibility of decisions and corrigibility of orientation – as a guiding principle for regulating emerging technologies.

title: Secondary risk in mineral resource management: a preliminary theoretical conception
summary: Mineral resource security, influenced by uneven global distribution and escalating geopolitical tensions, has emerged as a central issue in resource governance. Traditional research on mineral resource risk management has tended to overlook
content: Mineral resource security, influenced by uneven global distribution and escalating geopolitical tensions, has emerged as a central issue in resource governance. Traditional research on mineral resource risk management has tended to overlook the secondary risks that may arise from response measures, potentially resulting in an incomplete understanding of risk systems. This study attempts to integrate secondary risk theory into mineral resource management. It defines the scientific connotation of secondary risks in this context, constructs a full-industry-chain theoretical model, clarifies the “risk trigger-response-derivative iteration” logic, and identifies four potential risk evolutionary forms: persistence, migration, transformation, and restructuring. Using tin resources as a case, the study finds that response actions induce risk persistence, migration, and transformation, with affected entities shifting from upstream to downstream. This research pioneers defining secondary risk in mineral resources management, develops a full-industry-chain theoretical model, reveals its evolutionary forms, provides a new dynamic risk management paradigm, and offers implications for resource security and sustainable industrial development.

title: Governance and decision-making processes in local government: Opportunities for evidence inputs and stakeholder involvement in local authorities
summary: Background The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) has increased investment in research and evaluation of and by local authorities. This article aims to close gaps between research, policy and practice in local authoritie
content: Background The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) has increased investment in research and evaluation of and by local authorities. This article aims to close gaps between research, policy and practice in local authorities by analysing core governance and decision-making processes, ways in which different types of evidence could feed into those processes and potential measurement approaches. It also lays a foundation for future comparative analyses of decision-making and evidence use. Methods Within-case comparative analyses of three core, recurrent governance and decision-making processes: key decisions, Scrutiny Committee reviews and Regulatory Committee decisions (licensing and planning). Examples are drawn from a member-led, local authority with a Leader and Cabinet model of governance, where all members are elected every four years. Results Each process has specific requirements and varies somewhat in the types of evidence considered, although all three often draw on local evidence of need, publicly available guidance and resident feedback. All three processes involve elected councillors and council officers. Local authorities may also have procedure rules which allow members of the public to ask questions and make comments at meetings. Scrutiny Committee reviews tend to follow an annual cycle, whereas key decisions and Regulatory Committee decisions are ongoing but must adhere to specified timelines. Conclusions Evidence reviews, information on needs, alternative interventions and projected financial, legal, equalities and climate implications are particularly relevant and more feasible than large scale primary data collection, given timelines. Although reports and meetings where decisions are made are open to the public, what evidence is cited and discussed at these fora likely underestimates what may have informed a decision. Future comparative analyses would help to understand the extent of variation within and across processes and types of government institutions.

title: End-of-day price manipulation and enterprise total factor productivity: Evidence from China
summary: : Against the backdrop of the continuously expanding trading volume in the stock market, the stable operation of the capital market is a key support for the high-quality development of enterprises. This study examines the impact of End-of-d
content: : Against the backdrop of the continuously expanding trading volume in the stock market, the stable operation of the capital market is a key support for the high-quality development of enterprises. This study examines the impact of End-of-day price manipulation on the total factor productivity of enterprises and explores the path of the effect. Drawing on market manipulation theory and modern enterprise theory, it analyzes from the perspective of trader behavior how to suppress the improvement of enterprise total factor productivity. The End-of-day price manipulation behavior affects the high-quality development of enterprises by reshaping the internal resource allocation mode of enterprises, and empirical research on Chinese listed companies supports the above conclusion. In addition, the End-of-day price manipulation has a dynamic impact on the total factor productivity of enterprises by interfering with the resource allocation decisions of enterprises. Other heterogeneity analyses show that this inhibitory effect is more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, enterprises with a higher proportion of executive shareholding, and non-labor-intensive industries.

title: Maintaining to obstruct: Associated milieu and the ecology of fossil continuity
source: Environment and Planning E Nature and Space
summary: This article argues that the maintenance of the social environment that sustains fossil infrastructures and the obstruction of their phase-out are co-constitutive processes: the maintenance of what sustains the plant is the concrete mechani
content: This article argues that the maintenance of the social environment that sustains fossil infrastructures and the obstruction of their phase-out are co-constitutive processes: the maintenance of what sustains the plant is the concrete mechanism through which obstruction operates in the territory. Drawing on five years of research on the Torrevaldaliga Nord thermoelectric plant in Civitavecchia (Italy) and on a private archive assembled over decades by the activist Simona Ricotti, the article reconstructs a long-duration trajectory — the formation of the fossil territory (1952–2001), the coal conversion dispute (2001–2003), and the production of continuity after authorization (2003–2013) — to show how conventions, observatories, compensations, and promises function simultaneously as devices of maintenance and of obstruction. The article advances three contributions. First, it reframes climate obstruction as an ecological rather than primarily agential formation: deliberate strategies are effective because they operate in a milieu already receptive to them. Second, it extends Simondon's concept of milieu associé from the techno-geographic to the socio-political register, and connects this extension to Rippa’s (2024) “environing infrastructure” framework, showing that fossil plants do not occupy territories but actively environ them. Third, it identifies the unfulfilled promise as a temporal device of obstruction: the observatory promised in 1992, invoked in 2002, diagnosed as comatose in 2008, and reactivated in 2015 does not fail but performs — maintaining acceptability by deferring operativity

title: Systems thinking to reduce energy waste
summary: Extended abstract 2-003-26 Energy efficiency is the avoidance of ‘energy waste’. Historical thinking about reducing energy waste has been focussed on individual products, processes and practices at the point of final energy use. However, en
content: Extended abstract 2-003-26 Energy efficiency is the avoidance of ‘energy waste’. Historical thinking about reducing energy waste has been focussed on individual products, processes and practices at the point of final energy use. However, energy is wasted at all stages of the chain to supply energy services, from resource acquisition through to final use. The energy waste at different stages is inter-dependent, and therefore a whole system analysis is required. This insight is critical when thinking about fundamental change in energy systems, in particular in the transition to zero-carbon system. Electrification is critical to the elimination of direct use of fossil fuels. The main changes in the energy system after large-scale electrification with renewables include big reductions in energy waste in power generation, transportation and fossil fuel processing. Waste reductions in buildings are smaller, but there is a major increase in the use of ambient energy (via heat pumps), which can be thought of as the opposite of waste, allowing efficiencies to rise (perhaps counterintuitively) to above 100%. Maximising electrification of end use therefore has efficiency effects across the energy chain. We show that it can halve global primary energy demand to provide the existing level of energy services. Electrification is therefore critical to future efficiency goals, as it will be the main ‘provider’ of energy efficiency improvement over the next two decades. This requires changes to both the way energy supply analysts typically think about electrification – as a supply side change – but also to its conceptualisation by energy demand analysts as something additional to energy efficiency. Research and policy have not yet adequately adapted to the changed reality. It has some important implications. For example, taxes on electricity tend to deter electrification and therefore energy efficiency, improving the energy efficiency of fossil fuel use is at best a short term option, perhaps even in some cases counterproductive, minimum energy performance standards should switch focus from lights and appliances to the new large electricity loads – heating, vehicles and industrial processes. Read full abstract. Download presentation.

title: Trade law, policy and commercial diplomacy
summary: Trade law governs the legal conditions of cross-border exchange, but rules acquire practical meaning only through institutions, evidence, negotiation and power. This chapter integrates WTO law, regional agreements, quantitative policy analy
content: Trade law governs the legal conditions of cross-border exchange, but rules acquire practical meaning only through institutions, evidence, negotiation and power. This chapter integrates WTO law, regional agreements, quantitative policy analysis, commercial diplomacy and geoeconomic statecraft within one decision architecture. It develops MFN, national treatment, tariff bindings, services, intellectual property, SPS and TBT disciplines, customs valuation, origin, trade remedies, dispute settlement and AfCFTA implementation, then connects them to tariff and NTM indicators, gravity-model reasoning, international-relations theory, negotiation, sanctions, export controls, industrial policy and strategic dependencies. South Africa's citrus disputes with the European Union anchor the African legal problem; AfCFTA illustrates treaty implementation and continental bargaining; semiconductor export controls provide a comparative global geoeconomic case. The chapter distinguishes legal compliance from economic wisdom and moral legitimacy. Christian moral reasoning evaluates truth, sovereignty, subsidiarity, coercion, peace, conscience, justice and the protection of vulnerable persons while preserving the legitimacy of rules, prudent statecraft and responsible commerce. Keywords: international trade law; WTO; AfCFTA; trade remedies; dispute settlement; commercial diplomacy; trade negotiation; geoeconomics; sanctions; economic statecraft

title: A structured dataset of polymers in molecular dynamics simulations extracted by LLM-assisted text mining
summary: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are widely used to study polymer behavior, yet the resulting simulation data remain scattered across the literature and are rarely available in standardized, machine-readable formats. To address this gap,
content: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are widely used to study polymer behavior, yet the resulting simulation data remain scattered across the literature and are rarely available in standardized, machine-readable formats. To address this gap, we present a curated dataset of polymer MD simulations reported in peer-reviewed publications from 1995-2025 using largelanguage-model (LLM)-assisted extraction followed by expert curation. Starting from an initial set of 48,206 abstracts retrieved through keyword-based bibliographic searches, automated screening narrowed the corpus to 755 polymer-MD-relevant publications. Among these, 198 papers reported simulation-derived values for one or more of the six target properties: density, glass transition temperature, radius of gyration, Young's modulus, diffusion coefficient, and viscosity, resulting in 1,095 unique records. Each record captures the polymer system, force field, and available physical properties. By aggregating dispersed literature into a centralized, standardized database, this work supports data-driven analysis, enhances reproducibility in molecular modeling of polymeric systems, and facilitates the development of automated and machine-learning-assisted simulation workflows.

title: Data Envelopment Analysis in Business and Economics: Methods, Trends, and Research Frontiers
summary: ABSTRACT Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) has become an important multidimensional research method and is now widely used in business and economics. This study adopts a scoping‐review approach and uses Natural Language Processing (NLP), a da
content: ABSTRACT Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) has become an important multidimensional research method and is now widely used in business and economics. This study adopts a scoping‐review approach and uses Natural Language Processing (NLP), a data‐driven machine‐learning technique, to analyze 12,686 relevant studies and classify the literature into major research themes and categories. Specifically, we identify three DEA‐related themes, CoreDEA (11,167 studies), StatDEA (1266 studies), and DecisionDEA (253 studies), which can be further divided into 15 categories, including Dynamic DEA, Undesirable DEA, Bootstrap DEA, and ANP/AHP DEA. The findings show that traditional DEA methods, especially those within CoreDEA, continue to develop actively. At the same time, the growing prominence of sustainability‐related research suggests that SBM DEA and hybrid models incorporating bootstrap, meta‐frontier, and network DEA may represent an important direction for future research.

title: Do universal owners behave like universal owners? The emergence of a financial sector norm
summary: Abstract The past few years have seen a surge in scholarship on universal ownership, systematic stewardship, and system‐level investing. These concepts describe the reality that large diversified owners of capital own a more or less represe
content: Abstract The past few years have seen a surge in scholarship on universal ownership, systematic stewardship, and system‐level investing. These concepts describe the reality that large diversified owners of capital own a more or less representative slice of the market and therefore must concern themselves with systemic risks to the financial system as a whole. To date these treatments have not assessed whether practice follows theory, however. This Article answers the question: Do universal owners behave like universal owners? In this Article, I present the first empirical evidence as to whether investors that adopt a systemic mindset subsequently alter their policies and practices. This Article examines how norms in the financial system arise, take hold, and become self‐fulfilling, and evaluates universal ownership theory as an emerging norm in the financial system by testing it against two existing norm formation frameworks. It assesses the extent to which the largest global asset owner organizations publicly self‐identify as universal owners and analyzes these funds' use of two material devices that align with impact‐oriented approaches to investment and stewardship activities. This analysis finds stark differences between self‐identified universal owners and peer funds without such a self‐designation, suggesting that a universal ownership mindset may translate into the widespread use of high‐impact investor tools that non‐universal owners mainly neglect. The Article also introduces the concept of norm accelerants: mainstream actors and institutions that can play a significant role in shepherding an emerging norm to broad acceptability. The Appendix comprises two proposed experiments to test whether universal ownership theory could become self‐fulfilling, including an Advance Notice of Future Litigation (ANFL) that would allow litigation for future harms to be priced into the market in the present.

title: ผลกระทบของภาษคารบอนตอมลคากจการ: กรณศกษากลมอตสาหกรรมระดบโลก

content: การศึกษาครั้งนี้มีวัตถุประสงค์เพื่อศึกษาความสัมพันธ์ระหว่างภาระภาษีคาร์บอน (Carbon Tax) และระดับความเข้มข้นของการปล่อยคาร์บอน (Carbon Intensity) ที่มีต่อมูลค่ากิจการ โดยมุ่งเน้นที่กลุ่มบริษัทจดทะเบียนระดับโลกที่อยู่ในกลุ่มอุตสาหกรรม (Industrials Sector) ซึ่งเป็นองค์ประกอบของกองทุน iShares MSCI World Industrials Sector Advanced UCITS ETF การศึกษานี้ใช้ข้อมูลแบบแผง (Panel Data) ครอบคลุมระยะเวลา 5 ปี ตั้งแต่ปี พ.ศ. 2564 ถึง 2568 โดยคัดเลือกกลุ่มตัวอย่างได้จำนวน 36 บริษัท รวมเป็นจำนวนข้อมูลสังเกตการณ์ทั้งสิ้น 180 ค่าสังเกตการณ์ การวิเคราะห์ข้อมูลใช้แบบจำลองการถดถอยพหุคูณ (Multiple Regression Analysis) ด้วยวิธีกำลังสองน้อยที่สุดแบบรวมกลุ่ม (Pooled OLS) พร้อมทั้งมีการใช้ตัวแปรควบคุม ได้แก่ ขนาดของกิจการ อัตราส่วนหนี้สินต่อทุน อัตราผลตอบแทนต่อสินทรัพย์ และอัตราการเติบโตของกิจการผลการศึกษาพบว่า ภาระภาษีคาร์บอนไม่มีความสัมพันธ์ต่อมูลค่าของกิจการอย่างมีนัยสำคัญทางสถิติ ซึ่งสามารถอธิบายได้ว่า ค่าใช้จ่ายด้านสิ่งแวดล้อมของบริษัทในกลุ่มตัวอย่างอาจยังอยู่ในระดับที่ไม่สูงพอที่จะส่งผลกระทบต่อกระแสเงินสดอย่างมีนัยสำคัญ ทำให้นักลงทุนยังไม่ได้นำปัจจัยนี้มาพิจารณาปรับลดการประเมินมูลค่าของกิจการ ในทางกลับกัน ระดับความเข้มข้นของการปล่อยคาร์บอนมีความสัมพันธ์เชิงลบกับมูลค่าของกิจการอย่างมีนัยสำคัญทางสถิติ ผลลัพธ์นี้สะท้อนให้เห็นอย่างชัดเจนว่า บริษัทที่มีสัดส่วนการปล่อยก๊าซคาร์บอนในระดับสูง มีแนวโน้มที่จะต้องเผชิญกับความเสี่ยงด้านกฎระเบียบและภาระต้นทุนที่เพิ่มขึ้น ส่งผลให้ความเชื่อมั่นของนักลงทุนลดลงและกดดันมูลค่าตลาดของบริษัท นอกจากนี้ ยังพบว่าขนาดของกิจการ อัตราส่วนหนี้สินต่อทุน และอัตราผลตอบแทนต่อสินทรัพย์ ล้วนมีความสัมพันธ์อย่างมีนัยสำคัญทางสถิติต่อมูลค่ากิจการเช่นเดียวกัน
